children.translated_text: Thus have I heard.

children.text: ekasmin samaye bhagavāṃllaṅkāpure samudramalayaśikhare viharati sma nānāratnagotrapuṣpapratimaṇḍite mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena sārdhaṃ mahatā ca bodhisattvagaṇena nānābuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitair bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ anekasamādhivaśitābalābhijñāvikrīḍitair mahāmatibodhisattvapūrvaṃgamaiḥ sarvabuddhapāṇyabhiṣekābhiṣiktaiḥ svacittadṛśyagocaraparijñānārthakuśalair nānāsattvacittacaritrarūpanayavinayadhāribhiḥ pañcadharmasvabhāvavijñānanairātmyādvayagatiṃgataiḥ
children.translated_text: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, on the peak of Mount <s>Malaya</s> by the sea, adorned with many kinds of jewels, lineages, and flowers, together with a great community of monks and with a great assembly of bodhisattvas, bodhisattva great beings gathered from many buddha-fields. They sported in the mastery, powers, higher knowledges, and activities of many samādhis; the bodhisattva <s>Mahāmati</s> was foremost among them. They had been consecrated by the hands of all Buddhas; they were skilled in understanding the object-field seen as one's own mind; they bore the methods and disciplines suited to the forms of conduct of the minds of various beings; and they had gone to the course of non-duality concerning the five dharmas, own-being, consciousness, and the twofold selflessness.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān sāgaranāgarājabhavanāt saptāhenottīrṇo'bhūt
children.translated_text: Now at that time the Blessed One had emerged, after seven days, from the palace of <s>Sāgara</s>, king of the nāgas.

children.text: anekaśakrabrahmanāgakanyākoṭibhiḥ pratyudgamyamāno laṅkāmalayamavalokya smitamakarot pūrvakairapi tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairasmiṃllaṅkāpurīmalayaśikhare svapratyātmāryajñānatarkadṛṣṭitīrthyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāryaviṣaye tadbhāvito dharmo deśitaḥ
children.translated_text: Being received by many millions of <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and nāga maidens, he looked toward <s>Laṅkā</s> and Mount <s>Malaya</s> and smiled: "Here too, on the <s>Malaya</s> peak in this city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, former Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, taught the dharma cultivated by them in the sphere of noble knowledge personally realized by oneself, beyond reasoning, views, outsiders, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.

children.text: yannvahamapi atraiva rāvaṇaṃ yakṣādhipatimadhikṛtya etadevodbhāvayan dharmaṃ deśayeyam
children.translated_text: Why should I not also, right here, teach that very dharma, bringing it forth with reference to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the yakṣas?"

children.text: aśrauṣīdrāvaṇo rākṣasādhipatistathāgatādhiṣṭhānāt bhagavān kila sāgaranāgarājabhavanāduttīrya anekaśakrabrahmanāgakanyākoṭibhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ samudrataraṃgānavalokya ālayavijñānodadhipravṛttivijñānapavanaviṣaye preritāstebhyaḥ saṃnipatitebhyaścittānyavalokya tasminneva sthitaḥ udānamudānayati sma yannvahaṃ gatvā bhagavantamadhyeṣya laṅkāṃ praveśayeyam
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, heard through the Tathāgata's empowerment: "The Blessed One, it is said, has emerged from the palace of <s>Sāgara</s>, king of the nāgas, surrounded and honored by many millions of <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and nāga maidens. Looking at the waves of the ocean, at the domain where the winds of the active consciousnesses stir upon the ocean of storehouse-consciousness, and looking at the minds of those who had assembled there, he remains right there and utters an inspired utterance. Why should I not go, request the Blessed One, and bring him into <s>Laṅkā</s>?"

children.text: tanme syāddīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca
children.translated_text: "That would be for my welfare, benefit, and happiness for a long night, and for that of gods and humans."

children.text: atha rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipatiḥ saparivāraḥ pauṣpakaṃ vimānamadhiruhya yena bhagavāṃstenopajagāma
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, mounted the flowered aerial chariot with his retinue and went to where the Blessed One was.

children.text: upetya vimānādavatīrya saparivāro bhagavantaṃ triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tūryatālāvacaraiḥ pravādyadbhir indranīlamayena daṇḍena vaiḍūryamusārapratyuptāṃ vīṇāṃ priyaṅgupāṇḍunā anarghyeṇa vastreṇa pārśvāvalambitāṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍjarṣabhagāndhāradhaivataniṣādamadhyamakaiśikagītasvaragrāmamūrchanādiyuktenānusārya salīlaṃ vīṇāmanupraviśya gāthābhigītairanugāyati sma
children.translated_text: Having approached, he descended from the aerial chariot with his retinue, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and, while instruments with time-beaters were being played, took up a vīṇā with an indranīla handle, inlaid with beryl and musāra stones, hanging at his side by a priceless pale-priyaṅgu-colored cloth. Following the scale and modes of song joined with the notes ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, dhaivata, niṣāda, madhyama, and kaiśika, he gracefully entered into the vīṇā music and sang along with verses:
"Teach here, O Leader, the rule of dharma according to the nature of mind, the selflessness that is stainless because free from views,
and that which points out the course to be realized personally by oneself.
O Sage, today is the time to go to <s>Laṅkā</s>, to the Sugata whose body is accumulated from pure dharmas, who displays what is magically produced and constructed,

children.text: pratyātmavedyagatidharmarataṃ laṅkāṃ hi gantuṃ samayo'dya mune ||
children.translated_text: and who delights in the dharma whose course is to be realized personally by oneself.
This <s>Laṅkā</s> was inhabited by former Jinas and by their sons, bearers of many forms.

children.text: deśehi nātha iha dharmavaraṃ śroṣyanti yakṣa bahurūpadharāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Teach here, O Lord, the excellent dharma; the yakṣas, bearers of many forms, will listen."

children.text: atha rāvaṇo laṅkādhipatiḥ toṭakavṛttenānugāyya punarapi gāthābhigītenānugāyati sma saptarātreṇa bhagavān sāgarānmakarālayāt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, after singing in the toṭaka meter, again sang with verses: "After seven nights the Blessed One, from the ocean, the abode of makaras,
having risen from the palace of the lord of the ocean, stood upon the shore.
As soon as the Buddha was standing there, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with apsarases,
and with yakṣas of many diverse kinds, including the learned <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>,

children.text: ṛddhyā gatvā tamadhvānaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati nāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: went by supernatural power over that road to where the Leader stood.
Descending from the <s>Puṣpaka</s> vehicle, he bowed to and worshiped the Tathāgata,
and, empowered by the lord of Jinas, announced his name to him:
"I am <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the Ten-necked one, lord of the rākṣasas, come here.

children.text: anugṛhṇāhi me laṅkāṃ ye cāsmin puravāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Show favor to my <s>Laṅkā</s> and to those who dwell in this city.
For by former fully awakened Buddhas too, the sphere of the course personally realized by oneself
was made manifest on the jewel-studded peak in the middle of the city.
May the Blessed One also, right there on the jewel-adorned peak,
teach the stainless dharma, surrounded by the sons of the Jina.

children.text: śrotukāmā vayaṃ cādya ye ca laṅkānivāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We today, and those who dwell in <s>Laṅkā</s>, wish to hear it.
It is free from the method of discursive teaching and belongs to the sphere of the course personally realized by oneself:
the <s>Laṅkāvatārasūtra</s>, praised by former Buddhas.
I remember that this sūtra was spoken by former Buddhas
attended by sons of the Jina; may the Blessed One also proclaim it.
In a future time, whatever Buddhas and sons of Buddhas there will be,
they too, the Leaders, on the jewel-adorned peak,
will teach this very divine method out of compassion for the yakṣas.
In the delightful divine city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, adorned with many jewels,
with cool and lovely slopes and canopies of latticed jewels,
there are here, Blessed One, yakṣas free from passion and hatred, intent on the course personally realized by oneself,
who have been fulfilled by former Buddhas.
Their faith is fixed in the Mahāyāna method, and they are joined to one another.
The yakṣiṇīs and sons of yakṣas desire to understand the Mahāyāna.
Let the Blessed One, the Teacher, come to Mount <s>Malaya</s> in <s>Laṅkā</s>."
And the rākṣasas dwelling in the city, with <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> at their head,
devoted to the Great Vehicle, will hear the course of inner realization.
They have performed service to the Buddhas, and even now they will do so.

children.text: anukampārthaṃ mahyaṃ vai yāhi laṅkāṃ sutaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for me, go to <s>Laṅkā</s> together with your sons.
Accept my house, the companies of apsarases, and various necklaces,
and the lovely <s>Aśoka</s> grove, great sage.

children.text: ājñākaro'haṃ buddhānāṃ ye ca teṣāṃ jinātmajāḥ
children.translated_text: I am obedient to the Buddhas, and to those sons of the Victor.

children.text: nāsti tadyanna deyaṃ me anukampa mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing of mine that should not be given. Have compassion, great sage.
Having heard those words of his, the Lord of the three worlds said:
Even by past guides, lord of yakṣas, on the jeweled mountain,
the dharma of inner realization was taught, and you too were shown compassion.
Future ones also will speak on the mountain adorned with jewels.
For this is the abode of yogins who dwell in the directly seen dharma.
You are to be treated with compassion, lord of yakṣas, by the Sugatas and by me as well.
The Blessed One accepted in silence and remained settled in a mind of tranquility.
He mounted the flower-chariot presented by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
There <s>Rāvaṇa</s> himself and the other confident sons of the Victor,
being honored by apsarases with laughter, dancing, and the like, went to the city.

children.text: tatra gatvā purīṃ ramyāṃ punaḥ pūjāṃ pralabdhavān
children.translated_text: Having gone there to the lovely city, he again received worship.
He was honored by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the hosts of yakṣas, and by yakṣiṇīs,
by sons of yakṣas, daughters of yakṣas, and with nets of jewels.
By <s>Rāvaṇa</s> too necklaces adorned with jewels were placed
upon the heads of the Buddha, the Victor, and the sons of the Victor.
Having accepted the worship, the Blessed One, together with the learned sons of the Victor,
made clear the dharma whose field is the course of inner realization.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the hosts of yakṣas, having fully honored the best of speakers,
honored <s>Mahāmati</s> and entreated him again and again:
You are the questioner of all the Buddhas concerning the field of inner realization.

children.text: ahaṃ hi śrotā yakṣāśca jinaputrāśca sanniha
children.translated_text: I indeed am the hearer, and the yakṣas and the sons of the Victor are present.
I and the yakṣas, together with the learned sons of the Victor, entreat you.
Among disputants you are the great disputant; among yogins you carry the discipline of yoga.

children.text: adhyeṣayāmi tvāṃ bhaktyā nayaṃ pṛccha viśārada ||
children.translated_text: I entreat you with devotion: ask about the method, confident one,
free from the faults of the tīrthikas, and from pratyekabuddhas and śrāvakas,
pure as the nature of the dharma of inner realization, and illuminating the Buddha-stage.
There the Blessed One magically created peaks adorned with jewels,
and other divine things, ornamented with millions of jewels.
On each excellent mountain he displayed his own bodily form,
and there <s>Rāvaṇa</s> the yakṣa stood on each one.

children.text: atra tāḥ parṣadaḥ sarvā ekaikasmin hi dṛśyate
children.translated_text: On each one all those assemblies were seen there,

children.text: sarvakṣetrāṇi tatraiva ye ca teṣu vināyakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all the fields, and the guides who were in them.
The lord of rākṣasas was there too, and those dwelling in <s>Laṅkā</s>.
A <s>Laṅkā</s> corresponding to that one was manifested by the Victor,
as were other <s>Aśoka</s> groves and the beauties of the forest that were there.
On each mountain the Lord, urged on by <s>Mahāmati</s>,
taught the dharma to the yakṣa, indicating the course of inner realization.
On the mountain he taught the entire sūtra of one hundred thousand verses.
Then the Teacher and the sons of the Victor disappeared right there.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> the yakṣa saw his own body standing in his house.

children.text: cinteti kimidaṃ ko'yaṃ deśitaṃ kena vā śrutam
children.translated_text: He thought: What is this? Who is this? By whom was it taught, or by whom was it heard?

children.text: kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kena vā dṛṣṭaṃ nagaro vā kva saugataḥ ||
children.translated_text: What has been seen, or by whom has it been seen? Where is the city, and where is the Sugata?

children.text: tāni kṣetrāṇi te buddhā ratnaśobhāḥ kva saugatāḥ
children.translated_text: Where are those fields, those Buddhas, those jeweled splendors, those Sugatas?
Is this a dream, or perhaps an illusion, a city called a gandharva-city?
Or is what I have seen here like dimness of sight, a mirage, a dream, the birth of a barren woman's child,
or the smoke of a whirling firebrand?

children.text: atha vā dharmatā hyeṣā dharmāṇāṃ cittagocare
children.translated_text: Or else this is indeed the nature of dharmas within the field of mind.
But fools do not understand it, deluded by their imaginings of the world.

children.text: na draṣṭā na ca draṣṭavyaṃ na vācyo nāpi vācakaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no seer and nothing to be seen, no speaker and no speech.
This imagined construction, the state of forms of Buddha-dharmas, is something apart.

children.text: ye paśyanti yathādṛṣṭaṃ na te paśyanti nāyakam ||
children.translated_text: Those who see according to what is seen do not see the Guide.
And when conceptualization does not proceed, one does not see a Buddha as an object.
If one sees in the state where proceeding has ceased, then the Buddha is fully awakened.

children.text: samanantaraprativibuddhe parāvṛttāśraye svacittadṛśyamātrādhigame'vikalpapracārasthitasya laṅkādhipateḥ pūrvakuśalamūlasaṃcoditasya sarvaśāstravidagdhabuddher yathātathyadarśanasya aparapraṇeyasya svabuddhivicālanakuśalasya tarkadṛṣṭivyapetadarśanasya aparapraṇeyasya mahāyogayogino mahāviśvarūpadhāriṇaḥ upāyakauśalyagatiṃgatasya sarvabhūmyuttarottarasvalakṣaṇādhigamanakuśalasya cittamagomanovijñānasvabhāvavivekaratasya trisaṃtativyavacchinnadarśanasya sarvakāraṇatīrthyavyapetabuddheḥ tathā gatagarbhabuddhabhūmyadhyātmasamāpannasya sthitabuddhabuddher gaganādadhyātmavedyaśabdam aśrauṣīt sādhu sādhu laṅkādhipate sādhu khalu punastvaṃ laṅkādhipate
children.translated_text: Immediately after he had awakened, when the basis had turned about, when he had realized that what is seen is only his own mind, and when the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, established in the movement of non-conceptualization, stirred by former roots of merit, with an intellect skilled in all treatises, seeing reality as it is, not to be led by others, skilled in examining by his own understanding, whose vision was free from views based on reasoning, not dependent on another, a great yogin among yogins, bearer of a great universal form, one who had reached the way of skillful means, skilled in realizing the progressively higher own-characteristics of all stages, delighting in the discernment of the nature of mind, thought, and consciousness, seeing the three continuities as severed, whose understanding was free from all causal doctrines of the tīrthikas, inwardly attained to the tathāgatagarbha and the Buddha-stage, and whose awakened understanding was stable, heard from the sky a voice to be known inwardly: Good, good, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>; good indeed again, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yoginā yathā tvaṃ śikṣase
children.translated_text: A yogin should train in just this way, as you are training.

children.text: evaṃ ca tathāgatā draṣṭavyāḥ dharmāśca yathā tvayā dṛṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: And thus the Tathāgatas are to be seen, and dharmas too, just as you have seen them.
If they are seen otherwise, there is reliance on annihilation.
You should discern all dharmas while free from mind, mentation, and consciousness.
You should move inwardly, not be fixed upon the view of external objects.
Nor should you abide in a samādhi whose view has fallen into the range of objects reached by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and tīrthikas.
You should not be devoted to tales and old stories.

children.text: na svabhāvadṛṣṭinā na rājādhipatyamadapatitena na ṣaḍdhyānādidhyāyinā
children.translated_text: You should not hold a view of own-being, nor fall into the pride of royal supremacy, nor meditate on the six dhyānas and the like.

children.text: eṣa laṅkādhipate abhisamayo mahāyoginā parapravādamathanānām akuśaladṛṣṭidālanānām ātmadṛṣṭivyāvartanakuśalānāṃ sūkṣmam abhivijñānaparāvṛttikuśalānāṃ jinaputrāṇāṃ mahāyānacaritānām
children.translated_text: This, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is the realization of the sons of the Jina who are great yogins, who crush opposing doctrines, break down unwholesome views, are skilled in turning away the view of self, are skilled in the subtle transformation of higher consciousness, and practice the Mahāyāna.
You should undertake yoga in order to enter and attain the Tathāgata's own personally realized level.

children.text: evaṃ kriyamāṇe bhūyo 'pyuttarottaraviśodhako 'yaṃ laṅkādhipate mārgo yastvayā parigṛhītaḥ samādhikauśalasamāpattyā
children.translated_text: When this is done, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, this path that you have undertaken through skill in samādhi and attainment becomes ever more purified, higher and higher.

children.text: na ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyānupraveśasukhagocaro yathā bālatīrthayogayogibhiḥ kalpyate ātmagrāhadṛśyalakṣaṇābhiniviṣṭair bhūtaguṇadravyānucāribhir avidyāpratyayadṛṣṭyabhiniveśābhiniviṣṭaiḥ śūnyatotpādavikṣiptair vikalpābhiniviṣṭair lakṣyalakṣaṇapatitāśayaiḥ
children.translated_text: It is not the happy object-domain entered by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and tīrthikas, as imagined by childish yogins who practice the yoga of outsiders, who cling to the visible marks of self-grasping, who follow elements, qualities, and substances, who are fixed upon views conditioned by ignorance, who are distracted from emptiness and arising, fixed on conceptual construction, and whose intentions have fallen into object and characteristic.
This Mahāyāna attainment, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, brings one to courses of manifold form; it awakens one to the course within one's own realization.
And it proceeds for the obtaining of rebirth in a distinguished state of existence.
This entrance into Mahāyāna yoga, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, turns back the many waves of consciousness in the sheath of obscuration; it is not a fall into reliance on the yoga of the tīrthikas.
For the yoga of the tīrthikas, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, proceeds from the outsiders' clinging to self.
Because they see and cling to the meanings of the two own-natures of consciousness, the yoga of the founders of outside systems is ungracious.
Therefore, good, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>: reflect on this very matter.
As you reflected after seeing the Tathāgata,
that alone is seeing the Tathāgata.

children.text: atha tasminnantare rāvaṇasyaitadabhavat yannvahaṃ punarapi bhagavantaṃ sarvayogavaśavartinaṃ tīrthyayogavyāvartakaṃ pratyātmagatigocarodbhāvakaṃ nairmitanairmāṇikavyapetam adhigamabuddhir yadyogināṃ yogābhisamayakāle samādhimukhe samāptānāmadhigamo bhavati
children.translated_text: Then at that moment this occurred to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>: 'What if I were once again to see the Blessed One, who has mastery over all yogas, who turns back the yoga of the tīrthikas, who reveals the object-domain of the course personally realized by oneself, who is free from magically created and constructed appearances, and whose wisdom is attainment, the attainment that yogins have when, at the time of yogic realization, they have entered the doorway of samādhi?

children.text: tasya ca adhigamādyoginā yogaśabdo nipātyate adhigamaneneti
children.translated_text: And because of that attainment the word yoga is applied to a yogin, since there is attainment.

children.text: tadahaṃ kāruṇikaṃ kleśendhanavikalpakṣayakaraṃ taṃ jinaputraiḥ parivṛtaṃ sarvasattvacittāśayānupraviṣṭaṃ sarvagataṃ sarvajñaṃ kriyālakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ tayaivamṛddhyā paśyeyam taddarśanānnādhigatamadhigaccheyam adhigataṃ ca me nirvikalpācāraḥ sukhasamādhisamāpattivihārastathāgatagatibhūmiprāpako vivṛddhiṃ yāyāt
children.translated_text: May I see, through that very miraculous power, that compassionate one who brings about the exhaustion of the fuel of afflictions and conceptual construction, surrounded by sons of the Jina, entering into the mental dispositions of all beings, omnipresent, all-knowing, and turned away from marks of action. From seeing him may I attain what has not been attained; and may what has been attained by me, the conduct free from conceptual construction and the dwelling in the attainment of blissful samādhi that brings one to the Tathāgata's course and level, increase.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ laṅkādhipater anutpattikadharmakṣāntyadhigataṃ viditvā tayaiva śobhayā daśagrīvasyānukampayā punarapyātmānaṃ śikhare subahuratnakhacite ratnajālavitate darśayati sma
children.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One, knowing that the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> had attained acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas, out of compassion for <s>Daśagrīva</s>, with that same splendor, again showed himself on the peak richly inlaid with many jewels and spread with a net of jewels.

children.text: adrākṣīddaśagrīvo laṅkādhipatiḥ punarapi dṛṣṭānubhūtāṃ śobhāṃ śikhare tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvātriṃśadvaralakṣaṇavibhūṣitatanum
children.translated_text: <s>Daśagrīva</s>, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, again saw the splendor he had seen and experienced before: the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, his body adorned with the thirty-two excellent marks.

children.text: svātmabhāvaṃ caikaikasmingirau tathāgatānāṃ purataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ mahāmatinā sārdhaṃ tathāgatapratyātmagatigocarakathāṃ prakurvantaṃ yakṣaiḥ parivṛtaṃ tāṃ deśanāpāṭhakathāṃ kathayantam
children.translated_text: He also saw his own bodily form on each mountain before the Tathāgatas, the perfectly awakened Buddhas, together with <s>Mahāmati</s>, carrying on a discourse about the Tathāgata's object-domain of the course personally realized by oneself, surrounded by yakṣas, and teaching that chapter-discourse of instruction.
And those fields had their leaders.

children.text: atha bhagavān punarapi tasyāṃ velāyāṃ parṣadamavalokya buddhyā na māṃsacakṣuṣā siṃharājavadvijṛmbhya mahāhāsamahasat
children.translated_text: Then again at that time the Blessed One looked over the assembly with wisdom, not with the fleshly eye, stretched himself like a lion-king, and laughed a great laugh.

children.text: ūrṇākośācca raśmiṃ niścāryamāṇaḥ pārśvorukaṭikāyācca śrīvatsātsarvaromakūpebhyo yugāntāgniriva dīpyamānaḥ tejasendradhanurudayabhāskaropamena prabhāmaṇḍalena dedīpyamānaḥ śakrabrahmalokapālairgaganatale nirīkṣyamāṇaḥ sumeruśṛṅgapratispardhini śikhare niṣaṇṇo mahāhāsamahasat
children.translated_text: Emitting a ray from the curl of hair between his brows, and also from his sides, thighs, waist, body, from the śrīvatsa, and from every pore, blazing like the fire at the end of an age, shining with a halo like the splendor of <s>Indra</s>'s bow and the rising sun, watched in the sky by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the guardians of the world, seated on a peak rivaling the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, he laughed a great laugh.

children.text: atha tasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaḥ teṣāṃ ca śakrabrahmādīnāmetad abhavat ko nu khalvatra hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadbhagavān sarvadharmavaśavartī mahāhāsaṃ smitapūrvakaṃ hasati raśmīṃśca svavigrahebhyo niścārayati niścārya tūṣṇīmabhavat svapratyātmāryajñānagocarasamādhimukhe patitāśayo'vismitaḥ siṃhāvalokanatayā diśo'valokya rāvaṇasyaiva yogagatipracāram anuvicintayamānaḥ
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to that assembly of bodhisattvas and to those beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>: 'What indeed is the cause here, what is the condition, that the Blessed One, who has mastery over all dharmas, laughs a great laugh preceded by a smile, emits rays from his own limbs, and, having emitted them, has become silent, his intention absorbed in the samādhi-door whose object is noble knowledge personally realized by oneself, unastonished, looking about in the directions with a lion's gaze, contemplating <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s movement in the course of yoga?'

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvamevādhyeṣito rāvaṇasyānukampāmupādāya tasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaścittāśayavicāramājñāya anāgatāṃ janatāṃ cāvalokya deśanāpāṭhābhiratānāṃ sattvānāṃ cittavibhramo bhaviṣyatīti yathārutārthābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyayogabalābhiniviṣṭānāṃ tathāgatā api bhagavanto vinivṛttavijñānaviṣayā mahāhāsaṃ hasanti
children.translated_text: Then indeed the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, having already been urged before, out of compassion for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, knowing the investigation of his mental disposition and that of that assembly of bodhisattvas, and looking also toward future people, thought, "For beings who delight in the course of teaching there will be confusion of mind, since they cling to the meaning exactly as heard and cling to the powers of all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, outsiders, and yogins; yet even the Tathāgatas, the Blessed Ones, whose field of cognition has ceased, laugh a great laugh."

children.text: teṣāṃ kautūhalavinivṛttyarthaṃ bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchati sma kaḥ khalvatra hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya pravṛttaye bhagavānāha sādhu sādhu mahāmate sādhu khalu punastvaṃ mahāmate lokasvabhāvamavalokya kudṛṣṭipatitānāṃ ca lokānāṃ traikālyacittāvabodhāya mā praṣṭumārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of removing their curiosity, he asked the Blessed One: "What is the cause here, what is the condition, for the arising of the smile?" The Blessed One said, "Good, good, <s>Mahāmati</s>; good indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>. Having observed the nature of the world and the worlds fallen into false views, you have begun to ask for the awakening to mind in the three times.
Wise people who ask questions should be of this kind, for the sake of oneself, others, and both.

children.text: eṣa mahāmate rāvaṇo laṅkādhipatiḥ pūrvakānapi tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān praśnadvayaṃ pṛṣṭavān
children.translated_text: This <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, asked the former Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, the two questions.

He now wishes to ask me too, in order to make clear what has not been tasted: the characteristic of the divisions, course, and marks of the two questions of all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, outsiders, and yogins.

children.text: ya eṣa praṣṭukāmo daśagrīvo'nāgatānapi jinān prakṣyati
children.translated_text: This Ten-necked one, who wishes to ask it, will ask future Jinas also."

children.text: jānanneva bhagavāṃllaṅkādhipatim etad avocat pṛccha tvaṃ laṅkādhipate
children.translated_text: Knowing this, the Blessed One said this to the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>: "Ask, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
An opportunity has been granted to you by the Tathāgata.
Do not delay, O one whose diadem is trembling.

children.text: yadyadevākāṅkṣasi ahaṃ te tasya tasyaiva praśnasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: Whatever you desire, I will satisfy your mind by answering each of those questions.

children.text: yathā tvaṃ parāvṛttavikalpāśraye bhūmivipakṣakauśalena pravicayabuddhyā vicārayamāṇaḥ pratyātmanayalakṣaṇasamādhisukhavihāraṃ samādhibuddhaiḥ parigṛhītaḥ śamathasukhavyavasthitaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamādhipakṣān atikramya acalāsādhumatīdharmameghābhūmivyavasthito dharmanairātmyayathātathākuśalo mahāratnapadmavimāne samādhijinābhiṣekatāṃ pratilapsyase
children.translated_text: Thus, when you are examining with investigative understanding, through skill in the opposing factors of the stages, in the support where conceptual construction has turned back, you will dwell in the bliss of samādhi whose characteristic is the principle personally realized by oneself; you will be accepted by Buddhas in samādhi, established in the bliss of śamatha, and, having passed beyond the sides of the samādhis of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, established in the stages called <s>Acalā</s>, <s>Sādhumatī</s>, and <s>Dharmameghā</s>, skilled in the reality of the selflessness of dharmas, you will obtain consecration by Jinas in samādhi in a great jewel-lotus palace.

children.text: tadanurūpaiḥ padmaiḥ svakāyavicitrādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitais taiḥ padmaiḥ svakāyaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ drakṣyasi anyonyavaktramukhanirīkṣaṇaṃ ca kariṣyasi
children.translated_text: With lotuses corresponding to that, empowered by the varied empowering power of your own body, you will see your own body seated on those lotuses, and you will look face to face at one another.
Such an inconceivable object-field is that which, brought forth by a single skillful act of production, has been brought forth while one is established on the stage of practice.

children.text: upāyakauśalaparigrahābhinirhārābhinirhṛte tam acintyaviṣayam anuprāpsyasi bahurūpavikāratāṃ ca tathāgatabhūmim
children.translated_text: Through the production brought forth by the embrace of skillful means, you will reach that inconceivable object-field and the Tathāgata-stage with its manifold transformations.
You will attain what had not previously been seen by śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, outsiders, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and the rest."

children.text: atha khalu laṅkādhipatirbhagavatā kṛtāvakāśa utthāya tasmād raśmivimalaprabhād ratnapadmasadṛśād ratnaśikharāt sāpsarogaṇaparivṛto vividhairanekavidhairnānāprakāraiḥ puṣpamālyagandhadhūpavilepanachattradhvajapatākāhārārdhahārakirīṭamukuṭair anyaiśca adṛṣṭaśrutapūrvairābharaṇaviśeṣair viśiṣṭais tūryatālāvacarair devanāgayakṣarākṣasagandharvakiṃnaramahoragamanuṣyātikrāntaiḥ sarvakāmadhātuparyāpannān vādyabhāṇḍānabhinirmāya ye cānyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tūryaviśeṣā dṛṣṭāḥ tānabhinirmāya bhagavantaṃ bodhisattvāṃśca ratnajālenāvaṣṭabhya nānāvastrocchritapatākaṃ kṛtvā sapta tālān gagane'bhyudgamya mahāpūjāmeghānabhipravṛṣya tūryatālāvacarāṇi nirnādya tasmādgaganādavatīrya sūryavidyutprabhe dvitīye mahāratnapadmālaṃkṛtau ratnaśikhare niṣasāda
children.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, having been granted an opportunity by the Blessed One, rose from that jewel peak like a jewel lotus with stainless radiance of rays. Surrounded by a company of apsarases, with flowers, garlands, perfumes, incense, ointments, parasols, standards, banners, necklaces, half-necklaces, diadems, and crowns of various, manifold, and many kinds, and with other distinguished ornaments never seen or heard before, with excellent instruments and time-beaters surpassing those of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and humans, he magically produced all musical instruments included in the realm of desire, and also produced those special instruments that are seen in other buddha-fields. Covering the Blessed One and the bodhisattvas with a jewel net and raising banners of various cloths, he ascended seven palm-trees high into the sky, rained down great clouds of worship, sounded the instruments and time-beaters, descended from the sky, and sat down on a second jewel peak adorned with great jewel lotuses, shining like the sun and lightning.

children.text: niṣadya upacārātsmitapūrvaṃ bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśo bhagavantaṃ praśnadvayaṃ pṛcchati sma pṛṣṭā mayā pūrvakāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Having sat down, and having respectfully been granted an opportunity by the Blessed One with a smile beforehand, he asked the Blessed One the two questions: "I asked the former Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas,
and they too answered them.
Now I ask the Blessed One also.
And in the course of teaching this will certainly be described by the Buddhas and by you.
Blessed One, this pair of dharmas is spoken by magically created beings and magical creations.
It is not spoken by silent Tathāgatas.
For silent Tathāgatas, Blessed One, reveal only the domain of the bliss of samādhi.
They do not conceptually construct the domain,
but they teach it.

children.text: tatsādhu me bhagavān svayameva dharmavaśavartī dharmadvayaṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho deśayatu
children.translated_text: Therefore may the Blessed One himself, being subject to the power of dharma, may the Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha, teach me the pair of dharmas.
These sons of the Jina and I will listen."
The Blessed One said, "Speak, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the pair of dharmas."

children.text: rākṣasendra āha kirīṭāṅgadahāravajrasūtrāvabaddhābharaṇatanuśobhāśobhita dharmā eva prahātavyāḥ prāgevādharmāḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of rākṣasas said, "O you whose body is adorned with the beauty of ornaments bound with diadems, armlets, necklaces, and vajra-threads: dharmas themselves are to be abandoned, still more adharmas."

children.text: tatkathaṃ bhagavan dharmadvayaṃ prahāṇaṃ bhavati ke cādharmā dharmāḥ kathaṃ sati dvitvaṃ prahāṇadharmāṇāṃ vikalpalakṣaṇapatitānāṃ vikalpasvabhāvābhāvānām abhautikabhautikānām ālayavijñānāparijñānād aviśeṣalakṣaṇānāṃ keśoṇḍukasvabhāvāvasthitānām aśuddhakṣayajñānaviṣayiṇām
children.translated_text: How then, Blessed One, does abandonment of the pair of dharmas take place? And which are adharmas and dharmas? Since duality exists, how is there abandonment of things to be abandoned, which have fallen into the character of conceptual construction, whose own nature is the absence of conceptual construction, which are both non-material and material, whose mark is not distinguished because the storehouse-consciousness is not understood, which remain in the nature of hairs seen by diseased eyes, and which are objects of knowledge concerning the exhaustion of impurity?

children.text: tatkathaṃ teṣāṃ prahāṇam evaṃbhāvinām bhagavānāha nanu laṅkādhipate dṛṣṭo ghaṭādīnāṃ bhedanātmakānāṃ vināśadharmiṇāṃ bālavikalpagocaraiḥ prativibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: How, Blessed One, is there abandonment of them when they are of this kind? The Blessed One said: Is it not seen, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, that there is a differentiation, for the sphere of childish imagination, among jars and the like, things whose nature is breakage and whose property is destruction?

children.text: evamihāpi kiṃ na gṛhyate asti dharmādharmayoḥ prativibhāgo bālaprativikalpam upādāya na tvāryajñānādhigamaṃ prati darśanena
children.translated_text: So here too why is it not accepted that there is a differentiation of dharma and adharma, relying on childish conceptual construction, but not with respect to the attainment of noble knowledge through seeing?

children.text: tiṣṭhantu tāvallaṅkādhipate ghaṭādayo bhāvā vicitralakṣaṇapatitā bālānāṃ na tvāryāṇām
children.translated_text: Let jars and the like, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, remain aside for now: entities fallen into varied characteristics exist for fools, but not for noble ones.

A differentiation is seen among things of one nature, lit by flames arisen from one fire, established in houses, mansions, gardens, and palaces; and because of the fuel there are differences of long and short, little and great brightness.

children.text: evamihāpi kiṃ na gṛhyate asti dharmādharmayoḥ prativibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: So here too why is it not accepted that there is a differentiation of dharma and adharma?

children.text: na kevalam agnijvālāyā ekasaṃtānapatitāyā dṛṣṭo'rciṣaśca prativibhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Not only is a differentiation of flame and tongues of fire seen within a single continuum of fire.
Even among continuums produced from one seed, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, there are differences of stalk, sprout, joint, node, leaf, foliage, flower, fruit, and branch.

children.text: evaṃ sarvadharmaprarohadharmiṇāṃ bāhyānām ādhyātmikānām apyavidyāniryātānāṃ skandhadhātvāyatanopagānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ traidhātukopapannānāṃ dṛṣṭasukhasaṃsthānām abhilāpyagativiśeṣāḥ
children.translated_text: In this same way, among all things that have the nature of sprouting into dharmas, external and internal, issued from ignorance, included in the aggregates, elements, and sense-spheres, arisen in the three realms, and appearing as structures of seen pleasure, there are differences of expressible courses.

children.text: vijñānānām ekalakṣaṇānāṃ viṣayābhigrahaṇapravṛttānāṃ dṛṣṭo hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamaviśeṣo vyavadānāvyavadānataśca kuśalākuśalataśca
children.translated_text: Among consciousnesses, though they have one characteristic and operate by grasping objects, a difference is seen as inferior, superior, and middling, and also according to purity and impurity, and according to skillful and unskillful.

children.text: na kevalam eṣā laṅkādhipate dharmāṇāṃ prativibhāgaviśeṣaḥ yogināmapi yogamabhyasyatāṃ yogamārge pratyātmagatilakṣaṇaviśeṣo dṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Not only this, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is there a special differentiation among dharmas; for yogins too, practicing yoga on the path of yoga, a difference of characteristics in the course of personal realization is seen.

children.text: kimaṅga punar dharmādharmayoḥ prativikalpapravṛttayor viśeṣo na bhavati bhavatyeva
children.translated_text: How much more, then, would there not be a difference between dharma and adharma, which proceed through conceptual discrimination? There certainly is.
There is, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, a differentiation of dharma and adharma, because they have the character of conceptual construction.

children.text: tatra laṅkādhipate dharmāḥ katame yaduta ete tīrthyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabālavikalpakalpitāḥ
children.translated_text: There, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, which are the dharmas? Namely, those imagined by outsiders, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and fools through conceptual construction.

children.text: kāraṇato guṇadravyapūrvakā dharmā ityupadiśyante te prahātavyāḥ
children.translated_text: They are taught as dharmas on the basis of cause, quality, and substance; these are to be abandoned.
They are not to be conceptually discriminated by characteristic.

children.text: svacittadṛśyadharmatābhiniveśānna santi ghaṭādayo dharmā bālaparikalpitā alabdhaśarīrāḥ
children.translated_text: Because of clinging to the dharmatā of what appears as one's own mind, jars and the like, dharmas imagined by fools, do not exist; they have no obtained body.
For one who examines and sees distinctly with such insight, they are abandoned.

children.text: tatra adharmāḥ katame ye'labdhātmakā lakṣaṇavikalpāpracārā dharmā ahetukāḥ teṣāmapravṛttirdṛṣṭā bhūtābhūtataḥ
children.translated_text: There, which are the adharmas? Those dharmas whose self is not obtained, for which conceptual discrimination of characteristics does not operate, which are without cause; their non-arising is seen as neither existent nor non-existent.
Then abandonment of adharma takes place.
Again, which are the dharmas whose self is not obtained? Namely, dharmas such as a hare's horn, the horns of camels and horses, and a barren woman's son.
Because their self is not obtained, they are not to be imagined according to characteristic.

children.text: te'nyatra saṃvyavahārārthā abhidhīyante nābhiniveśato yathā ghaṭādayaḥ
children.translated_text: They are spoken of only for the sake of conventional usage, not through clinging, as jars and the like are.

children.text: yathā te praheyā agrahaṇato vijñānena tathā vikalpabhāvā api praheyāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as they are to be abandoned because they are not grasped by consciousness, so too the states of conceptual construction are to be abandoned.
Thus there is abandonment of dharma and adharma.

children.text: yaduktavānasi laṅkādhipate dharmādharmāḥ kathaṃ praheyā iti tadetaduktam
children.translated_text: What you said, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, 'How are dharmas and adharmas to be abandoned?' has now been stated.

children.text: yadapyuktavānasi laṅkādhipate pūrvakā api tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā mayā pṛṣṭāḥ taiśca visarjitaṃ pūrvam
children.translated_text: And as for what you said, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, that former Tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas were also asked by you and that they too answered before:
this, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is a designation for conceptual construction.
Even the past is conceptualized as 'past.'
So too the future and the present are conceptualized according to dharmatā.
The Tathāgatas are free from conceptual construction, beyond all proliferation of conceptual constructions.
They are not conceptualized as having the own-nature of form.
Rather, for the sake of happiness they are made manifest through attainment of knowledge.
By wisdom they move without signs.
Therefore the Tathāgatas are of the nature of knowledge; they have bodies of knowledge.
They do not conceive, and they are not conceived.

children.text: kena na kalpante manasā ātmato jīvataḥ pudgalataḥ
children.translated_text: By what do they not conceive? By mind, as self, as living being, or as person.

children.text: kathaṃ na vikalpante manovijñānena viṣayārthahetukena yathā rūpalakṣaṇasaṃsthānākārataśca
children.translated_text: How are they not conceptually constructed? By mental consciousness caused by the object as its purpose, and according to form, characteristic, configuration, and shape.
Therefore one should be one who has gone beyond conceptualization and non-conceptualization.
Moreover, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the activity of beings is like figures painted on a wall.
The arrangement of the world, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is motionless and devoid of action and activity, because all dharmas are without being.
And here no one hears, nor is anything heard.
For the arrangement of the world, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is like something magically fashioned.
But outsider and foolish yogins do not understand this.

children.text: ya evaṃ paśyati laṅkādhipate sa samyakpaśyati
children.translated_text: The one who sees in this way, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, sees correctly.
Those who see otherwise move in conceptual construction."
Their own conceptual constructions grasp in two ways.

children.text: tadyathā darpaṇāntargataṃ svabimbapratibimbaṃ jale vā svāṅgacchāyā vā jyotsnādīpapradīpite vā gṛhe vā aṅgacchāyā pratiśrutkāni
children.translated_text: For example: one's own reflected image inside a mirror, or one's own bodily shadow in water, or the shadow of a body in a house lit by moonlight, a lamp, and the like, or echoes.
Then, having accepted the grasping of their own conceptualization, they conceptually distinguish <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
And they do not proceed by abandoning <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
They imagine and nourish them, and they do not obtain pacification.

children.text: ekāgrasyaitad adhivacanam tathāgatagarbhasvapratyātmāryajñānagocarasyaitat praveśo yatsamādhiḥ paramo jāyata iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the designation of one-pointedness; this is the entrance into the domain of the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> (embryo of the Tathāgata) and of noble knowledge personally realized in oneself, namely, that the supreme <s>samādhi</s> arises.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatir bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāmatibodhisattvasahitaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrānucārī buddhānubhāvena utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantaṃ gāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, accompanied by the bodhisattva <s>Mahāmati</s>, roaming through all buddha-fields, by the power of the Buddhas rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, bowed with folded hands toward the Blessed One, and praised the Blessed One with verses.
The world is free from arising and destruction, like a flower in the sky.
It is not apprehended by you as existent or nonexistent, through your wisdom and your compassion.
All dharmas are like illusion, devoid of mind and consciousness.
They are not apprehended by you as existent or nonexistent, through your wisdom and your compassion.
And the world, always like a dream, is free from eternalism and annihilationism.
It is not apprehended by you as existent or nonexistent, through your wisdom and your compassion.
What praise can there be of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (body of dharma), whose nature is illusion and dream?
The non-arising of things that are without own-nature: that is their arising.
For one whose seeing is invisible and disconnected from the senses and their objects,

children.text: praśaṃsā yadi vā nindā tasyocyeta kathaṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: how could either praise or blame be spoken, O Sage?
The selflessness of dharmas and persons, and the afflictive and knowable obscurations, are always

children.text: viśuddham ā nimittena prajñayā kṛpayā ca te ||
children.translated_text: purified by you, free from signs, through wisdom and compassion.

children.text: na nirvāsi nirvāṇena nirvāṇaṃ tvayi saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: You are not extinguished by nirvāṇa; nirvāṇa abides in you,
free from Buddha and what is to be awakened to, free from the side of existence and nonexistence.
Those who see the peaceful Sage in this way, free from arising,
become free from appropriation, stainless here and hereafter.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatir bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantamābhiḥ sārūpyābhir gāthābhir abhiṣṭutya svanāmagotraṃ bhagavate saṃśrāvayati sma
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, having praised the Blessed One with these fitting verses, announced his own name and lineage to the Blessed One.
I am <s>Mahāmati</s>, Blessed One, one who has entered the course of the Great Vehicle.
I ask one hundred and eight questions of the best of speakers.

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā buddho lokavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard that speech of his, the Buddha, best of those who know the world,
looked over the whole assembly and addressed the son of the Sugata:

children.text: pṛcchantu māṃ jinasutāstvaṃ ca pṛccha mahāmate
children.translated_text: Let the sons of the Jina ask me, and you too ask, <s>Mahāmati</s>.
I shall teach you the domain of the course personally realized within oneself.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatir bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśo bhagavataścaraṇayornipatya bhagavantaṃ praśnaṃ paripṛcchati sma
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, given permission by the Blessed One, fell at the Blessed One's feet and asked the Blessed One a question.

children.text: kathaṃ hi śudhyate tarkaḥ kasmāttarkaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: How, then, is reasoning purified? Why does reasoning proceed?

children.text: kathaṃ hi dṛśyate bhrāntiḥ kasmādbhrāntiḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: How, then, is illusion seen? Why does illusion proceed?
Why are there fields, emanations, marks, and those who are outsiders?

children.text: nirābhāsaḥ kramaḥ kena jinaputrāśca te kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By what is there freedom from appearance and sequence, and from where are those sons of the Jina?

children.text: muktasya gamanaṃ kutra baddhaḥ kaḥ kena mucyate
children.translated_text: Where is the going of one who is liberated? Who is bound, and by what is he released?

children.text: dhyāyināṃ viṣayaḥ ko'sau kathaṃ yānatrayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: What is that object-domain of meditators? How can there be the three vehicles?

children.text: pratyaye jāyate kiṃ tatkāryaṃ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ca kim
children.translated_text: What is it that is born from conditions? What is effect, and what is cause?
By what, and how, does talk of both extremes proceed?
How can there be formless attainment and cessation?
And how is there cessation of perception? How and why is one released?
By what does action proceed, and the movement of embodied beings?

children.text: kathaṃ dṛśyaṃ vibhāvaḥ kathaṃ kathaṃ bhūmiṣu vartate ||
children.translated_text: How is the visible object manifestation? How does one proceed on the stages?

children.text: nirbhidyettribhavaṃ ko'sau kiṃ sthānaṃ kā tanurbhavet
children.translated_text: Who is it that pierces through the three worlds? What is the place, and what body would there be?

children.text: sthitaḥ pravartate kutra jinaputraḥ kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Where does one stand and proceed? How does one become a son of the Jina?
By what does one obtain the superknowledges, the masteries, and the samādhis?

children.text: samādhyate kathaṃ cittaṃ brūhi me jinapuṃgava ||
children.translated_text: How is the mind brought into samādhi? Tell me, bull among Jinas.
How and why are there the <s>ālaya</s> (storehouse consciousness) and just the mind-consciousness?
How does the visible object proceed, and how does one turn away from the visible object?
How and by what are lineage and non-lineage? How can there be mind-only?

children.text: lakṣaṇasya vyavasthānaṃ nairātmyaṃ ca kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: How is the establishment of a mark, and how can there be selflessness?

children.text: kathaṃ na vidyate sattvaḥ saṃvṛtyā deśanā katham
children.translated_text: How is it that no being exists? How is teaching given conventionally?
How does the view of eternalism and annihilationism not proceed?

children.text: kathaṃ hi tīrthikāstvaṃ ca lakṣaṇairna virudhyase
children.translated_text: How, then, are the outsiders and you not in contradiction with respect to marks?
Tell me, how will the logicians be in the future?

children.text: śūnyatā ca kathaṃ kena kṣaṇabhaṅgaśca te katham
children.translated_text: How and by what is emptiness, and how is your momentary destruction?

children.text: kathaṃ pravartate garbhaḥ kathaṃ loko nirīhikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How does the embryo proceed, and how is the world inactive?
By what is it like illusion and dream? How is it like a gandharva-city?
By what is the world like a mirage and the moon in water? Tell me.
How and by what are the factors of awakening? From where are the aids to awakening?
How are <s>Māras</s>, disturbance of a country, and the view of becoming?
How is it unborn and unceasing, like a flower in the sky?

children.text: kathaṃ ca budhyase lokaṃ kathaṃ brūṣe nirakṣaram ||
children.translated_text: And how do you understand the world? How do you say it is without syllables?
By what can there be non-conceptuality, and how are they like the sky?
How many kinds of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) are there, and how many kinds of mind and pāramitās?
By what is there the sequence of stages, and what is the course free from appearances?

children.text: nairātmyaṃ ca dvidhā kena kathaṃ jñeyaṃ viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: By what is selflessness twofold, and how is what is to be known purified?

children.text: jñānaṃ katividhaṃ nātha śīlaṃ sattvākarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: How many kinds of knowledge are there, Lord, and how many kinds of moral discipline and forms of beings?
By what are lineages set in motion, those born from gold, jewels, and pearls?
By what is speech born, and by what is there the variety of the states of beings?
And how, and by whom, were the sciences and arts made manifest?
How many kinds of verse are there, and how are prose and metrical verse?

children.text: kathaṃ yuktiḥ katividhā vyākhyānaṃ ca kathaṃvidham ||
children.translated_text: How many kinds of reasoning are there, and what kind of exposition is there?

children.text: annapānaṃ ca vaicitryaṃ maithunaṃ jāyate katham
children.translated_text: How does the variety of food and drink arise, and how does sexual union arise?

children.text: rājā ca cakravartī ca maṇḍalī ca kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And how can there be a king, a universal monarch, and a regional ruler?
How should a kingdom be protected, and what are the bodies of the gods like?
By what are the groups of earth and stars, and how are the moon and sun?

children.text: vidyāsthānaṃ bhavetkiṃ ca mokṣo yogī katividhaḥ
children.translated_text: What is a science, and how many kinds of liberation and yogin are there?
How many kinds of disciple are there, and what is a teacher like?
How many kinds of Buddha are there, and what are the birth-stories like?
How many kinds of <s>Māra</s> are there, and how many kinds of heretics?
How many kinds of own-nature are there, and how many kinds of mind can there be?

children.text: prajñaptimātraṃ ca kathaṃ brūhi me vadatāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: And how is there mere designation? Tell me, best of speakers.

children.text: ghanāḥ khe pavanaṃ kena smṛtirmeghaḥ kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: By what are clouds in the sky? How can memory be a cloud?

children.text: taruvallyaḥ kathaṃ kena brūhi me tribhaveśvara ||
children.translated_text: By what, and how, are trees and creepers? Tell me, Lord of the three worlds.

children.text: hayā gajā mṛgāḥ kena grahaṇaṃ yānti bāliśāḥ
children.translated_text: By what do horses, elephants, deer, and foolish beings come to be seized?

children.text: uhoḍimā narāḥ kena brūhi me cittasārathe ||
children.translated_text: By what are men of the uhoḍima type? Tell me, charioteer of the mind.
By what is the grasping of the six seasons, and how can there be an <s>icchantika</s>?

children.text: strīpuṃnapuṃsakānāṃ ca kathaṃ janma vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: And tell me how birth occurs among women, men, and neuters.
How does one turn away from yoga, and how does yoga proceed?

children.text: kathaṃ caivaṃvidhā yoge narāḥ sthāpyā vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: And tell me how people of such a kind are to be established in yoga.

children.text: gatyāgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ kiṃ liṅgaṃ kiṃ ca lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: What is the sign and what is the mark of beings who go and come?

children.text: dhaneśvaraḥ kathaṃ kena brūhi me gaganopama ||
children.translated_text: How, and by what, is there a lord of wealth? Tell me, sky-like one.
How, and by what, is there the Śākya lineage? How is it born from <s>Ikṣvāku</s>?
By what was the seer of long austerity, and how was it brought about by him?
Why are you yourself seen everywhere, in all fields,
surrounded by sons of the Jina with various names and such forms?

children.text: abhakṣyaṃ hi kathaṃ māṃsaṃ kathaṃ māṃsaṃ niṣidhyate
children.translated_text: Why is meat not to be eaten, and why is meat prohibited?
By what do those born in lineages of flesh-eaters eat meat?
How are the arrangements of moon and sun like <s>Meru</s> and lotuses?
By what are fields arranged like the <s>śrīvatsa</s> and a lion? Tell me.
How are they inverted and facing downward, like magical illusions?

children.text: sarvaratnamayāḥ kṣetrāḥ kathaṃ kena vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: By what are fields made entirely of all jewels? Tell me.
How are they arranged like vīṇās and drums, and like various flowers and fruits?
How are they stainless like the sun and moon? By what? Tell me.

children.text: kena nirmāṇikā buddhāḥ kena buddhā vipākajāḥ
children.translated_text: By what are Buddhas emanational, and by what are Buddhas born of maturation?

children.text: tathatā jñānabuddhā vai kathaṃ kena vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: How, and by what, are the Buddhas of suchness and knowledge? Tell me.

children.text: kāmadhātau kathaṃ kena na vibuddho vadāhi me
children.translated_text: How, and by what, is one not awakened in the desire-realm? Tell me.
But for what reason do you awaken among the dispassionate in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>?
When the <s>Sugata</s> has passed into nirvāṇa, who will uphold the teaching?
How long-lasting will the teacher be, and how long will the doctrine remain?
How many kinds is your established doctrine, and what kind is view?

children.text: vinayo bhikṣubhāvaśca kathaṃ kena vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: How, and by what, are discipline and the state of being a monk? Tell me.
By what is there the state of transformation, and how the state free from appearances?
Tell me about the solitary Jinas' sons and the hearers.
By what are there worldly superknowledges, and how can they be supramundane?

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta kathaṃ kena vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: How, and by what, are the seven stages mind? Tell me.
How many kinds is your Saṅgha, and how can there be a schism in the Saṅgha?

children.text: cikitsāśāstraṃ sattvānāṃ kathaṃ kena vadāhi me ||
children.translated_text: How, and by what, is there medical science for beings? Tell me.
You say, 'I am <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Ṛkuchanda</s>, and also <s>Konākamuni</s>,
among the sons of the Jina'; tell me why, great Sage.
By what is there talk whose nature is unreal, and how is there talk of permanence and destruction?
Why do you not everywhere proclaim the truth as mind-only?
By what are groves of men and women, and groves of harītakī and āmalakī trees?
How are <s>Kailāsa</s>, the <s>Cakravāla</s>, and adamantine formations?
Who are the immovable ones there between, adorned with various jewels,
filled with seers and gandharvas? How, and by what, are they? Tell me.

children.text: idaṃ śrutvā mahāvīro buddho lokavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the great hero, the Buddha, best of those who know the world,
whose mind is made of the Great Vehicle, the heart and strength of the Buddhas, said:
Good, good, greatly wise <s>Mahāmati</s>; listen.
I shall explain in sequence what has been fully asked by you:
arising and non-arising, nirvāṇa, the characteristic of emptiness,
transition, absence of own-nature, Buddhas, pāramitās, sons of the Sugata,
hearers, sons of the Jina, and outsiders who dwell in the formless realms,
<s>Meru</s>, oceans, mountains, continents, fields, and the earth,
stars, the sun, the moon, outsiders, gods, and asuras,
liberations, masteries, superknowledges, powers, meditations, and samādhis,

children.text: nirodhā ṛddhipādāśca bodhyaṅgā mārga eva ca
children.translated_text: cessations, bases of miraculous power, factors of awakening, and the path,
the meditations, the immeasurables, the aggregates, and comings and goings,
attainment, cessations, emergence, and the teaching of mind.
Mind, manas, consciousness, selflessness, and the five dharmas:

children.text: svabhāvaḥ kalpanā kalpyaṃ dṛśyaṃ dṛṣṭidvayaṃ katham
children.translated_text: own-being, imagination, what is imagined, the visible object, and the twofold view: how are these?
The forms of the vehicles and the lineages, and those born from gold, jewels, and pearls:
the <s>icchantikas</s>, the great elements, bees, and the one Buddhahood:

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyo gamaṃ prāptiḥ sattvānāṃ ca bhavābhavam ||
children.translated_text: knowledge, the knowable, going, attainment, and the becoming and non-becoming of beings:

children.text: hayā gajā mṛgāḥ kena grahaṇaṃ brūhi me katham
children.translated_text: horses, elephants, and deer: by what are they? Tell me, how is grasping?
How is the established doctrine, joined with examples and reasons, the teaching?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ kena nānābhrāntistathā nayam
children.translated_text: By what are effect and cause, and thus the various delusions and the method?

children.text: cittamātraṃ na dṛśyo'sti bhūmīnāṃ nāsti vai kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is mind-only, no visible object; indeed there is no sequence of stages:
By what do you speak to me of a hundred transformations free from appearance?
Medicine, the crafts, and likewise the tradition of arts and sciences:

children.text: acalānāṃ tathā meroḥ pramāṇaṃ hi kṣiteḥ katham
children.translated_text: how, indeed, is the measure of the immovable things, of <s>Meru</s>, and of the earth?
Tell me, how is the measure of the ocean, the moon, and the sun?
How many atoms are there in the body of a being, whether inferior, superior, or middling?

children.text: kṣetre kṣetre rajāḥ kṛtto dhanvo dhanve bhavetkati ||
children.translated_text: In each field how many atoms are cut up? How many are there from bow to bow?
In a hand, a bow-length, a step, a krośa, a yojana, and half a yojana?

children.text: śaśavātāyanaṃ likṣā eḍakaṃ hi yavāḥ kati ||
children.translated_text: How many barley grains are there in a hare's window, a nit, and a sheep-louse?

children.text: prasthe hi syādyavāḥ kyantaḥ prasthārdhe ca yavāḥ kati
children.translated_text: How many barley grains are there in a prastha, and how many in half a prastha?

children.text: droṇe khāryāṃ tathā lakṣāḥ koṭyo vai bimbarāḥ kati ||
children.translated_text: In a droṇa and a khārī, and how many lakṣas, koṭis, and bimbaras?

children.text: sarṣape hyaṇavaḥ kyanto rakṣikā sarṣapāḥ kati
children.translated_text: How many atoms are there in a mustard seed, and how many mustard seeds in a rakṣikā?
How many rakṣikās make a māṣa? How many māṣas make a dharaṇa?

children.text: karṣo hi dharaṇāḥ kyantaḥ palaṃ vai kati kārṣikā
children.translated_text: How many dharaṇas make a karṣa? How many karṣas make a pala?
By this characterization of mass, how many palas would <s>Meru</s> be?

children.text: evaṃ hi pṛccha māṃ putra anyathā kiṃ nu pṛcchasi ||
children.translated_text: Ask me in this way, my son; why, then, do you ask otherwise?
Of the pratyekabuddhas, the śrāvakas, the Buddhas, and the sons of the Jina,

children.text: katyaṇuko bhavetkāyaḥ kiṃ nu eva na pṛcchasi ||
children.translated_text: how many atoms would the body be? Why do you not ask just this?

children.text: vahneḥ śikhā katyaṇukā pavane hyaṇavaḥ kati
children.translated_text: How many atoms are in a flame of fire? How many atoms are in the wind?

children.text: indriye indriye kyanto romakūpe bhruvoḥ kati ||
children.translated_text: How many are there in each sense faculty, and how many in a pore and in the eyebrows?
By what are men lords of wealth, and kings, and wheel-turning monarchs?

children.text: rājyaṃ ca taiḥ kathaṃ rakṣyaṃ mokṣaścaiṣāṃ kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: How is their kingdom to be protected, and how can their liberation come about?

children.text: gadyaṃ padyaṃ kathaṃ brūṣe maithunaṃ lokaviśrutā
children.translated_text: How do you speak prose and verse? How is sexual union known in the world?
How is the variety of food and drink, and how are men, women, and forests?

children.text: vajrasaṃhananāḥ kena hyacalā brūhi me katham
children.translated_text: By what are the adamantine bodies? Tell me, how are the immovable mountains?
By what are they like illusion and dream? How are they comparable to a mirage?

children.text: ghanānāṃ saṃbhavaḥ kutra ṛtūnāṃ ca kuto bhavet
children.translated_text: Where is the arising of clouds, and from where do the seasons come?
Whence is the savoriness of flavors? Why are there female, male, and neuter?

children.text: śobhāśca jinaputrāśca kutra me pṛccha māṃ suta
children.translated_text: Where are beauties and sons of the Jina? Ask me, my son.
How, indeed, are the divine immovable mountains adorned with sages and gandharvas?

children.text: muktasya gamanaṃ kutra baddhaḥ kaḥ kena mucyate
children.translated_text: Where is the going of one who is liberated? Who is bound, and by what is he released?
What is that object-domain of meditators, and what are emanation and the holy places?
By what is there no action of nonbeing and being? How does the visible object cease?

children.text: kathaṃ hi śudhyate tarkaḥ kena tarkaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: How, indeed, is reasoning purified? By what does reasoning proceed?

children.text: kriyā pravartate kena gamanaṃ brūhi me katham
children.translated_text: By what does action proceed? Tell me, how is going?
By what is the cutting off of perception, and by what is samādhi so called?

children.text: vidārya tribhavaṃ ko'sau kiṃ sthānaṃ kā tanurbhavet
children.translated_text: Who is it that splits open the three worlds? What is the place, and what body would there be?
By what is there talk whose nature is unreal? How is teaching given by convention?

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ pṛcchase kena nairātmyaṃ pṛcchase katham
children.translated_text: By what do you ask about the mark? How do you ask about selflessness?

children.text: garbhā naiyāyikāḥ kena pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By what are embryos and logicians? You ask me, sons of the Jina.
By what are the views of eternalism and annihilationism, and how is the mind brought into samādhi?
Expression, likewise knowledge, moral discipline, and lineage, O sons of the Jina:
proper explanation, teacher and pupil, and the diversity of beings: how are these?
Food and drink, the sky, clouds, <s>Māras</s>, and what is mere designation:

children.text: taruvallyaḥ kathaṃ kena pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasa
children.translated_text: trees and creepers: by what are they? You ask me, son of the Jina.
By what is the diversity of fields, and likewise the sage of long austerity?

children.text: vaṃśaḥ kaste guruḥ kena pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasa
children.translated_text: What is your lineage, and by what is there a teacher? You ask me, son of the Jina.

children.text: uhoḍimā narā yoge kāmadhātau na budhyase ||
children.translated_text: Men intent on yoga in the desire realm do not awaken.

children.text: siddhānto hyakaniṣṭheṣu yuktiṃ pṛcchasi me katham
children.translated_text: How do you ask me about the doctrine and reasoning among the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s>?

children.text: abhijñāṃ laukikāṃ kena kathaṃ bhikṣutvameva ca ||
children.translated_text: By what is worldly superknowledge, and how indeed is monkhood?

children.text: nairmāṇikān vipākasthān buddhān pṛcchasi me katham
children.translated_text: How do you ask me about magically created Buddhas and Buddhas established as fruition?
And how are the Buddhas of the knowledge of suchness, and the Saṅghas?
Buddha-fields shining like vīṇās, drums, and flowers, devoid of worlds:

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasa
children.translated_text: mind, indeed, and the seven stages: you ask me, son of the Jina.

children.text: etāṃścānyāṃśca subahūn praśnān pṛcchasi māṃ suta ||
children.translated_text: These and many other questions you ask me, my son.
Each one is furnished with its own characteristics and free from the faults of views.

children.text: siddhāntaṃ deśanāṃ vakṣye sahasā tvaṃ śṛṇohi me ||
children.translated_text: I shall teach the established doctrine and the teaching; listen to me at once.

children.text: upanyāsaṃ kariṣyāmi padānāṃ śṛṇu me suta
children.translated_text: I shall make an exposition of the terms; listen to me, my son:
the hundred and eight terms, as they have been described by the Buddhas.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatir bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocatkatamadbhagavan aṣṭottarapadaśatam bhagavānāha utpādapadam anutpādapadam nityapadamanityapadam lakṣaṇapadam alakṣaṇapadam sthityanyathātvapadam asthityanyathātvapadaṃ kṣaṇikapadam akṣaṇikapadaṃ svabhāvapadam asvabhāvapadam śūnyatāpadam aśūnyatāpadam ucchedapadam anucchedapadaṃ cittapadam acittapadam madhyamapadam amadhyamapadaṃ śāśvatapadam aśāśvatapadam pratyayapadam apratyayapadam hetupadamahetupadam kleśapadam akleśapadam tṛṣṇāpadam atṛṣṇāpadam upāyapadam anupāyapadam kauśalyapadam akauśalyapadam śuddhipadam aśuddhipadam yuktipadam ayuktipadam dṛṣṭāntapadam adṛṣṭāntapadam śiṣyapadam aśiṣyapadam gurupadam agurupadam gotrapadam agotrapadam yānatrayapadam ayānatrayapadam children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the one hundred and eightfold set of terms?" The Blessed One said: "The term arising and the term non-arising; the term permanent and the term impermanent; the term mark and the term absence of mark; the term remaining otherwise and the term not remaining otherwise; the term momentary and the term non-momentary; the term own-nature and the term absence of own-nature; the term emptiness and the term non-emptiness; the term annihilation and the term non-annihilation; the term mind and the term no-mind; the term middle and the term non-middle; the term eternal and the term non-eternal; the term condition and the term non-condition; the term cause and the term non-cause; the term affliction and the term non-affliction; the term craving and the term non-craving; the term means and the term non-means; the term skillfulness and the term non-skillfulness; the term purity and the term impurity; the term reasoning and the term non-reasoning; the term example and the term non-example; the term disciple and the term non-disciple; the term teacher and the term non-teacher; the term lineage and the term non-lineage; the term three vehicles and the term no three vehicles; the term non-appearance and the term appearance; the term vow and the term non-vow; the term threefold circle and the term non-threefold circle; the term sign and the term signless; the term side of existence and nonexistence and the term not the side of existence and nonexistence; the term both and the term not both; the term noble knowledge personally realized within oneself and the term not noble knowledge personally realized within oneself; the term happiness in the present life and the term not happiness in the present life; the term field and the term non-field; the term atom and the term non-atom; the term water and the term non-water; the term wilderness and the term non-wilderness; the term element and the term non-element; the term number and calculation and the term non-number and non-calculation; the term superknowledge and the term non-superknowledge; the term weariness and the term non-weariness; the term solid mass and the term non-solid mass; the term crafts, arts, and sciences and the term not crafts, arts, and sciences; the term wind and the term non-wind; the term stage and the term non-stage; the term thinkable and the term unthinkable; the term designation and the term non-designation; the term own-nature and the term absence of own-nature; the term aggregates and the term non-aggregates; the term being and the term non-being; the term intellect and the term non-intellect; the term nirvāṇa and the term non-nirvāṇa; the term knowable and the term unknowable; the term outsider and the term non-outsider; the term clamor and the term non-clamor; the term illusion and the term non-illusion; the term dream and the term non-dream; the term mirage and the term non-mirage; the term image and the term non-image; the term wheel and the term non-wheel; the term <s>gandharva</s> and the term non-<s>gandharva</s>; the term god and the term non-god; the term food and drink and the term non-food and non-drink; the term sexual union and the term non-sexual union; the term seen and the term unseen; the term perfection and the term non-perfection; the term morality and the term non-morality; the term moon, sun, and stars and the term not moon, sun, and stars; the term truth and the term untruth; the term fruit and the term non-fruit; the term cessation and the term non-cessation; the term emergence from cessation and the term non-emergence from cessation; the term healing and the term non-healing; the term mark and the term absence of mark; the term limb and the term non-limb; the term arts and sciences and the term not arts and sciences; the term meditation and the term non-meditation; the term error and the term non-error; the term visible object and the term non-visible object; the term to be protected and the term not to be protected; the term lineage and the term non-lineage; the term seer and the term non-seer; the term kingdom and the term non-kingdom; the term grasping and the term non-grasping; the term jewel and the term non-jewel; the term prediction and the term non-prediction; the term <s>icchantika</s> and the term non-<s>icchantika</s>; the term female, male, and neuter and the term not female, male, and neuter; the term taste and the term non-taste; the term action and the term non-action; the term body and the term non-body; the term logic and the term non-logic; the term moving and the term unmoving; the term faculty and the term non-faculty; the term conditioned and the term unconditioned; the term cause and effect and the term not cause and effect; the term lowest and the term non-lowest; the term season and the term non-season; the term trees, shrubs, creepers, and bowers and the term not trees, shrubs, creepers, and bowers; the term variety and the term non-variety; the term entry into instruction and the term non-entry into instruction; the term discipline and the term non-discipline; the term monk and the term non-monk; the term empowerment and the term non-empowerment; the term syllable and the term non-syllable."
"This, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the one hundred and eightfold set of terms, described by the former Buddhas."

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat katividho bhagavan vijñānānāmutpādasthitinirodho bhavati bhagavānāha dvividho mahāmate vijñānānām utpattisthitinirodho bhavati na ca tārkikā avabudhyante yaduta prabandhanirodho lakṣaṇanirodhaśca
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, of how many kinds is the arising, abiding, and cessation of consciousnesses?" The Blessed One said: "<s>Mahāmati</s>, the arising, abiding, and cessation of consciousnesses is twofold, and the logicians do not understand it, namely cessation as continuity and cessation as characteristic."
"The arising of consciousnesses is twofold: arising as continuity and arising as characteristic."
"Abiding is twofold: abiding as continuity and abiding as characteristic."

children.text: trividhaṃ vijñānaṃ pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ karmalakṣaṇaṃ jātilakṣaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: "Consciousness is threefold: characterized by activity, characterized by action, and characterized by birth."

children.text: dvividhaṃ mahāmate vijñānaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa aṣṭalakṣaṇoktaṃ khyātivijñānaṃ vastuprativikalpavijñānaṃ ca
children.translated_text: In brief, <s>Mahāmate</s>, consciousness is twofold, though spoken of as having eight characteristics: appearance-consciousness and object-discriminating consciousness.

children.text: yathā mahāmate darpaṇasya rūpagrahaṇam evaṃ khyātivijñānasyākhyāsyati
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a mirror apprehends forms, so appearance-consciousness will be explained.
And, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there is appearance-consciousness and object-discriminating consciousness.
Both of these have undivided characteristics and are causes for one another.
Among these, appearance-consciousness, <s>Mahāmate</s>, has as its cause the transformation of inconceivable latent impressions.

children.text: vastuprativikalpavijñānaṃ ca mahāmate viṣayavikalpahetukam anādikālaprapañcavāsanāhetukaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And object-discriminating consciousness, <s>Mahāmate</s>, has as its cause discrimination with regard to objects, and also has as its cause the latent impressions of conceptual proliferation from beginningless time.

children.text: tatra sarvendriyavijñānanirodho mahāmate yaduta ālayavijñānasya abhūtaparikalpavāsanāvaicitryanirodhaḥ
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the cessation of all sense-consciousnesses is the cessation of the manifold latent impressions of false imagination in the <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness).
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the cessation of characteristics.
But as for the cessation of the continuum, <s>Mahāmate</s>, from what does it proceed?
From what, <s>Mahāmate</s>? From its support and from its objective basis.

children.text: tatra yadāśrayam anādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanā yadālambanaṃ svacittadṛśyavijñānaviṣaye vikalpāḥ
children.translated_text: There the support is the latent impression of the coarseness of conceptual proliferation from beginningless time; the objective basis is the discriminations in the domain of consciousness, which is what is seen by one's own mind.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate mṛtparamāṇubhyo mṛtpiṇḍaḥ na cānyo nānanyaḥ tathā suvarṇaṃ bhūṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a lump of clay is made from atoms of clay, yet it is neither different nor non-different from them; so too gold in relation to an ornament.

children.text: yadi ca mahāmate mṛtpiṇḍo mṛtparamāṇubhyo'nyaḥ syāt tairnārabdhaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: If, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the lump of clay were different from the atoms of clay, it would not have been produced by them.
But it has been produced by those atoms of clay; therefore it is not different.

children.text: athānanyaḥ syāt mṛtpiṇḍaparamāṇvoḥ pratibhāgo na syāt
children.translated_text: Yet if it were non-different, there would be no distinction between the lump of clay and the atoms.

children.text: evameva mahāmate pravṛttivijñānānyālayavijñānajātilakṣaṇād anyāni syuḥ anālayavijñānahetukāni syuḥ
children.translated_text: In just the same way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, if the active consciousnesses were different from the class-characteristic of <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s>, they would not have <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> as their cause.

children.text: athānanyāni pravṛttivijñānanirodhe ālayavijñānavirodhaḥ syāt sa ca na bhavati svajātilakṣaṇanirodhaḥ
children.translated_text: But if the active consciousnesses were non-different, then when the active consciousnesses ceased, there would be opposition to, or cessation of, <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s>; and that does not occur as the cessation of its own class-characteristic.

children.text: tasmānmahāmate na svajātilakṣaṇanirodho vijñānānāṃ kiṃ tu karmalakṣaṇanirodhaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, it is not the own class-characteristic of the consciousnesses that ceases, but rather the characteristic of their activity.
If the own class-characteristic were to cease, there would be the cessation of <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s>.

children.text: ālayavijñāne punarnirudhyamāne nirviśiṣṭastīrthakarocchedavāde nāyaṃ vādaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: And if <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> were to cease, this doctrine would be no different from the annihilationist doctrine of the non-Buddhist teachers.

children.text: tīrthakarāṇāṃ mahāmate ayaṃ vādo yaduta viṣayagrahaṇoparamād vijñānaprabandhoparamo bhavati
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the doctrine of the non-Buddhist teachers: that from the cessation of grasping objects there is the cessation of the continuum of consciousness.
From the cessation of the continuum of consciousness, there would be the cutting off of the beginningless continuum.
And, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the non-Buddhist teachers describe the continuation of the continuum as arising from a cause.

children.text: na cakṣurvijñānasya rūpālokasamudayata utpattiṃ varṇayanti anyatra kāraṇataḥ
children.translated_text: They do not describe the arising of eye-consciousness as coming from the conjunction of form and light, except as coming from a cause.
And the cause, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is what is taught in doctrines of primordial matter, person, Lord, time, and atoms.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate saptavidho bhāvasvabhāvo bhavati yaduta samudayasvabhāvo bhāvasvabhāvo lakṣaṇasvabhāvo mahābhūtasvabhāvo hetusvabhāvaḥ pratyayasvabhāvo niṣpattisvabhāvaśca saptamaḥ
