children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there is a sevenfold nature of entities, namely: the nature of arising, the nature of entity, the nature of characteristic, the nature of the great elements, the nature of cause, the nature of condition, and, as the seventh, the nature of accomplishment.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate saptavidhaḥ paramārtho yaduta cittagocaro jñānagocaraḥ prajñāgocaro dṛṣṭidvayagocaro dṛṣṭidvayātikrāntagocaraḥ sutabhūmyanukramaṇagocaras tathāgatasya pratyātmagatigocaraḥ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, ultimate truth is sevenfold, namely: the domain of mind, the domain of knowledge, the domain of wisdom, the domain of the two views, the domain that transcends the two views, the domain of the successive stages of the sons, and the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s own realization.

children.text: etanmahāmate atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bhāvasvabhāvaparamārthahṛdayaṃ yena samanvāgatāstathāgatā laukikalokottaratamān dharmānāryeṇa prajñācakṣuṣā svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitān vyavasthāpayanti
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the heart of the nature of entities and of ultimate truth for the past, future, and present <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened Buddhas. Endowed with it, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by the noble eye of wisdom, establish the worldly and supremely supramundane dharmas as falling under their own and shared characteristics.

children.text: tathā ca vyavasthāpayanti yathā tīrthakaravādakudṛṣṭisādhāraṇā na bhavanti
children.translated_text: And they establish them in such a way that they are not held in common with the bad views taught by the non-Buddhist teachers.

children.text: kathaṃ ca mahāmate tīrthakaravādakudṛṣṭisādhāraṇā bhavanti yaduta svacittaviṣayavikalpadṛṣṭyanavabodhanadvijñānānām
children.translated_text: How, then, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are they held in common with the bad views taught by the non-Buddhist teachers? It is because of not understanding the view that the object-domain of one's own mind is a discrimination of the two consciousnesses.

Because they do not enter into the fact that what is seen is only one's own mind, <s>Mahāmate</s>, foolish ordinary people become proponents of the two views concerning being and nonbeing, nature and ultimate truth.

Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, I shall teach the turning away from the suffering of the three realms of discriminative existence, the turning away from the conditions of ignorance, craving, and karma, and the seeing of the illusory objects that are seen by one's own mind.

children.text: ye kecinmahāmate śramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā abhūtvā śraddhāhetuphalābhivyaktidravyaṃ ca kālāvasthitaṃ pratyayeṣu ca skandhadhātvāyatanānām utpādasthitiṃ cecchanti bhūtvā ca vyayam te mahāmate saṃtatikriyotpādabhaṅgabhavanirvāṇamārgakarmaphalasatyavināśocchedavādino bhavanti
children.translated_text: Whatever ascetics or brahmins, <s>Mahāmate</s>, wish for a substance which was previously nonexistent and later manifests as faith, cause, and result, and which remains in time, and wish for the arising and abiding of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases among conditions, and then for their destruction after having come to be: these, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are annihilationists who destroy continuity, activity, arising, breaking apart, existence, nirvāṇa, the path, karma, result, and truth.
For what reason? Because this is not directly perceived, and because there is no seeing of a beginning.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate ghaṭakapālābhāvo ghaṭakṛtyaṃ na karoti nāpi dagdhabījamaṅkurakṛtyaṃ karoti evameva mahāmate ye skandhadhātvāyatanabhāvā niruddhā nirudhyante nirotsyante svacittadṛśyavikalpadarśanāhetutvānnāsti nairantaryapravṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the absence of a potsherd does not perform the function of a pot, nor does a burned seed perform the function of a sprout. In the same way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, because the entities that are aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, which have ceased, are ceasing, and will cease, are not causes for seeing discriminations of what is seen by one's own mind, there is no uninterrupted continuation.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate abhūtvā śraddhāvijñānānāṃ trisaṃgatipratyayakriyāyogenotpattirabhaviṣyat asatāmapi mahāmate kūrmaromnāmutpattirabhaviṣyat sikatābhyo vā tailasya
children.translated_text: But if, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the arising of faith and cognitions, though previously nonexistent, were to occur through the conjunction of three conditions and causal activity, then, <s>Mahāmati</s>, even nonexistent hairs on a tortoise would arise, or oil from grains of sand.

children.text: pratijñāhānir niyamanirodhaśca mahāmate prasajyate kriyākarmakaraṇavaiyarthyaṃ ca sadasato bruvataḥ
children.translated_text: For one who asserts being and nonbeing, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there follows the abandonment of the thesis, the cessation of regular order, and the uselessness of activity, action, and instruments.

children.text: teṣāmapi mahāmate trisaṃgatipratyayakriyāyogenopadeśo vidyate hetuphalasvalakṣaṇatayā atītānāgatapratyutpannāsatsallakṣaṇāstitāṃ yuktyāgamaistarkabhūmau vartamānāḥ svadṛṣṭidoṣavāsanatayā nirdekṣyanti
children.translated_text: For them too, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is an instruction through the conjunction of three conditions and causal activity, in terms of the intrinsic marks of cause and result; operating on the ground of logic, with reasoning and scripture, they will point out the existence of the marks of nonexistent and existent things in past, future, and present, because of the habitual impressions of the faults of their own views.

children.text: evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭidaṣṭā viṣamamatayo'jñaiḥ praṇītaṃ sarvapraṇītamiti vakṣyanti
children.translated_text: Just so, <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary people, bitten by false views and of distorted understanding, will say, 'Whatever has been taught by the ignorant is the whole of what has been taught.'

children.text: ye punaranye mahāmate śramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā niḥsvabhāvaghanālātacakragandharvanagarānutpādamāyāmarīcyudakacandrasvapnasvabhāvabāhyacittadṛśyavikalpānādikālaprapañcadarśanena svacittavikalpapratyayavinivṛttirahitāḥ parikalpitābhidhānalakṣyalakṣaṇābhidheyarahitā dehabhogapratiṣṭhāsamālayavijñānaviṣayagrāhyagrāhakavisaṃyuktaṃ nirābhāsagocaramutpādasthitibhaṅgavarjyaṃ svacittotpādānugataṃ vibhāvayiṣyanti nacirātte mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ saṃsāranirvāṇasamatāprāptā bhaviṣyanti
children.translated_text: But other ascetics or brahmins, <s>Mahāmati</s>, who, through seeing from beginningless time the proliferation of imagined external objects seen by mind, whose nature is without self-nature, like a mass, a firebrand-circle, a city of gandharvas, non-arising, illusion, a mirage, water-moon, or dream, are free from the conditions of their own mental construction; who are free from the imagined designation, object, mark, and thing designated; who are disconnected from body, enjoyment, establishment, and the object-spheres of storehouse consciousness, grasper, and grasped; who contemplate the object-domain without appearance, devoid of arising, duration, and destruction, and following the arising of their own mind: before long, <s>Mahāmati</s>, those bodhisattvas, great beings, will attain the equality of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa.

children.text: mahākaruṇopāyakauśalyānābhogagatena mahāmate prayogena sarvasattvamāyāpratibimbasamatayā anārabdhapratyayatayā adhyātmabāhyaviṣayavimuktatayā cittabāhyādarśanatayā animittādhiṣṭhānānugatā anupūrveṇa bhūmikramasamādhiviṣayānugamanatayā traidhātukasvacittatayā adhimuktitaḥ prativibhāvayamānā māyopamasamādhiṃ pratilabhante
children.translated_text: By a practice, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that has entered effortless great compassion and skillful means, through the equality of all beings with magical reflections, through the fact that conditions are not initiated, through freedom from internal and external objects, through not seeing anything external to mind, they follow the basis of signlessness; gradually, by following the object-spheres of the successive stages and samādhis, and by understanding the three realms as their own mind, they obtain the illusion-like samādhi.

children.text: svacittanirābhāsamātrāvatāreṇa prajñāpāramitāvihārānuprāptā utpādakriyāyogavirahitāḥ samādhivajrabimbopamaṃ tathāgatakāyānugataṃ tathatānirmāṇānugataṃ balābhijñāvaśitākṛpākaruṇopāyamaṇḍitaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetratīrthyāyatanopagataṃ cittamanomanovijñānarahitaṃ parāvṛttyānuśrayānupūrvakaṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ mahāmate te bodhisattvāḥ pratilapsyante
children.translated_text: By entering mere nonappearance of their own mind, having attained the abiding in the perfection of wisdom, free from the conjunction of production and activity, those bodhisattvas, <s>Mahāmati</s>, will obtain the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>: like the image of vajra in samādhi, following the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, following the construction of suchness, adorned with powers, superknowledges, masteries, pity, compassion, and skillful means, present in all Buddha-fields and abodes of non-Buddhists, devoid of mind, mentation, and mental consciousness, and gradual by means of the support of transformation.

children.text: tasmāttarhi mahāmate bodhisattvair mahāsattvaistathāgatakāyānugamena pratilābhinā skandhadhātvāyatanacittahetupratyayakriyāyogotpādasthitibhaṅgavikalpaprapañcarahitair bhavitavyaṃ cittamātrānusāribhiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, bodhisattvas, great beings, who wish to obtain what follows from the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, should be free from conceptual proliferation about the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, mind, causes, conditions, causal activity, arising, duration, and destruction, and should follow mind-only.

children.text: anādikālāprapañcadauṣṭhulyavikalpavāsanahetukaṃ tribhavaṃ paśyato nirābhāsabuddhabhūmyanutpādasmaraṇatayā pratyātmāryadharmagatiṃ gataḥ svacittavaśavartī anābhogacaryāgatiṃgato viśvarūpamaṇisadṛśaḥ sūkṣmaiḥ sattvacittānupraveśakair nirmāṇavigrahaiś cittamātrāvadhāraṇatayā bhūmikramānusaṃdhau pratiṣṭhāpayati
children.translated_text: When he sees the threefold existence as caused by the habitual impressions of beginningless proliferation, coarseness, and construction, and by recollecting non-arising on the Buddha-stage without appearance, he has reached the course of the noble dharma realized personally; having mastery over his own mind and having reached the course of effortless conduct, like a jewel of manifold forms, by means of emanated bodies that subtly enter the minds of beings, he establishes them in the continuity of the stages through the ascertainment of mind-only.

children.text: tasmāttarhi mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena svasiddhāntakuśalena punarapi mahāmatirāha deśayatu me bhagavān cittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇakusumadharmaparyāyaṃ buddhabodhisattvānuyātaṃ svacittadṛśyagocaravisaṃyojanaṃ sarvabhāṣyayuktitattvalakṣaṇavidāraṇaṃ sarvabuddhapravacanahṛdayaṃ laṅkāpurigirimalaye nivāsino bodhisattvān ārabhyodadhitaraṃgālayavijñānagocaraṃ dharmakāyaṃ tathāgatānugītaṃ prabhāṣasva
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, a bodhisattva, a great being, should be skilled in his own doctrine. Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'Blessed One, please teach me the flower-like discourse of dharma on mind, mentation, mental consciousness, the five dharmas, and the marks of self-nature, followed by Buddhas and bodhisattvas, which disconnects one from the object-domain seen by one's own mind, breaks open the true marks of all explanations and reasonings, and is the heart of all the teachings of the Buddhas. For the bodhisattvas dwelling on <s>Mount Malaya</s> in the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, proclaim the dharmakāya, the object-domain of the storehouse consciousness like ocean-waves, praised by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat caturbhirmahāmate kāraṇaiścakṣurvijñānaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again said this to the bodhisattva, the great being <s>Mahāmati</s>: 'By four causes, <s>Mahāmati</s>, eye-consciousness comes into operation.'

'By what four? Namely, through not understanding the grasping of what is seen by one's own mind; through attachment to the habitual impressions of forms and beginningless proliferating coarseness; through the own-nature of the nature of consciousness; and through curiosity about the varied marks of form.'

children.text: ebhirmahāmate caturbhiḥ kāraṇairoghāntarajalasthānīyād ālayavijñānāt pravṛttivijñānataraṃga utpadyate
children.translated_text: 'By these four causes, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the wave of active consciousness arises from the storehouse consciousness, which is like the water in a flood.'

children.text: yathā mahāmate cakṣurvijñāne evaṃ sarvendriyaparamāṇuromakūpeṣu yugapatpravṛttikramaviṣayādarśabimbadarśanavat udadheḥ pavanāhatā iva mahāmate viṣayapavanacittodadhitaraṃgā avyucchinnahetukriyālakṣaṇā anyonyavinirmuktāḥ karmajātilakṣaṇasuvinibaddharūpasvabhāvānavadhāriṇo mahāmate pañca vijñānakāyāḥ pravartante
children.translated_text: 'As with eye-consciousness, <s>Mahāmati</s>, so in all sense faculties, atoms, and pores, whether simultaneous or successive, like seeing images in a mirror, the waves of the ocean of mind, struck by the wind of objects, <s>Mahāmati</s>, proceed as the five groups of consciousness, with the marks of uninterrupted causal activity, not separate from one another, and not determining their own nature as forms well bound by the marks of karma and birth.'

children.text: saha taireva mahāmate pañcabhirvijñānakāyair hetuviṣayaparicchedalakṣaṇāvadhārakaṃ nāma manovijñānaṃ taddhetujaśarīraṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: 'Together with those very five groups of consciousness, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there comes into operation what is called mental consciousness, which determines the marks that delimit causes and objects, and has a body born from those causes.'

children.text: na ca teṣāṃ tasya caivaṃ bhavati vayamatrānyonyahetukāḥ svacittadṛśyavikalpābhiniveśapravṛttā iti
children.translated_text: And neither they nor it think in this way: "Here we are mutually causal, proceeding through attachment to discriminations of what is seen by one's own mind."
And yet, furnished with characteristics that are not separate from one another, they proceed in the delimitation of the object of representation.

children.text: tathā ca pravartamānāḥ pravartante yathā samāpannasyāpi yoginaḥ sūkṣmagativāsanāpravṛttā na prajñāyante
children.translated_text: And proceeding in that way, they proceed just as, even for a yogin who has entered attainment, the subtle activity of latent tendencies is not perceived.

children.text: yoginā caivaṃ bhavati nirodhya vijñānāni samāpatsyāmahe iti
children.translated_text: And the yogin thinks in this way: "Having stopped the consciousnesses, we shall enter attainment."

children.text: te cāniruddhaireva vijñānaiḥ samāpadyante vāsanābījānirodhādaniruddhāḥ viṣayapravṛttagrahaṇavaikalyānniruddhāḥ
children.translated_text: But they enter attainment with the consciousnesses not stopped at all: they are not stopped because the seeds of latent tendencies have not been stopped; they are stopped because of the absence of apprehension engaged with objects.

children.text: evaṃ sūkṣmo mahāmate ālayavijñānagatipracāro yattathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā bhūmipratiṣṭhitāṃśca bodhisattvān na sukaramanyaiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyayogayogibhir adhigantuṃ samādhiprajñābalādhānato'pi vā paricchettum
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the movement and activity of <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) is subtle; apart from the <s>Tathāgata</s> and bodhisattvas established on the stages, it is not easy for other yogins practicing the yogas of disciples, solitary buddhas, or non-Buddhists to understand it, or to distinguish it even through the application of the power of concentration and wisdom.

children.text: anyatra bhūmilakṣaṇaprajñājñānakauśalapadaprabhedaviniścayajinānantakuśalamūlopacayasvacittadṛśyavikalpaprapañcavirahitair vanagahanaguhālayāntargatair mahāmate hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamayogayogibhirna śakyaṃ svacittavikalpadṛśyadhārādraṣṭranantakṣetrajinābhiṣekavaśitābalābhijñāsamādhayaḥ prāptum
children.translated_text: Except through skill in the knowledge of the characteristics of the stages, through decisive understanding of the divisions of the terms, through the accumulation of infinite roots of goodness before the Jina, and through freedom from the conceptual proliferation of discriminations of what is seen by one's own mind, <s>Mahāmati</s>, yogins of inferior, superior, and middling practice dwelling within forest thickets, caves, and retreats cannot attain the concentrations, masteries, powers, and superknowledges that behold the stream of what is seen as the discrimination of one's own mind and the consecrations by the Jinas in endless fields.

But when they are accompanied by good friends and by the Jinas, <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is possible to cross the ocean of becoming in saṃsāra, whose nature is the domain of the discrimination of what is seen by one's own mind as mind, mentation, and consciousness, and whose causes are karma, craving, and ignorance.

children.text: ata etasmāt kāraṇānmahāmate yoginā kalyāṇamitrajinayoge yogaḥ prārabdhavyaḥ
children.translated_text: For this reason, <s>Mahāmati</s>, a yogin should begin the practice in union with good friends and the Jinas.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:
Just as the waves of the ocean, stirred by the condition of wind,
proceed dancing, and there is no interruption,
so too the flood of the <s>ālaya</s> always, stirred by the wind of objects,
proceeds dancing with the various waves of consciousness.

children.text: nīle rakte'tha lavaṇe śaṅkhe kṣīre ca śārkare
children.translated_text: In blue, red, salt, conch-shell, milk, and sugar,
and with astringent substances, fruits, flowers, and the like, as rays are in the sun,

children.text: na cānyena ca nānanyena taraṃgā hyudadhermatāḥ
children.translated_text: the waves of the ocean are held to be neither different nor non-different from another.

children.text: vijñānāni tathā sapta cittena saha saṃyutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too the seven consciousnesses are joined together with mind.
This diversity of waves is a transformation of the ocean;

children.text: ālayaṃ hi tathā citraṃ vijñānākhyaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: so too the variegated <s>ālaya</s> proceeds under the name of consciousness.
Mind, mentation, and consciousness are imagined for the sake of characteristic and meaning;

children.text: abhinnalakṣaṇā hyaṣṭau na lakṣyā na ca lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: the eight, having undivided characteristics, are neither what is marked nor the mark.
Just as there is no distinction between the ocean and the waves,

children.text: vijñānānāṃ tathā cittaiḥ pariṇāmo na labhyate ||
children.translated_text: so no transformation of the consciousnesses is obtained apart from minds.

children.text: cittena cīyate karma manasā ca vicīyate
children.translated_text: By mind karma is accumulated, and by mentation it is considered;
by consciousness one cognizes, while with the five one imagines the visible object.
For people, consciousness appears indeed in forms such as blue and red.
Tell me, <s>Mahāmati</s>, why there is similarity between waves and mind.
For forms such as blue and red are not found in waves,

children.text: vṛttiśca varṇyate cittaṃ lakṣaṇārthaṃ hi bāliśān ||
children.translated_text: and activity is described as mind for the sake of characteristic and meaning for the childish.

children.text: na tasya vidyate vṛttiḥ svacittaṃ grāhyavarjitam
children.translated_text: It has no activity; one's own mind is devoid of what is grasped.

children.text: grāhye sati hi vai grāhastaraṃgaiḥ saha sādhyate ||
children.translated_text: For when there is something grasped, grasping is indeed established together with the waves.
For people, consciousness appears as the support of body, enjoyment, and abode;
therefore its activity is seen to be similar to that of waves.
The ocean is conceived as dancing in the form of waves;

children.text: ālayasya tathā vṛttiḥ kasmādbuddhyā na gamyate ||
children.translated_text: why is the activity of the <s>ālaya</s> not understood by the intellect in the same way?
Because of the deficiency of the childish in understanding, the <s>ālaya</s>, like the ocean,
is introduced by an example through its similarity to the activity of waves.
Just as the sun rises upon the Jina, whether equal, inferior, or superior,

children.text: tathā tvaṃ lokapradyota tattvaṃ deśesi bāliśān ||
children.translated_text: so you, light of the world, teach reality to the childish.
Having established a standpoint among dharmas, why do you not speak reality?

children.text: bhāṣase yadi vā tattvaṃ citte tattvaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Or if you do speak reality, reality is not found in mind.

children.text: udadheryathā taraṃgā hi darpaṇe supine yathā
children.translated_text: Just as the waves of the ocean, or as in a mirror or in a dream,
are seen at one and the same time, so mind is seen in its own domain.
Because of the deficiency of objects, it proceeds by successive activity:
one cognizes by consciousness, and then thinks by mentation.

children.text: pañcānāṃ khyāyate dṛśyaṃ kramo nāsti samāhite
children.translated_text: The visible object appears to the five; there is no sequence for one who is concentrated.
Just as some master painter, or even a pupil painter,
would apply colors for the sake of a picture, so indeed do I teach.

children.text: raṅge na vidyate citraṃ na bhūmau na ca bhājane
children.translated_text: The picture is not found in the color, nor on the ground, nor in the vessel;
for the sake of attracting beings, a picture is imagined by means of colors.
Teaching is provisional, while reality is indeed free from syllables.
Having established a standpoint among dharmas, I teach reality to yogins.
Reality is to be reached personally within oneself and is free from the imagined and the imagining.
I teach it to the sons of the Jina; this teaching is not for the childish.

children.text: vicitrā hi yathā māyā dṛśyate na ca vidyate
children.translated_text: Just as a variegated illusion is seen and yet does not exist,
so too the varied teaching is taught as unerring.
For what is teaching for one person is not teaching for another.
Just as a physician gives medicine to each sick person,

children.text: buddhā hi tadvatsattvānāṃ cittamātraṃ vadanti vai ||
children.translated_text: For the Buddhas indeed declare, in just that way, that for beings there is only mind.
It is not an object for logicians, nor indeed for śrāvakas,
that which the Lords teach as the domain of realization within oneself.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena svacittadṛśyagrāhyagrāhakavikalpagocaraṃ parijñātukāmena saṃgaṇikāsaṃsargamiddhanivaraṇavigatena bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a bodhisattva who wishes to know that the grasped object and grasping subject which appear as his own mind are the domain of discrimination must be free from social company, association, sleepiness, and hindrance.
He must be devoted to the practice of wakefulness in the first, middle, and last parts of the night.
And he must be free from treatises and stories of wrong-path teachers, and from the characteristics of the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
The bodhisattva great being must have entered into the course of the characteristics of discrimination of what appears as his own mind.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena cittavijñānaprajñālakṣaṇavyavasthāyāṃ sthitvā upariṣṭādāryajñānalakṣaṇatrayayogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, after the bodhisattva great being has stood in the determination of the characteristics of mind, consciousness, wisdom, and knowledge, he should then undertake the discipline of the three characteristics of noble knowledge.

children.text: tatropariṣṭādāryajñānalakṣaṇatrayaṃ mahāmate katamat yaduta nirābhāsalakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhasvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇaṃ pratyātmāryajñānagatilakṣaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And there, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what are the three characteristics of noble knowledge that come next? Namely, the characteristic of non-appearance, the characteristic of the empowerment arising from all Buddhas' own vows, and the characteristic of the course of noble knowledge realized within oneself.

children.text: yānyadhigamya yogī khañjagardabha iva cittaprajñājñānalakṣaṇaṃ hitvā jinasutāṣṭamīṃ prāpya bhūmiṃ taduttare lakṣaṇatraye yogamāpadyate
children.translated_text: Having realized these, the yogin, like a lame donkey, abandons the characteristic of mind, wisdom, and knowledge, reaches the eighth stage of the sons of the Jina, and enters the discipline of the three further characteristics.
There, the characteristic of non-appearance, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from acquaintance with all the characteristics of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and tīrthikas.
The characteristic of empowerment, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from the empowerment of the former Buddhas' own vows.

children.text: pratyātmāryajñānagatilakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate sarvadharmalakṣaṇānabhiniveśato māyopamasamādhikāyapratilambhād buddhabhūmigatigamanapracārāt pravartate
children.translated_text: The characteristic of the course of noble knowledge realized within oneself, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from non-attachment to the characteristics of all dharmas, from obtaining the body of samādhi like an illusion, and from the movement and range of going to the Buddha-stage.

children.text: etanmahāmate āryāṇāṃ lakṣaṇatrayaṃ yenāryeṇa lakṣatrayeṇa samanvāgatā āryāḥ svapratyātmāryajñānagatigocaramadhigacchanti
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the threefold characteristic of the noble ones; endowed with this threefold characteristic, noble ones realize the domain of the course of noble knowledge within themselves.
Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the discipline of the three characteristics of noble knowledge should be undertaken.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punareva tasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaścittāśayavicāramājñāya āryajñānavastupravicayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhito bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchati sma deśayatu me bhagavānāryajñānavastupravicayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam aṣṭottarapadaśataprabhedāśrayam yamāśritya tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitānāṃ parikalpitasvabhāvagatiprabhedaṃ deśayanti yena parikalpitasvabhāvagatiprabhedena suprativibhāgaviddhena pudgaladharmanairātmyapracāraṃ prativiśodhya bhūmiṣu kṛtavidyāḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthakaradhyānasamādhisamāpattisukhamatikramya tathāgatācintyaviṣayapracāragatipracāraṃ pañcadharmasvabhāvagativinivṛttaṃ tathāgataṃ dharmakāyaṃ prajñājñānasunibaddhadharmaṃ māyāviṣayābhinivṛttaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetratuṣitabhavanākaniṣṭhālayopagaṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ pratilabheran
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, again knowing the thought and intention of that bodhisattva assembly, empowered by the empowerment of all Buddhas, asked the Blessed One about the dharma-discourse called the investigation of the basis of noble knowledge: "May the Blessed One teach me the dharma-discourse called the investigation of the basis of noble knowledge, resting on the distinction of one hundred and eight terms. Relying on it, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, teach bodhisattva great beings, who have fallen under particular and shared characteristics, the distinction of the course of imagined nature. When that distinction of the course of imagined nature has been well and clearly analyzed, they purify the operation of the selflessness of persons and dharmas; being accomplished in knowledge on the stages, they pass beyond the happiness of the meditations, samādhis, and attainments of all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and tīrthakaras; they obtain the <s>Tathāgata</s> dharma-body, bound together with wisdom and knowledge, moving in the inconceivable domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, turned away from the course of the five dharmas and own-natures, turned back from the sphere of illusion, and reaching all Buddha-fields, the <s>Tuṣita</s> palace, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> abode."

children.text: bhagavānāha iha mahāmate eke tīrthyātīrthyadṛṣṭayo nāstitvābhiniviṣṭā vikalpabuddhihetukṣayasvabhāvābhāvānnāsti śaśasya viṣāṇaṃ vikalpayanti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Here, <s>Mahāmate</s>, some tīrthikas, attached to non-Buddhist views, are fixed on nonexistence and, because they take the destruction of the cause of discriminating cognition as the absence of own-nature, imagine that there is no horn of a rabbit.
Just as a rabbit's horn does not exist, so, they say, all dharmas do not exist.

children.text: anye punarmahāmate bhūtaguṇāṇudravyasaṃsthānasaṃniveśaviśeṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāstiśaśaśṛṅgābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭā asti gośṛṅgamiti kalpayanti
children.translated_text: But others, <s>Mahāmate</s>, seeing the particular arrangement, configuration, and disposition of real qualities, atoms, and substances, and being attached to the fixation on the nonexistence of a rabbit's horn, imagine, 'A cow's horn exists.'
They, <s>Mahāmate</s>, have fallen into the view of the two extremes, their minds not ascertaining mind-only.
They nourish these views through discrimination of the realm of their own mind.

children.text: dehabhogapratiṣṭhāgativikalpamātre mahāmate śaśaśṛṅgaṃ nāstyastivinivṛttaṃ na kalpayettathā mahāmate sarvabhāvānāṃ nāstyastivinivṛttaṃ kalpayitavyam
children.translated_text: With regard to the mere discrimination of the course of body, enjoyment, and establishment, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one should not imagine that a rabbit's horn is free from nonexistence and existence; likewise, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one should imagine all entities as free from nonexistence and existence.

children.text: ye punarmahāmate nāstyastivinivṛttā nāsti śaśaśṛṅgaṃ na kalpayanti tairanyonyāpekṣahetutvānnāsti śaśaviṣāṇamiti na kalpayitavyam
children.translated_text: And those, <s>Mahāmate</s>, who, being free from nonexistence and existence, do not imagine 'there is no rabbit's horn,' should not imagine 'there is no rabbit's horn' on the grounds that it is a cause dependent on another.

children.text: āparamāṇupravicayād vastvanupalabdhabhāvānmahāmate āryajñānagocaravinivṛttamasti gośṛṅgamiti na kalpayitavyam
children.translated_text: Because, upon analysis down to the atom, no real object is found, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one should not imagine that a cow's horn exists apart from the domain of noble knowledge.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat nanu bhagavan vikalpasyāpravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā anumimīmahe vikalpāpravṛttyapekṣaṃ tasya nāstitvam
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, do we not infer its nonexistence, dependent on the non-arising of discrimination, after seeing that the characteristic of discrimination is non-arising?"

children.text: bhagavānāha na hi mahāmate vikalpāpravṛttyapekṣaṃ tasya nāstitvam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "No, <s>Mahāmate</s>; its nonexistence is not dependent on the non-arising of discrimination.
For what reason? Because it is the cause of the arising of that discrimination.
For, <s>Mahāmate</s>, discrimination arises in dependence on that horn as its basis."

children.text: yasmādviṣāṇāśrayapravṛtto mahāmate vikalpaḥ tasmādāśrayahetutvādanyānanyavivarjitatvānna hi tadapekṣaṃ nāstitvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇasya ||
children.translated_text: Since, <s>Mahāmate</s>, discrimination proceeds depending on a horn, therefore, because that is a supporting cause, and because it is free from being either different or non-different, the nonexistence of a hare's horn is not something dependent upon that.
But if, <s>Mahāmate</s>, discrimination were different from the hare's horn, it would have as its cause something that is not a horn.

children.text: athānanyaḥ syāt taddhetukatvād āparamāṇupravicayānupalabdher viṣāṇādananyatvāt tadabhāvaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: If it were non-different, then because it would have that as its cause, and because, when analyzed down to atoms, it is not apprehended, and because it is non-different from the horn, its absence would follow.

children.text: tadubhayabhāvābhāvātkasya kimapekṣya nāstitvaṃ bhavati atha na bhavati mahāmate apekṣya nāstitvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇasya astitvamapekṣya nāstitvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇaṃ na kalpayitavyaṃ viṣamahetutvānmahāmate nāstyastitvam siddhirna bhavati nāstyastitvavādinām
children.translated_text: Since there is neither the being nor the nonbeing of both of these, of what does nonexistence arise, and in dependence on what? Or if, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there is no dependent nonexistence of the hare's horn, one should not imagine the hare's horn as nonexistent in dependence on existence. Because the cause is unequal, <s>Mahāmate</s>, no establishment of nonexistence and existence occurs for those who propound nonexistence and existence.

children.text: anye punarmahāmate tīrthakaradṛṣṭayo rūpakāraṇasaṃsthānābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭā ākāśabhāvāparicchedakuśalā rūpamākāśabhāvavigataṃ paricchedaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikalpayanti
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, other views of the non-Buddhist teachers, fixed in attachment to the configuration that is the cause of form and unskilled in delimiting the state of space, see form as delimited apart from the state of space and conceptualize it.
And, <s>Mahāmate</s>, space itself is form.
Because it has entered into the material elements, <s>Mahāmate</s>, form itself is space.
The distinction between form and space as cause, <s>Mahāmate</s>, should be understood according to the arrangement of contained and container.

children.text: bhūtāni mahāmate pravartamānāni parasparasvalakṣaṇabhedabhinnāni ākāśe cāpratiṣṭhitāni
children.translated_text: The elements, <s>Mahāmate</s>, when they are functioning, are differentiated from one another by distinctions of their own characteristics, and they are not established in space.
Yet space is not absent in them.

children.text: evameva śaśasya viṣāṇaṃ mahāmate goviṣāṇamapekṣya bhavati
children.translated_text: In just the same way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the horn of a hare exists in dependence on the horn of a cow.

children.text: goviṣāṇaṃ punarmahāmate aṇuśo vibhajyamānaṃ punarapyaṇavo vibhajyamānā aṇutvalakṣaṇe nāvatiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: But, <s>Mahāmate</s>, when a cow's horn is divided atom by atom, and the atoms again are divided, they do not remain in the characteristic of atomicity.

children.text: tasya kimapekṣya nāstitvaṃ bhavati athānyadapekṣya vastu tadapyevaṃdharmi
children.translated_text: In dependence on what, then, does its nonexistence arise? And if it depends on some other entity, that too has the same nature.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat śaśagośṛṅgākāśarūpadṛṣṭivikalpavigatena mahāmate bhavitavyam tadanyaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again said this to the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>: "<s>Mahāmate</s>, you and the other bodhisattvas should be free from the discriminations that are views of hare horn, cow horn, space, and form.
And, <s>Mahāmate</s>, you should have a mind that follows the discrimination of what is seen by one's own mind.
And in the circles of the fields of all sons of the Jina, you should give instruction in the yoga of what is seen by one's own mind."

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:

children.text: dṛśyaṃ na vidyate cittaṃ cittaṃ dṛśyātpravartate
children.translated_text: There is no visible object; there is mind. Mind proceeds from the visible object.
The <s>ālaya</s> (storehouse) appears to people as the foundation of divine enjoyments.
Mind, mentation, and consciousness, own-nature, and the fivefold group of dharmas,
the twofold selflessness and purity: these the Leaders proclaim.
Relation such as long and short proceeds mutually from one another.
There is no proof of existence; there is proof of nonexistence.

children.text: aṇuśo bhajyamānaṃ hi naiva rūpaṃ vikalpayet
children.translated_text: When it is being divided atom by atom, one should not imagine form at all.
The establishment is mind-only; it is not clarified by wrong view.
It is indeed not the domain of the logicians, nor is it that of the disciples,
which the Protectors teach as the domain of personal realization.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi svacittadṛśyadhārāviśuddhyarthaṃ bhagavantam adhyeṣate sma kathaṃ bhagavansvacittadṛśyadhārā viśudhyati yugapatkramavṛttyā vā bhagavānāha kramavṛttyā mahāmate svacittadṛśyadhārā viśudhyati na yugapat
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, again for the purification of the stream of what is seen by his own mind, entreated the Blessed One: "How, Blessed One, is the stream of what is seen by one's own mind purified, all at once or by gradual operation?" The Blessed One said: "By gradual operation, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the stream of what is seen by one's own mind is purified, not all at once.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate āmraphalāni kramaśaḥ pacyante na yugapat evameva mahāmate svacittadṛśyadhārā sattvānāṃ kramaśo viśudhyati na yugapat
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, mango fruits ripen gradually, not all at once, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the stream of what is seen by the own mind of beings is purified gradually, not all at once.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate kumbhakāraḥ kramaśo bhāṇḍāni kurute na yugapat evameva mahāmate tathāgataḥ sattvānāṃ svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ kramaśo viśodhayati na yugapat
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a potter makes vessels gradually, not all at once, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies the stream of what is seen by the own mind of beings gradually, not all at once.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate pṛthivyāṃ tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ kramavṛttyā virohanti na yugapat evameva mahāmate sattvānāṃ tathāgataḥ kramaśaḥ svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ viśodhayati na yugapat
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees grow on the earth by gradual operation, not all at once, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies the stream of what is seen by the own mind of beings gradually, not all at once.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate hāsyalāsyagītavāditravīṇālekhyayogyāḥ kramaśaḥ pravartante na yugapat evameva mahāmate tathāgataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kramaśaḥ svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ viśodhayati na yugapat
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, laughter, dance, song, instrumental music, vīṇā-playing, writing, and exercises proceed gradually, not all at once, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies the stream of what is seen by the own mind of all beings gradually, not all at once.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate darpaṇāntargatāḥ sarvarūpāvabhāsāḥ saṃdṛśyante nirvikalpā yugapat evameva mahāmate svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ yugapat tathāgataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ viśodhayati nirvikalpāṃ nirābhāsagocarām
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all reflections of forms contained in a mirror are seen all at once, without discrimination, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies all at once, for all beings, the stream of what is seen by one's own mind, making it without discrimination and having as its domain what is without appearance.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate somādityamaṇḍalaṃ yugapatsarvarūpāvabhāsān kiraṇaiḥ prakāśayati evameva mahāmate tathāgataḥ svacittadṛśyadauṣṭhulyavāsanāvigatānāṃ sattvānāṃ yugapadacintyajñānajinagocaraviṣayaṃ saṃdarśayati
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the disks of the moon and sun illuminate by their rays all appearances of forms all at once, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> shows all at once, to beings who are free from the latent impressions of coarseness in what is seen by their own mind, the object-domain of the inconceivable knowledge of the Jina.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate ālayavijñānaṃ svacittadṛśyadehapratiṣṭhābhogaviṣayaṃ yugapadvibhāvayati evameva mahāmate niṣyandabuddho yugapatsattvagocaraṃ paripācya ākaniṣṭhabhavanavimānālayayogaṃ yogināmarpayati
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) makes manifest all at once the body, support, enjoyments, and objects seen by one's own mind, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the transformation-body Buddha, having all at once matured the domain of beings, bestows on yogins the yoga of the palace-abode in the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> realm.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate dharmatābuddho yugapan niṣyandanirmāṇakiraṇair virājate evameva mahāmate pratyātmāryagatidharmalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvābhāvakudṛṣṭivinivartanatayā yugapadvirājate
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, just as the dharmatā Buddha shines forth at once with rays of outflow and emanation, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the characteristic of the dharma that is the course of the noble ones' realization within themselves shines forth at once by turning away from false views about existence and nonexistence.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate dharmatāniṣyandabuddhaḥ svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitāt sarvadharmāt svacittadṛśyavāsanāhetulakṣaṇopanibaddhāt parikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśahetukānatadātmakavividhamāyāraṅgapuruṣavaicitryābhiniveśānupalabdhito mahāmate deśayati
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the dharmatā and niṣyanda Buddha teaches from all dharmas that have fallen under particular and shared characteristics, bound by the characteristic whose cause is the latent impression of what appears as one's own mind, and from the non-apprehension of attachment to the manifold, illusory variety of stage-figures, which are not such in themselves and whose cause is attachment to imagined own-being.
Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the characteristic of the operation of imagined own-being proceeds from attachment to dependent own-being.

children.text: tadyathā tṛṇakāṣṭhagulmalatāśrayānmāyāvidyāpuruṣasaṃyogāt sarvasattvarūpadhāriṇaṃ māyāpuruṣavigraham abhiniṣpannaikasattvaśarīraṃ vividhakalpavikalpitaṃ khyāyate tathā khyāyannapi mahāmate tadātmako na bhavati evameva mahāmate paratantrasvabhāve parikalpitasvabhāve vividhavikalpacittavicitralakṣaṇaṃ khyāyate
children.translated_text: Just as, dependent on grass, wood, bushes, and creepers, and through the conjunction of an illusionist's spell and a person, an illusory human form bearing the appearances of all beings appears as a single produced body of a being, imagined with various conceptual constructions, yet, <s>Mahāmate</s>, although it appears, it is not of that nature; in just the same way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, in dependent own-being, imagined own-being appears with the variegated characteristics of a mind of many discriminations.
By imagining on account of the latent impression of attachment to the characteristic of object-imagination, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there is the characteristic of imagined own-being.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the teaching of the niṣyanda Buddha.
The dharmatā Buddha, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, establishes the arrangement of the domain of the noble course realized within oneself, separated from the characteristic of mind's own-being.

The created nirmāṇa Buddha, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, establishes the propagation of distinctions in the characteristics of giving, morality, meditation, samādhi, varied wisdom and knowledge, the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, liberations, consciousnesses, and destinies.
And he teaches, in opposition to the view of the tīrthikas, the characteristic of passing beyond the form realm.
The dharmatā Buddha, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is without support.

He is free from support, withdrawn from all the characteristics of activity, faculties, and means of knowledge, not an object for those fixed in attachment to the self-characteristics of childish people, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and tīrthaṃkaras.
Therefore, then, <s>Mahāmate</s>, practice should be undertaken with regard to the distinctive characteristic of the noble course realized within oneself.
And you should possess the view that turns away from the characteristic of what appears as your own mind.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate dvividhaṃ śrāvakayānanayaprabhedalakṣaṇaṃ yaduta pratyātmāryādhigamaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca bhāvavikalpasvabhāvābhiniveśalakṣaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the characteristic of the distinction in the method of the śrāvaka vehicle is twofold: namely, the characteristic of the distinction of noble realization within oneself, and the characteristic of attachment to own-being discriminated as entities.

children.text: tatra mahāmate pratyātmāryādhigamaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ katamat yaduta śūnyatānātmaduḥkhānityaviṣayasatyavairāgyopaśamāt
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the characteristic of the distinction of the śrāvakas' noble realization within themselves? It is this: through calming by revulsion toward the truths whose objects are emptiness, selflessness, suffering, and impermanence,

and through knowing as they really are the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, their particular and shared characteristics, and the characteristic of the destruction of external objects, the mind becomes concentrated.

children.text: svacittaṃ samādhāya dhyānavimokṣasamādhimārgaphalasamāpattivimuktivāsanācintyapariṇaticyutivigataṃ pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇasukhavihāraṃ mahāmate adhigacchanti śrāvakāḥ
children.translated_text: Having concentrated their own mind, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the śrāvakas attain the pleasant abiding characterized by the noble course realized within themselves, which is free from the inconceivable transformation and death associated with the latent impressions of meditation, liberations, samādhi, path, fruit, attainment, and release.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of the śrāvakas' noble course realized within themselves.

children.text: etaddhi mahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyātmāryādhigamavihārasukhamadhigamya bodhisattvena mahāsattvena nirodhasukhaṃ samāpattisukhaṃ ca sattvakriyāpekṣayā pūrvasvapraṇidhānābhinirhṛtatayā ca na sākṣātkaraṇīyam
children.translated_text: But, <s>Mahāmate</s>, after attaining this happiness of abiding in the śrāvakas' noble realization within themselves, a bodhisattva great being should not actualize the happiness of cessation and the happiness of attainment, out of regard for the activity of beings and because he has been drawn forth by his former own vow.

children.text: etanmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇasukhaṃ yatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇasukhe na śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the happiness characterized by the śrāvakas' noble course realized within themselves, in which a bodhisattva great being should not train as the happiness characterized by the noble course realized within oneself.

children.text: bhāvavikalpasvabhāvābhiniveśaḥ punarmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ katamaḥ yaduta nīlapītoṣṇadravacalakaṭhināni mahābhūtānyakriyāpravṛttāni svasāmānyalakṣaṇayuktyāgamapramāṇasuvinibaddhāni dṛṣṭvā tatsvabhāvābhiniveśavikalpaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the śrāvakas' attachment to own-being discriminated as entities? It is this: seeing the great elements as blue, yellow, hot, liquid, moving, and hard, inactive in operation, and well bound by reasoning, scripture, and means of knowledge concerning particular and shared characteristics, the discrimination that clings to their own-being proceeds.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, should be understood and turned away from by the bodhisattva.

By entering into the characteristic of the selflessness of dharmas, he should remove the view of the characteristic of the selflessness of persons and should establish himself in the successive connection of the stages.

children.text: etanmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ bhāvavikalpasvabhāvābhiniveśalakṣaṇaṃ yaduktam idaṃ tatpratyuktam
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is what was stated as the characteristic of the śrāvakas' attachment to own-being discriminated as entities; this has been explained.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat nityamacintyaṃ ca bhagavatā pratyātmāryagatigocaraṃ paramārthagocaraṃ ca prabhāṣitam
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, the Blessed One has taught that the domain of the noble course realized within oneself and the domain of ultimate truth are eternal and inconceivable.

children.text: nanu bhagavaṃstīrthakarā api nityācintyavādinaḥ kāraṇānām bhagavānāha na mahāmate tīrthakarāṇāṃ kāraṇasya nityācintyatāṃ prāpnoti
children.translated_text: But, Blessed One, do the tīrthakaras too not teach a doctrine of the eternal and inconceivable with regard to causes?" The Blessed One said: "No, <s>Mahāmate</s>; the eternal and inconceivable nature of the cause as taught by the tīrthakaras is not established.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tīrthakarāṇāṃ mahāmate nityācintyaṃ na hetusvalakṣaṇayuktam
children.translated_text: For what reason? <s>Mahāmate</s>, the eternal and inconceivable of the tīrthakaras is not endowed with the own-characteristic of a cause.

children.text: yasya mahāmate nityācintyaṃ na hetusvalakṣaṇayuktam tatkathakenābhivyajyate nityamacintyamiti nityācintyavādaḥ punarmahāmate yadi hetusvalakṣaṇayuktaḥ syāt nityaṃ kāraṇādhīnahetulakṣaṇatvānnityam acintyaṃ na bhavati
children.translated_text: That which, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is eternal and inconceivable but is not endowed with the own-characteristic of a cause: by what, and through whom, is it made manifest as eternal and inconceivable? Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, if the doctrine of the eternal and inconceivable were endowed with the own-characteristic of a cause, then, because what is eternal would have the characteristic of a cause dependent on causes, it would not be eternal and inconceivable.

children.text: mama tu mahāmate paramārthanityācintyaṃ paramārthalakṣaṇahetuyuktaṃ bhāvābhāvavigataṃ pratyātmāryādhigamalakṣaṇatvāl lakṣaṇavatparamārthajñānahetutvāc ca hetumadbhāvābhāvavigatatvād akṛtakākāśanirvāṇanirodhadṛṣṭāntasādharmyānnityam
children.translated_text: But for me, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the eternal and inconceivable ultimate reality is endowed with a cause conforming to the characteristic of ultimate reality, is free from existence and nonexistence, and is eternal because it has the character of the personal realization of the noble ones, because it is the cause of knowledge of ultimate reality possessing characteristics, because it is free from caused existence and nonexistence, and because it has a similarity to the examples of the unconditioned: space, nirvāṇa, and cessation.
Therefore this, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is not the same as the doctrine of the eternal and inconceivable held by the tīrthakaras.
This eternal inconceivability, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the suchness attained through the personal noble knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

children.text: tasmāttarhi mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena nityācintyapratyātmāryajñānādhigamāya yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a bodhisattva great being should practice yoga for the attainment of the eternal and inconceivable through personal noble knowledge.
Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the eternal inconceivability of the tīrthakaras has as its cause a distinction from impermanent entities.
It is not eternal through being made manifest by a characteristic cause created by itself.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate tīrthakarāṇāṃ nityācintyatā kṛtakabhāvābhāvādanityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā anumānabuddhyā nityaṃ samāpyate tenaiva hetunā mamāpi mahāmate kṛtakabhāvābhāvādanityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā nityamahetūpadeśāt
children.translated_text: But if, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the eternal inconceivability of the tīrthakaras is established as eternal by inferential understanding after seeing impermanence because conditioned existence is absent, then by that very reason, <s>Mahāmate</s>, my teaching too would be eternal after seeing impermanence because conditioned existence is absent, since eternality would be taught without a cause.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate hetulakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ nityācintyatā tīrthakarāṇāṃ hetubhāvasvalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvācchaśaviṣāṇatulyā mahāmate nityācintyatā vāgvikalpamātrā ca mahāmate tīrthakarāṇāṃ prasajyate
children.translated_text: But if, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the eternal inconceivability of the tīrthakaras is connected with the characteristic of a cause, then because there is no own-characteristic existence of causal being, their eternal inconceivability, <s>Mahāmate</s>, becomes like the horn of a hare and is merely verbal discrimination.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yaduta vāgvikalpamātraṃ hi mahāmate śaśaviṣāṇaṃ svahetulakṣaṇābhāvāt
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the horn of a hare is only verbal discrimination, since it has no characteristic cause of its own.

children.text: mama tu mahāmate nityācintyatā pratyātmāryādhigamalakṣaṇahetutvāt kṛtakabhāvābhāvavarjitatvānnityam na bāhyabhāvābhāvanityānityānupramāṇān nityam
children.translated_text: But my eternal inconceivability, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is eternal because it has as its cause the characteristic of personal noble realization and because it is excluded from conditioned existence and nonexistence; it is not eternal by an inference based on external existence or nonexistence, permanence or impermanence.

children.text: yasya punarmahāmate bāhyābhāvān nityānumānānnityācintyatvānnityam tasyā nityācintyatāyāḥ svahetulakṣaṇaṃ na jānīte
children.translated_text: But one who holds that it is eternal because of external nonexistence, by an inference of permanence, and because it is eternally inconceivable, does not know the own causal characteristic of that eternal inconceivability.
Those who are outside the characteristic that is the domain of personal attainment and noble knowledge, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are inexpressible with respect to it.
Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those frightened by the fear and suffering of the discrimination of saṃsāra seek nirvāṇa.

children.text: saṃsāranirvāṇayoraviśeṣajñāḥ sarvabhāvavikalpābhāvād indriyāṇām anāgataviṣayoparamācca mahāmate nirvāṇaṃ vikalpayanti na pratyātmagativijñānālayaṃ parāvṛttipūrvakaṃ mahāmate
children.translated_text: Not knowing that saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are undifferentiated, because there is no discrimination of any entity and because the faculties cease with respect to future objects, <s>Mahāmate</s>, they imagine nirvāṇa; they do not know the course of personal realization preceded by the transformation of the <s>vijñāna-ālaya</s> (storehouse consciousness), <s>Mahāmate</s>.

children.text: ataste mahāmate mohapuruṣā yānatrayavādino bhavanti na cittamātragatinirābhāsavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those deluded people become proponents of the three vehicles, not proponents of mind-only, whose course is free from appearances.

children.text: ataste mahāmate atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ svacittadṛśyagocarānabhijñā bāhyacittadṛśyagocarābhiniviṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, not knowing the object-domain seen by their own mind, as taught by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present, they are attached to an external object-domain seen by mind.
They wander again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, in the wheel of the course of saṃsāra.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate anutpannān sarvadharmān atītānāgatapratyutpannās tathāgatā bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present teach that all dharmas are unborn.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yaduta svacittadṛśyabhāvābhāvāt sadasator utpattivirahitatvānmahāmate anutpannāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? Namely, because there is no existence or nonexistence of what is seen by one's own mind, and because arising from either being or nonbeing is absent, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all entities are unborn.
All dharmas, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are like the horns of a hare, horse, donkey, or camel.
Because they are imagined by the discrimination of a non-existent, falsely constructed own-nature by foolish ordinary people, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all entities are unborn.

children.text: pratyātmāryajñānagatigocaro hi mahāmate sarvabhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇotpādaḥ na bālapṛthagjanavikalpadvayagocarasvabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: For, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the arising of the characteristic of the own-nature of all entities is the domain of the course of personal noble knowledge, not the own-nature that is the domain of the twofold discrimination of foolish ordinary people.

children.text: dehabhogapratiṣṭhāgatisvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ mahāmate ālayavijñānaṃ grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇena pravartamānaṃ bālā utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭidvayapatitāśayā utpādaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ sadasatorvikalpayanti
children.translated_text: The <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), <s>Mahāmate</s>, whose own characteristic is the course of body, enjoyment, and support, proceeds with the characteristic of grasped and grasper; fools whose dispositions have fallen into the dualistic view of arising, duration, and destruction discriminate the arising of all entities as either being or nonbeing.
In this matter, <s>Mahāmate</s>, you should practice yoga.
Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there are five lineages of realization.

children.text: katamāni pañca yaduta śrāvakayānābhisamayagotraṃ pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotraṃ tathāgatayānābhisamayagotram aniyataikataragotram agotraṃ ca pañcamam
children.translated_text: What are the five? Namely, the lineage of realization of the śrāvaka vehicle, the lineage of realization of the pratyekabuddha vehicle, the lineage of realization of the <s>Tathāgata</s> vehicle, an indeterminate lineage of either one, and, fifth, no lineage.

children.text: kathaṃ punarmahāmate śrāvakayānābhisamayagotraṃ pratyetavyam yaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanasvasāmānyalakṣaṇaparijñānādhigame deśyamāne romāñcitatanurbhavati
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the lineage of realization of the śrāvaka vehicle to be recognized? When the knowledge and attainment of the particular and shared characteristics of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases is being taught, his body becomes thrilled with horripilation.
His understanding rushes toward knowledge that acquaints itself with characteristics, but not toward acquaintance with the characteristic of dependent arising as inseparable.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the lineage of realization of the śrāvaka vehicle.

children.text: yaḥ śrāvakayānābhisamayaṃ dṛṣṭvā ṣaṭpañcamyāṃ bhūmau paryutthānakleśaprahīṇo vāsanakleśāprahīṇo 'cintyācyutigataḥ samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadati kṣīṇā me jātiḥ uṣitaṃ brahmacaryam ityevamādi nigadya pudgalanairātmyaparicayād yāvannirvāṇabuddhir bhavati
children.translated_text: One who, after seeing the realization of the śrāvaka vehicle, on the sixth and fifth stages has abandoned manifest afflictions but has not abandoned the afflictions as latent impressions, has entered inconceivable passing away, and utters the correct lion's roar, saying, 'Birth is exhausted for me; the holy life has been lived,' and the like, comes to have the thought of nirvāṇa as far as acquaintance with the selflessness of persons.
Others, <s>Mahāmate</s>, seek nirvāṇa through the awakening to self, being, living soul, nourished being, person, individual, and sentient being.

children.text: anye punarmahāmate kāraṇādhīnān sarvadharmān dṛṣṭvā nirvāṇagatibuddhayo bhavanti
children.translated_text: Still others, <s>Mahāmate</s>, seeing all dharmas as dependent on causes, come to have the thought of the course toward nirvāṇa.
Because they do not see the selflessness of dharmas, there is no liberation, <s>Mahāmate</s>.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the understanding, with regard to non-departure and departure, of one whose lineage is oriented toward realization of the śrāvaka vehicle.

children.text: atra te mahāmate kudṛṣṭivyāvṛttyarthaṃ yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Mahāmate</s>, yoga should be practiced for the sake of turning away wrong views.

children.text: tatra mahāmate pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotrakaḥ yaḥ pratyekābhisamaye deśyamāne aśruhṛṣṭaromāñcitatanurbhavati
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one whose lineage is oriented toward realization of the pratyekabuddha vehicle is the person whose body becomes tearful, thrilled, and bristling with hair when the individual realization is being taught.

children.text: asaṃsargapratyayād bhāvābhiniveśabahuvividhasvakāyavaicitryarddhivyastayamakaprātihāryadarśane nirdiśyamāne 'nunīyate sa pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotraka iti viditvā pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayānurūpā kathā karaṇīyā
children.translated_text: When, because of conditions of isolation, the many and various miraculous transformations of one's own body, the supernormal powers, displays, and paired miracles are being explained for one attached to entities, he is drawn to them. Knowing him to be one whose lineage is oriented toward realization of the pratyekabuddha vehicle, a discourse suited to realization of the pratyekabuddha vehicle should be given.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of one whose lineage is oriented toward realization of the pratyekabuddha vehicle.

children.text: tatra mahāmate tathāgatayānābhisamayagotraṃ trividham yaduta svabhāvaniḥsvabhāvadharmābhisamayagotram adhigamasvapratyātmāryābhisamayagotram bāhyabuddhakṣetraudāryābhisamayagotraṃ ca
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the lineage oriented toward realization of the <s>Tathāgata</s> vehicle is threefold, namely the lineage for realizing dharmas as without own-nature, the lineage for realizing the noble attainment personally within oneself, and the lineage for realizing the grandeur of external Buddha-fields.

children.text: yadā punarmahāmate trayāṇāmapyeṣāmanyatame deśyamāne svacittadṛśyadehālayabhogapratiṣṭhācintyaviṣaye deśyamāne nottrasati na saṃtrasati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate veditavyamayaṃ tathāgatayānābhisamayagotraka iti
children.translated_text: But when, <s>Mahāmate</s>, any one of these three is being taught, and when the inconceivable domain of body, <s>ālaya</s> (storehouse), enjoyments, and support seen by one's own mind is being taught, he does not tremble, is not frightened, and does not fall into fear, it should be known that he belongs to the lineage oriented toward realization of the <s>Tathāgata</s> vehicle.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of one whose lineage is oriented toward realization of the <s>Tathāgata</s> vehicle.

children.text: aniyatagotrakaḥ punarmahāmate triṣvapyeteṣu deśyamāneṣu yatrānunīyate tatrānuyojyaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one of uncertain lineage should be guided toward whichever of these three he is drawn to when they are being taught.
This classification of lineages, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is a preparatory stage.
The classification is made for the sake of entering the stage free from appearances.

children.text: pratyātmālaye tu svakleśavāsanāśuddhasya dharmanairātmyadarśanāt samādhisukhavihāraṃ prāpya śrāvako jinakāyatāṃ pratilapsyate
children.translated_text: But when his own <s>ālaya</s> has been purified of the latent impressions of his own defilements, and when, from seeing the selflessness of dharmas, he has attained the pleasant abiding of samādhi, the śrāvaka will obtain the state of the body of the Jina.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:
The fruit of stream-entry, and likewise that of the once-returner,
the fruit of the non-returner and arhatship are a bewilderment of mind.
I teach the three vehicles, the one vehicle, and no vehicle,
for fools of dull understanding, and the seclusion of the noble ones.
For the doorway to the highest truth is representation free from duality;
when one is established in the appearance-free, how could there be the establishment of three vehicles?
The meditations, the immeasurables, and the formless samādhis,
the cessation of perception, all of this does not exist in mind-only.

children.text: tatrecchantikānāṃ punarmahāmate anicchantikatāmokṣaṃ kena pravartate yaduta sarvakuśalamūlotsargataśca sattvānādikālapraṇidhānataśca
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, by what does the state of icchantikas, who do not desire liberation, arise? It arises from abandoning all roots of merit and from the vow concerning beings from beginningless time.

children.text: tatra sarvakuśalamūlotsargaḥ katamaḥ yaduta bodhisattvapiṭakanikṣepo'bhyākhyānaṃ ca naite sūtrāntā vinayamokṣānukūlā iti bruvataḥ sarvakuśalamūlotsargatvānna nirvāyate
children.translated_text: There, what is the abandonment of all roots of merit? It is the rejection and slandering of the bodhisattva basket, saying, 'These sūtras are not conducive to discipline or liberation.' Because he has abandoned all roots of merit, he does not attain nirvāṇa.

children.text: dvitīyaḥ punarmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ bhavapraṇidhānopāyapūrvakatvānnāparinirvṛtaiḥ sarvasattvaiḥ parinirvāsyāmīti tato na parinirvāti
children.translated_text: The second, however, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is precisely the bodhisattva great being who, because his former practice is guided by the vow in existence, thinks, 'I shall attain final nirvāṇa only when all beings who have not attained final nirvāṇa have done so.' Therefore he does not attain final nirvāṇa.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of those whose nature is not to attain final nirvāṇa, through which they reach the state of an icchantika.

children.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha katamo'tra bhagavan atyantato na parinirvāti bhagavānāha bodhisattvecchantiko'tra mahāmate ādiparinirvṛtān sarvadharmān viditvā atyantato na parinirvāti
children.translated_text: Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said, 'Blessed One, which of these absolutely does not attain final nirvāṇa?' The Blessed One said, 'Here, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the bodhisattva icchantika, having known that all dharmas are originally in final nirvāṇa, absolutely does not attain final nirvāṇa.'
But not the icchantika who has abandoned all roots of merit.
For, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the icchantika who has abandoned all roots of merit may at some time, by the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, again cause roots of merit to arise.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yaduta aparityaktā hi mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ sarvasattvāḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? Because, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all beings have not been abandoned by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.
For this reason, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the bodhisattva icchantika does not attain final nirvāṇa.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena svabhāvalakṣaṇatrayakuśalena bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a bodhisattva great being should be skilled in the three characteristics of own-nature.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the imagined own-nature proceeds from a sign.

children.text: kathaṃ punarmahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvo nimittātpravartate tatra mahāmate paratantrasvabhāvo vastunimittalakṣaṇākāraḥ khyāyate
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Mahāmate</s>, does the imagined own-nature proceed from a sign? There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the dependent own-nature appears as the form characterized by the sign of an object.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, attachment to the characteristic of the sign of an object is again of two kinds.

children.text: parikalpitasvabhāvaṃ vyavasthāpayanti tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā nāmābhiniveśalakṣaṇena ca nāmavastunimittābhiniveśalakṣaṇena ca
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas establish imagined own-nature by the characteristic of attachment to name and by the characteristic of attachment to the sign of name and object.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the characteristic of attachment to the sign of an object is attachment to internal and external dharmas.

children.text: nimittalakṣaṇābhiniveśaḥ punar yaduta teṣveva ādhyātmikabāhyeṣu dharmeṣu svasāmānyalakṣaṇaparijñānāvabodhaḥ
children.translated_text: Attachment to the characteristic of a sign, again, is the understanding and apprehension of the particular and general characteristics in those very internal and external dharmas.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the twofold characteristic of imagined own-nature.
That which proceeds in dependence on a basis and an object-support is the dependent.

children.text: tatra mahāmate pariniṣpannasvabhāvaḥ katamaḥ yaduta nimittanāmavastulakṣaṇavikalpavirahitaṃ tathatāryajñānagatigamanapratyātmāryajñānagatigocaraḥ
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the perfected own-nature? It is that which is free from the discrimination of the characteristics of sign, name, and object: suchness, the course and domain of the noble knowledge realized within oneself.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the perfected own-nature, the heart of the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>.
Then at that time the Blessed One spoke this verse:
Sign, name, and conceptual construction are the characteristic of the two own-natures;
right knowledge and suchness are the characteristic of the perfected.

children.text: eṣa mahāmate pañcadharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇapravicayo nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ pratyātmāryajñānagatigocaraḥ yatra tvayā anyaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the discourse called the examination of the characteristics of the five dharmas and the own-natures, the domain of the course of noble knowledge realized within oneself; in this you and the other bodhisattvas should train.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena nairātmyadvayalakṣaṇapravicayakuśalena bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a bodhisattva great being should become skilled in examining the characteristic of the twofold selflessness.

children.text: tatra mahāmate katamannairātmyadvayalakṣaṇam yaduta ātmātmīyarahitaskandhadhātvāyatanakadambakam ajñānakarmatṛṣṇāprabhavaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpādigrahaṇābhiniveśātpravartamānaṃ vijñānaṃ sarvendriyaiḥ svacittadṛśyabhājanadehālayasvacittavikalpavikalpitaṃ vijñāpayati
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the characteristic of the twofold selflessness? It is this: the heap of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, devoid of self and what belongs to self, arises from ignorance, karma, and craving; from attachment to the grasping of forms and so on by the eye, consciousness proceeds, and by all the faculties it makes known the body, support, and receptacle seen as one's own mind, discriminated by the discriminations of one's own mind.

children.text: nadībījadīpavāyumeghasadṛśakṣaṇaparamparābhedabhinnaṃ capalaṃ vānaramakṣikāsadṛśam acaukṣamacaukṣaviṣayacāryanātho'nala ivātṛptam anādikālaprapañcaviṣayavāsanārahitam araghaṭṭacakrayantracakravat saṃsārabhavagaticakre vicitradeharūpadhārimāyāvetālayantrapratimaṃ pravartamānaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: It proceeds as something split apart by the difference of a momentary series, like a river, a seed, a lamp, wind, or a cloud; restless like a monkey or a fly; impure, ranging over impure objects; unsatisfied like fire; not free from beginningless latent impressions of proliferation about objects; and, like the mechanism of a water-wheel, moving in the wheel of the courses of becoming in saṃsāra, bearing varied bodily forms like an illusion, a corpse-demon, or a mechanical figure.
The knowledge that is skillful regarding the characteristic in this matter, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is called the knowledge of the selflessness of persons.

children.text: tatra mahāmate dharmanairātmyajñānaṃ katamat yaduta skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇasvabhāvāvabodhaḥ
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the knowledge of the selflessness of dharmas? It is the understanding of the imagined characteristic and own-nature of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: yathā mahāmate skandhadhātvāyatanānyātmavirahitāni skandhasamūhamātraṃ hetukarmatṛṣṇāsūtropanibaddhamanyonyapratyayatayā pravartate nirīham tathā skandhā api mahāmate svasāmānyalakṣaṇavirahitā abhūtaparikalpalakṣaṇavicitraprabhāvitā bālairvikalpyante na tvāryaiḥ
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are devoid of self, and the mere collection of aggregates, bound by the thread of causes, karma, and craving, proceeds through mutual conditionality and is without agency, so too the aggregates, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are devoid of particular and shared characteristics; they are diversified by the characteristic of unreal imagination and are discriminated by fools, but not by the noble ones.

children.text: cittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvarahitān mahāmate sarvadharmān vibhāvayan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmanairātmyakuśalo bhavati
children.translated_text: When a bodhisattva great being, <s>Mahāmate</s>, discerns all dharmas as devoid of mind, mentation, mental consciousness, the five dharmas, and own-nature, he becomes skilled in the selflessness of dharmas.

children.text: dharmanairātmyakuśalaḥ punarmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvo nacirātprathamāṃ bodhisattvabhūmiṃ nirābhāsapravicayāṃ pratilabhate
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a bodhisattva great being who is skilled in the selflessness of dharmas before long attains the first bodhisattva stage, the examination free from appearances.

children.text: bhūmilakṣaṇapravicayāvabodhāt pramuditānantaram anupūrvaṃ navasu bhūmiṣu kṛtavidyo mahādharmameghāṃ pratilabhate
children.translated_text: Through understanding the examination of the characteristics of the stages, after the Joyous stage he gradually becomes accomplished in knowledge on the nine stages and attains the great Dharma-cloud.

children.text: sa tasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito'nekaratnamuktopaśobhite mahāpadmarāje padmakṛtau mahāratnavimāne māyāsvabhāvagocaraparicayābhinirvṛtte niṣaṇṇaḥ tadanurūpairjinaputraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrāgatair buddhapāṇyabhiṣekaiś cakravartiputravadabhiṣicyate
children.translated_text: Established there, seated in a great jewel palace shaped like a lotus, on a great royal lotus adorned with many jewels and pearls, brought forth by familiarity with the object-domain whose own-nature is illusion, and surrounded by corresponding sons of the Victorious Ones who have come from all buddha-fields, he is consecrated by the hands of the Buddhas, like a son of a wheel-turning king.

children.text: buddhasutabhūmim atikramya pratyātmāryadharmagatigamanatvāt tathāgato dharmakāyavaśavartī bhaviṣyati dharmanairātmyadarśanāt
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond the stage of a son of the Buddha, because he has entered the course of the noble dharma realized within oneself, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, master of the <s>dharmakāya</s>, through seeing the selflessness of dharmas.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of the selflessness of all dharmas.

children.text: atra te mahāmate śikṣitavyam anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ
children.translated_text: In this you should train, <s>Mahāmate</s>, and so should the other bodhisattvas great beings.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat samāropāpavādalakṣaṇaṃ me bhagavān deśayatu yathāhaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvāḥ samāropāpavādakudṛṣṭivarjitamatayaḥ kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyeran
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One teach me the characteristic of superimposition and denial, so that I and the other bodhisattvas, our minds free from the false views of superimposition and denial, may quickly awaken to unsurpassed complete perfect awakening.
Having awakened, free from the eternalist view of superimposition and from denial as the view of annihilation, they will not disparage your buddha-lineage."

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmaterbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyādhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having again understood the request of the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>, spoke this verse:
In mind-only there is no superimposition or denial.
Those who do not understand mind as appearing as body, enjoyment, and support
wander in superimposition and denial; they are without insight.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavānetameva gāthārthamuddyotayan punarapyetad avocat caturvidho mahāmate asatsamāropaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, illuminating the meaning of that very verse, again said this: "There are four kinds of unreal superimposition, <s>Mahāmate</s>.
What are the four? Namely, superimposition of an unreal characteristic, superimposition of an unreal view, superimposition of an unreal cause, and superimposition of an unreal entity.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the fourfold superimposition.

children.text: apavādaḥ punarmahāmate katamaḥ yaduta asyaiva kudṛṣṭisamāropasyānupalabdhipravicayābhāvād apavādo bhavati
children.translated_text: And what, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is denial? Denial occurs from the absence of examination into the non-apprehension of this very false-view superimposition.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of superimposition and denial."

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate asallakṣaṇasamāropasya lakṣaṇaṃ katamat yaduta skandhadhātvāyatanānām asatsvasāmānyalakṣaṇābhiniveśaḥ idam evamidaṃ nānyatheti
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the characteristic of the superimposition of a non-existent characteristic? It is attachment to particular and shared characteristics in the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, though they do not exist: 'This is thus, and not otherwise.'
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of the superimposition of a non-existent characteristic.
For this discrimination that superimposes a non-existent characteristic, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from attachment to the manifold latent impressions of the corrupt elaboration beginningless in time.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of the superimposition of a non-existent characteristic.

Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the superimposition of a non-existent view is the superimposition, upon those very aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, of views of self, life-principle, creature, nourished being, person, and individual.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is called the superimposition of a non-existent view.

children.text: asaddhetusamāropaḥ punarmahāmate yaduta ahetusamutpannaṃ prāgvijñānaṃ paścādabhūtvā māyāvadanutpannaṃ pūrvaṃ cakṣūrūpālokasmṛtipūrvakaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the superimposition of a non-existent cause is this: consciousness is first said to arise without cause and, not having existed before, to be unborn like an illusion, and then it proceeds on the basis of eye, form, light, and memory.
