And after it has proceeded and come into being, it again perishes.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the superimposition of a non-existent cause.
Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the superimposition of a non-existent entity is the superimposition of attachment to the existence of unconditioned things such as space, cessation, and nirvāṇa.
And these, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are free from existence and non-existence.
All dharmas, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are like the horns of a hare, horse, donkey, or camel, or like a hair-net before the eyes; they are beyond the positions of existent and non-existent.
Superimposition and denial are imagined by fools whose understanding has not determined that what is seen is only one's own mind, but not by the noble ones.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the characteristic of the superimposition and denial that discriminate a non-existent entity.
Therefore, then, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one should be free from the views of superimposition and denial.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvāś cittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvanairātmyalakṣaṇadvayagatiṃ gatvā parahitahetor anekarūpaveṣadhāriṇo bhavanti
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas, having understood the course of the twofold characteristic of mind, mentation, mental consciousness, the five dharmas, own-nature, and selflessness, assume many forms and appearances for the sake of benefiting others.

children.text: parikalpitasvabhāvā iva paratantrāśayā viśvarūpacintāmaṇisadṛśāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣanmaṇḍalagatā māyāsvapnapratibhāsapratibimbodakacandragatisamān utpādabhaṅgaśāśvatocchedarahitān sarvadharmān saṃmukhaṃ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānavirahān dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇvanti samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇi ca pratilabhante
children.translated_text: Like imagined own-nature, dependent on the intentions of others, and resembling the wish-fulfilling jewel of manifold forms, they go into the assemblies in all buddha-fields and, directly before all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, hear the teaching of dharma that is free from the vehicles of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, concerning all dharmas as like illusion, dream, appearance, reflection, and the moon in water, and as devoid of arising, destruction, permanence, and annihilation; and they obtain hundreds of thousands of entrances into samādhi.

children.text: yāvadanekāni samādhikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhya taiḥ samādhibhiḥ kṣetrātkṣetraṃ saṃkrāmanti
children.translated_text: Having obtained many hundreds of thousands of koṭis and niyutas of samādhis, they pass by means of those samādhis from field to field.

children.text: buddhapūjābhiyuktāśca sarvopapattidevabhavanālayeṣu ratnatrayamupadeśya buddharūpamāsthāya śrāvakagaṇabodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtāḥ svacittadṛśyamātrāvatāraṇatayā bāhyabhāvābhāvopadeśaṃ kurvanti sadasatpakṣavinivṛttyartham
children.translated_text: Intent on worshiping the buddhas, in all the abodes of birth and divine mansions they teach the Three Jewels, assume buddha-forms, and, surrounded by hosts of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, give instruction in the non-existence of external entities so as to introduce beings to the fact that what appears is only their own mind, for the purpose of turning them away from the positions of existent and non-existent.
Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:
When the children of the Victors behold the world as mind-only,
then they obtain a magically created body, free from actions and formations,
endowed with powers, superknowledges, and masteries.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantam adhyeṣate sma deśayatu bhagavān śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām yena śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇāvabodhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā nāstyastivikalpavarjitāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach the characteristic of emptiness, non-arising, non-duality, and lack of own-nature in all dharmas, so that, by understanding the characteristic of emptiness, non-arising, non-duality, and lack of own-nature, I and other bodhisattva great beings, free from discrimination of non-existence and existence, may quickly awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocattena hi mahāmate śṛṇu tatsādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said this to the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>: 'Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, listen, and attend carefully and well.
I shall speak to you.'

children.text: sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt
children.translated_text: 'Good, Blessed One,' the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this: '<s>Mahāmate</s>, "emptiness, emptiness" is a word belonging to imagined own-nature.
Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, through attachment to imagined own-nature, people become proponents of emptiness, non-arising, non-being, non-duality, and lack of own-nature.
In this matter, <s>Mahāmate</s>, in brief, emptiness is sevenfold:

children.text: yaduta lakṣaṇaśūnyatā bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā apracaritaśūnyatā pracaritaśūnyatā sarvadharmanirabhilāpyaśūnyatā paramārthāryajñānamahāśūnyatā itaretaraśūnyatā ca saptamī
children.translated_text: namely, emptiness of characteristic, emptiness of the own-nature of entities, emptiness of the unpracticed, emptiness of the practiced, emptiness of the inexpressibility of all dharmas, great emptiness of the noble knowledge of ultimate truth, and, as the seventh, emptiness of one thing by another.

children.text: tatra mahāmate lakṣaṇaśūnyatā katamā yaduta svasāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is emptiness of characteristic? It is this: all entities are empty of particular and shared characteristics.
Because they depend on mutual aggregation, and because there is no division in analysis, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the particular and shared characteristic does not occur.
And because self, other, and both are absent, <s>Mahāmate</s>, no characteristic is established.
Therefore it is said that all entities are empty of their own characteristics.

children.text: bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā yaduta svayaṃ svabhāvābhāvotpattito mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā bhavati sarvadharmāṇām
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is emptiness of the own-nature of entities? It is this: because own-nature does not arise by itself, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there is emptiness of the own-nature of entities in all dharmas.
Therefore it is called emptiness of the own-nature of entities.'

children.text: apracaritaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā yaduta apracaritapūrvaṃ nirvāṇaṃ skandheṣu
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is unused emptiness? It is this: nirvāṇa, previously unused, in relation to the aggregates.
Therefore it is called unused emptiness.

children.text: pracaritaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā yaduta skandhā ātmātmīyarahitā hetuyuktikriyākarmayogaiḥ pravartamānāḥ pravartante
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is used emptiness? It is this: the aggregates, devoid of self and what belongs to self, proceed as they proceed through the combinations of causes, reasoning, activity, action, and connection.
Therefore it is called used emptiness.

children.text: sarvadharmanirabhilāpyaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā yaduta parikalpitasvabhāvān abhilāpyatvānnirabhilāpyaśūnyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the emptiness of all dharmas as inexpressible? It is this: all dharmas are empty of expressibility as inexpressible, because the imagined own-nature is expressible.
Therefore it is called the emptiness of inexpressibility.

children.text: paramārthāryajñānamahāśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā yaduta svapratyātmāryajñānādhigamaḥ sarvadṛṣṭidoṣavāsanābhiḥ śūnyaḥ
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the great emptiness of ultimate noble knowledge? It is this: the realization of noble knowledge within oneself is empty of the latent impressions of all faults of views.
Therefore it is called the great emptiness of ultimate noble knowledge.

children.text: itaretaraśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā yaduta yadyatra nāsti tattena śūnyamityucyate
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the emptiness of one thing by another? It is this: when something is not present somewhere, that place is said to be empty of that thing.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate śṛgālamātuḥ prāsāde hastigavaiḍakādyā na santi
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, elephants, cattle, sheep, and the like are not present in the palace of <s>Śṛgālamātṛ</s>.
And I have said that it is not empty of monks.
Yet it is called empty of those things.

children.text: na ca punarmahāmate prāsādaḥ prāsādabhāvato nāsti bhikṣavaśca bhikṣubhāvato na santi
children.translated_text: But, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the palace is not nonexistent as a palace, nor are the monks nonexistent as monks.

children.text: na ca te'nyatra hastigavaiḍakādyā bhāvā nāvatiṣṭhante
children.translated_text: Nor do those entities, elephants, cattle, sheep, and the like, fail to exist elsewhere.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the particular and shared characteristic of all dharmas.
But one thing is not found in another.
Therefore it is called the emptiness of one thing by another.
This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the sevenfold emptiness.
And this emptiness of one thing by another, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the lowest of all.
It should be avoided by you.

children.text: na svayamutpadyate na ca punarmahāmate te notpadyante anyatra samādhyavasthāyām
children.translated_text: They do not arise by themselves, and again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, they do not arise except in the state of samādhi.
Therefore they are called unborn and without own-nature.
With reference to non-arising, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all entities are without own-nature.
And because there is no continuous succession of momentary continuity, and because a state of becoming otherwise is seen, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all entities are without own-nature.
Therefore it is said that all entities are without own-nature.

children.text: advayalakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate katamat yaduta chāyātapavaddīrghahrasvakṛṣṇaśuklavan mahāmate dvayaprabhāvitā na pṛthakpṛthak
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the characteristic of non-duality? It is this: <s>Mahāmate</s>, as with shade and sunlight, long and short, black and white, things conditioned by a pair are not separate one by one.
In the same way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all dharmas are non-dual, like saṃsāra and nirvāṇa.

children.text: na yatra mahāmate nirvāṇaṃ tatra saṃsāraḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is nirvāṇa, <s>Mahāmate</s>, there is not saṃsāra.

children.text: na ca yatra saṃsārastatra nirvāṇam vilakṣaṇahetusadbhāvāt
children.translated_text: And where there is saṃsāra, there is not nirvāṇa, because there is the existence of distinct causes.
Therefore it is said that all dharmas are non-dual, like saṃsāra and complete nirvāṇa.
Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, practice should be undertaken with regard to the characteristic of emptiness, non-arising, non-duality, and absence of own-nature.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmime gāthe abhāṣata
children.translated_text: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:
I always teach emptiness, free from eternalism and annihilationism;

children.text: saṃsāraṃ svapnamāyākhyaṃ na ca karma vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: saṃsāra is called dream and illusion, and yet karma does not perish.
Space, then nirvāṇa, cessation, and also duality:
the foolish imagine them as unconditioned; the noble are free from existence and nonexistence.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam etadavocad etaddhi mahāmate śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ sarvasūtrāntagatam
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again said this to the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s>: This characteristic of emptiness, non-arising, non-duality, and absence of own-nature, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is found in all the sūtrāntas of all buddhas.
Wherever it occurs in a sūtrānta, this very meaning should be discerned.

children.text: eṣa hi mahāmate sūtrāntaḥ sarvasattvāśayadeśanārthavyabhicāriṇī na sā tattvapratyavasthānakathā
children.translated_text: For this sūtrānta, <s>Mahāmate</s>, varies in order to teach according to the dispositions of all beings; it is not a discourse establishing reality itself.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate mṛgatṛṣṇikā mṛgollāpinī udakabhāvābhiniveśenābhiniveśyate tasyāṃ codakaṃ nāsti evameva mahāmate sarvasūtrāntadeśanā dharmā bālānāṃ svavikalpasaṃtoṣaṇam na tu sā tattvāryajñānavyavasthānakathā
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a mirage deceives deer and is grasped through fixation on the existence of water, though there is no water in it. In just this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all sūtrānta teachings of dharmas are for satisfying the own discriminations of foolish people, not a discourse establishing the reality of noble knowledge.

children.text: tasmāttarhi mahāmate arthānusāriṇā bhavitavyaṃ na deśanābhilāpābhiniviṣṭena
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one should follow the meaning, not become attached to the verbal expressions of the teaching.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocattathāgatagarbhaḥ punarbhagavatā sūtrāntapāṭhe'nuvarṇitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: Blessed One, the tathāgatagarbha has again been described by the Blessed One in the recitation of the sūtrāntas.

children.text: sa ca kila tvayā prakṛtiprabhāsvaraviśuddhyādiviśuddha eva varṇyate dvātriṃśallakṣaṇadharaḥ sarvasattvadehāntargataḥ
children.translated_text: And you describe it as purified by its natural luminosity and primordial purity, bearing the thirty-two marks, and contained within the bodies of all beings.

children.text: mahārghamūlyaratnaṃ malinavastupariveṣṭitamiva skandhadhātvāyatanavastuveṣṭito rāgadveṣamohābhūtaparikalpamalamalino nityo dhruvaḥ śivaḥ śāśvataśca bhagavatā varṇitaḥ
children.translated_text: Like a jewel of great value wrapped in a soiled cloth, it is wrapped in the substances of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, stained by the stains of passion, hatred, delusion, and unreal imagination; and it is described by the Blessed One as eternal, firm, auspicious, and everlasting.

children.text: tatkathamayaṃ bhagavaṃstīrthakarātmavādatulyastathāgatagarbhavādo na bhavati tīrthakarā api bhagavan nityaḥ kartā nirguṇo vibhuravyaya ityātmavādopadeśaṃ kurvanti
children.translated_text: How then, Blessed One, is this doctrine of the tathāgatagarbha not the same as the tīrthakaras' doctrine of self? For the tīrthakaras too, Blessed One, teach a doctrine of self as eternal, a maker, without qualities, all-pervading, and imperishable.

children.text: bhagavānāha na hi mahāmate tīrthakarātmavādatulyo mama tathāgatagarbhopadeśaḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: No, <s>Mahāmate</s>; my teaching of the tathāgatagarbha is not the same as the tīrthakaras' doctrine of self.

children.text: kiṃ tu mahāmate tathāgatāḥ śūnyatābhūtakoṭinirvāṇānutpādānimittāpraṇihitādyānāṃ mahāmate padārthānāṃ tathāgatagarbhopadeśaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bālānāṃ nairātmyasaṃtrāsapadavivarjanārthaṃ nirvikalpanirābhāsagocaraṃ tathāgatagarbhamukhopadeśena deśayanti
children.translated_text: Rather, <s>Mahāmate</s>, after giving the instruction on the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> with regard to such entities as emptiness, the limit of reality, nirvāṇa, non-arising, signlessness, wishlessness, and so on, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas teach the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, the domain free from conceptual construction and appearance, by means of the instruction called <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, in order to avoid the occasion of terrifying fools with selflessness.

children.text: na cātra mahāmate anāgatapratyutpannaiḥ bodhisattvairmahāsattvairātmābhiniveśaḥ kartavyaḥ
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas great beings of the future and the present should not form an attachment to a self.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate kumbhakāra ekasmānmṛtparamāṇurāśervividhāni bhāṇḍāni karoti hastaśilpadaṇḍodakasūtraprayatnayogāt evameva mahāmate tathāgatāstadeva dharmanairātmyaṃ sarvavikalpalakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ vividhaiḥ prajñopāyakauśalyayogair garbhopadeśena vā nairātmyopadeśena vā kumbhakāravaccitraiḥ padavyañjanaparyāyair deśayante
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a potter makes various vessels from one mass of clay atoms through the application of manual skill, a staff, water, cord, and effort, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach that very selflessness of dharmas, free from the characteristics of all conceptual constructions, through various forms of wisdom and skillful means, whether by instruction on the womb or by instruction on selflessness, like potters, with varied modes of words and syllables.
For this reason, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the instruction on the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is not equivalent to the non-Buddhist teachers' instruction on a self.

children.text: evaṃ hi mahāmate tathāgatagarbhopadeśamātmavādābhiniviṣṭānāṃ tīrthakarāṇāmākarṣaṇārthaṃ tathāgatagarbhopadeśena nirdiśanti kathaṃ bata abhūtātmavikalpadṛṣṭipatitāśayā vimokṣatrayagocarapatitāśayopetāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeranniti
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach through the instruction on the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> for the purpose of attracting non-Buddhist teachers attached to the doctrine of self, thinking, 'How might those whose dispositions have fallen into the view that falsely imagines a self, and who are endowed with dispositions fallen into the domain of the three liberations, quickly awaken to unsurpassed complete perfect awakening?'

children.text: etadarthaṃ mahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tathāgatagarbhopadeśaṃ kurvanti
children.translated_text: For this purpose, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas give the instruction on the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>.
Therefore this is not equivalent to the self-doctrine of the non-Buddhist teachers.

children.text: tasmāttarhi mahāmate tīrthakaradṛṣṭivinivṛttyarthaṃ tathāgatanairātmyagarbhānusāriṇā ca te bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, in order to turn away from the view of the non-Buddhist teachers, you should follow the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> of selflessness.
Then at that time the Blessed One spoke this verse:
Person, continuum, aggregates, conditions, and atoms as well,
the primordial matter, <s>Īśvara</s>, the maker, and mind-only are imagined.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo'nāgatāṃ janatāṃ samālokya punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma deśayatu me bhagavān yogābhisamayaṃ yathā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva <s>Mahāmati</s>, looking toward the people of the future, again requested the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the realization of yoga, by which bodhisattvas great beings become great yogins devoted to great yoga.'

children.text: bhagavānāha caturbhirmahāmate dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: '<s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas become great yogins when they are endowed with four dharmas.

children.text: katamaiścaturbhiḥ yaduta svacittadṛśyavibhāvanatayā ca utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭivivarjanatayā ca bāhyabhāvābhāvopalakṣaṇatayā ca svapratyātmāryajñānādhigamābhilakṣaṇatayā ca
children.translated_text: With which four? Namely, with the discernment that what is seen is one's own mind; with the abandonment of the view of arising, abiding, and destruction; with the recognition of the existence and nonexistence of external things; and with the characteristic mark of attaining noble knowledge realized within oneself.

children.text: ebhirmahāmate caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti
children.translated_text: Endowed with these four dharmas, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas great beings become great yogins.

children.text: tatra kathaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svacittadṛśyavibhāvanākuśalo bhavati yaduta sa evaṃ pratyavekṣate svacittamātramidaṃ traidhātukamātmātmīyarahitaṃ nirīham āyūhaniyūhavigatam anādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanābhiniveśavāsitaṃ traidhātukavicitrarūpopacāropanibaddhaṃ dehabhogapratiṣṭhāgativikalpānugataṃ vikalpyate khyāyate ca
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, how does a bodhisattva great being become skilled in discerning that what is seen is one's own mind? Namely, he examines thus: This triple world is merely one's own mind, without self or what belongs to self, inactive, free from coming and going, perfumed by the latent impressions of attachment to the defects of proliferation from beginningless time, bound to the conventional designation of the variegated forms of the triple world, and followed by discriminations of body, enjoyment, support, and destiny; it is imagined and it appears.

children.text: evaṃ hi mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svacittadṛśyavibhāvanākuśalo bhavati
children.translated_text: In this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a bodhisattva great being becomes skilled in discerning that what is seen is one's own mind.

children.text: kathaṃ punarmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭivivarjito bhavati yaduta māyāsvapnarūpajanmasadṛśāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ svaparobhayābhāvān notpadyante
children.translated_text: And how, <s>Mahāmate</s>, does a bodhisattva great being become free from the view of arising, abiding, and destruction? Namely, all entities are like illusion, dream, and a reflected form; because there is no self, other, or both, they do not arise.

children.text: svacittamātrānusāritvād bāhyabhāvābhāvadarśanād vijñānānāmapravṛttiṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyayānāmakūṭarāśitvaṃ ca vikalpapratyayodbhavaṃ traidhātukaṃ paśyanto 'dhyātmabāhyasarvadharmānupalabdhibhir niḥsvabhāvadarśanād utpādadṛṣṭivinivṛttau māyādidharmasvabhāvānugamād anutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabhante
children.translated_text: Following mind-only, seeing the existence and nonexistence of external things, seeing the non-activity of the consciousnesses, and seeing that conditions are not a gathered heap, they see the triple world as arisen from the conditions of conceptual construction. Through the non-apprehension of all internal and external dharmas and through seeing their absence of own-nature, with the view of arising turned away, and by following the nature of dharmas such as illusion, they attain patience toward the non-arising of dharmas.

Established on the eighth stage, through attaining the reversal of the course of mind, mentation, mental consciousness, the five dharmas, the own-natures, and the twofold selflessness, they obtain the mind-made body.

children.text: mahāmatirāha manomayakāya iti bhagavan kena kāraṇena bhagavānāha manomaya iti mahāmate manovad apratihataśīghragāmitvān manomaya ityucyate
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said, 'Blessed One, why is it called a mind-made body?' The Blessed One said, '<s>Mahāmate</s>, it is called mind-made because, like the mind, it goes swiftly and without obstruction.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate mano'pratihataṃ girikuḍyanadīvṛkṣādiṣvanekāni yojanaśatasahasrāṇi pūrvadṛṣṭānubhūtān viṣayānanusmaran svacittaprabandhāvicchinnaśarīramapratihatagati pravartate evameva mahāmate manomayakāyasahapratilambhena māyopamasamena samādhinā balavaśitābhijñānalakṣaṇakusumitam āryagatinikāyasahajo mana iva pravartate'pratihatagatiḥ pūrvapraṇidhānaviṣayān anusmaran sattvaparipākārtham
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the mind, unobstructed by mountains, walls, rivers, trees, and the like, proceeds through many hundreds of thousands of yojanas, remembering objects formerly seen and experienced, its body an unbroken continuum of its own mind and its movement unobstructed, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, with the simultaneous obtaining of the mind-made body, through a samādhi equal to illusion, flowering with the characteristics of powers, masteries, and superknowledges, born together with the body of the noble course, it proceeds like the mind with unobstructed movement, remembering the objects of former vows, for the purpose of bringing beings to maturity.'

children.text: evaṃ hi mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭivivarjito bhavati
children.translated_text: For in this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the bodhisattva great being becomes free from views of arising, abiding, and dissolution.

children.text: tatra kathaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bāhyabhāvābhāvopalakṣaṇakuśalo bhavati yaduta marīcisvapnakeśoṇḍukaprakhyā mahāmate sarvabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: There, how, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is a bodhisattva great being skilled in recognizing the existence and nonexistence of external entities? It is this: all entities, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are like a mirage, a dream, or a hair-net seen before the eyes.

Seeing that all entities and their own-being are caused by attachment to the latent impressions of discriminations, the varied maturation of the corruption of conceptual proliferation from beginningless time, he longs for the domain of the course of noble knowledge realized within oneself.

children.text: ebhirmahāmate caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti
children.translated_text: Endowed with these four dharmas, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas great beings become great yogins of yoga.
In this, <s>Mahāmate</s>, you should practice yoga.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma deśayatu me bhagavān hetupratyayalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām yena hetupratyayalakṣaṇāvabodhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sadasaddṛṣṭivikalparahitāḥ sarvabhāvanākramaṃ yugapadutpattiṃ na kalpayeyuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One teach me the characteristic of causes and conditions of all dharmas, so that through understanding the characteristic of causes and conditions I and the other bodhisattvas great beings, free from discriminative views of existence and nonexistence, may not imagine the gradual or simultaneous arising of all processes of becoming."

children.text: bhagavānāha dviprakāraṃ mahāmate pratītyasamutpādahetulakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yaduta bāhyaṃ ca ādhyātmikaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "The characteristic of the cause of dependent origination of all dharmas is twofold, <s>Mahāmate</s>: external and internal.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, external dependent origination is as follows.
A pot, <s>Mahāmate</s>, arises through conditions such as a lump of clay, a stick, a wheel, string, water, and human effort.

children.text: yathā ca mahāmate ghaṭo mṛtpiṇḍādeva tantubhyaḥ paṭāḥ vīraṇebhyaḥ kaṭāḥ bījādaṅkuraḥ manthādipuruṣaprayatnayogāddadhno navanīta utpadyate evameva mahāmate bāhyaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pūrvottarottaro draṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: And just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a pot arises from a lump of clay and so on, cloths from threads, mats from reeds, a sprout from a seed, and butter from curds through churning and the application of human effort, so too, <s>Mahāmate</s>, external dependent origination should be understood as proceeding from each prior condition to the next.

children.text: tatra ādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādo yaduta avidyā tṛṣṇā karmetyevamādyā mahāmate dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpādasaṃjñāṃ pratilabhante
children.translated_text: There, internal dependent origination is this: dharmas such as ignorance, craving, and karma, <s>Mahāmate</s>, receive the name dependent origination.

children.text: ebhya utpannā mahāmate skandhadhātvāyatanākhyā dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpādasaṃjñāṃ pratilabhante
children.translated_text: The dharmas called aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, which arise from these, <s>Mahāmate</s>, receive the name dependent origination.
Yet they are not distinct, though they are imagined by fools.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, cause is sixfold.

children.text: yaduta bhaviṣyaddhetuḥ saṃbandhaheturlakṣaṇahetuḥ kāraṇahetur vyañjanahetur upekṣāhetur mahāmate ṣaṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Namely, <s>Mahāmate</s>: future cause, connection cause, characteristic cause, instrumental cause, manifesting cause, and, as the sixth, indifference cause.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the future cause performs the function of a cause in the arising of internal and external dharmas.
The connection cause, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, performs the function of an objective support in the arising of internal and external things such as the aggregates and seeds.
The characteristic cause, moreover, <s>Mahāmate</s>, produces what is bound to the characteristic of immediately subsequent activity.
The instrumental cause, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, performs the function of authority and predominance, like a wheel-turning king.

children.text: vyañjanahetuḥ punarmahāmate utpannasya vikalpasya bhāvasya lakṣaṇoddyotanakṛtyaṃ karoti pradīpavadrūpādīnām
children.translated_text: The manifesting cause, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, performs the function of illuminating the characteristics of an entity whose discrimination has arisen, like a lamp illuminating forms and the like.
The indifference cause, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, at the time of cessation effects the cutting off of the activity of continuity when non-discrimination arises.

children.text: ete hi mahāmate svavikalpakalpitā bālapṛthagjanairna kramavṛttyā na yugapatpravartante
children.translated_text: These, <s>Mahāmate</s>, imagined by fools and ordinary people through their own discrimination, do not operate either in sequential occurrence or simultaneously.

children.text: tat kasya hetoḥ yadi punarmahāmate yugapatpravarteran kāryakāraṇavibhāgo na syād apratilabdhahetulakṣaṇatvāt
children.translated_text: Why is that? If, <s>Mahāmate</s>, they operated simultaneously, there would be no division between effect and cause, because the characteristic of cause would not have been obtained.

children.text: atha kramavṛttyā pravarteran alabdhasya lakṣaṇātmakatvātkramavṛttyā na pravartate
children.translated_text: But if they operated sequentially, since what has not been obtained has no characteristic nature, they do not operate sequentially.
Like the words "father" and "son" in the case of an unborn son, <s>Mahāmate</s>, they do not fit together through a relation of sequential occurrence.

According to the logicians, things do not arise sequentially, <s>Mahāmate</s>, through being generated and generating by means of causal condition, object condition, immediately preceding condition, predominant condition, and so on.
They do not arise simultaneously, <s>Mahāmate</s>, because their characteristic is attachment to imagined own-nature.

children.text: svacittadṛśyadehabhogapraviṣṭhānatvāt svasāmānyalakṣaṇabāhyabhāvābhāvān mahāmate krameṇa yugapadvā notpadyante
children.translated_text: Since body, enjoyment, and abode are entered into as what is seen by one's own mind, and since external entities with their particular and shared characteristics do not exist, <s>Mahāmate</s>, they do not arise either sequentially or simultaneously.
Rather, consciousness proceeds because it is conceptually constructed by discrimination as what is seen by one's own mind.
Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, you must be free from the views of the characteristic of causal and conditional activity as sequential or simultaneous.
On this point it is said:
Nothing here arises through conditions, nor is anything brought to cessation.
The conditions themselves, imagined, are what arise and cease.
The defilement of dissolution and arising among conditions is not what is prevented;

children.text: yatra bālā vikalpanti pratyayaiḥ sa nivāryate ||
children.translated_text: what is prevented is that in which fools discriminate by means of conditions.
And since among conditions there is no arising of dharmas from what is nonexistent,
because mind, confused by latent impressions, appears in the three realms,
nothing is born after not having existed, nor is anything obstructed by conditions.
When they see the conditioned as the son of a barren woman or as a flower in the sky,

children.text: tadā grāhaśca grāhyaṃ ca bhrāntiṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate ||
children.translated_text: then, having seen grasping and the grasped as delusion, they turn away.

children.text: na cotpādya na cotpannaḥ pratyayo'pi na kiṃcana
children.translated_text: There is nothing produced, nothing arisen; nor is there any condition at all.
No things are found anywhere; it is only convention that is spoken of."

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocad deśayatu me bhagavān vāgvikalpalakṣaṇahṛdayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ yena vāgvikalpalakṣaṇahṛdayena bhagavan suprativibhāgavinibaddhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā abhilāpābhilāpyārthadvayagatiṃgatāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya abhilāpābhilāpyārthadvayagatiṃ sarvasattvānāṃ viśodhayeyuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One teach me the Dharma discourse called the heart of the characteristics of verbal discrimination. Blessed One, when that heart of the characteristics of verbal discrimination has been well analyzed and set forth, I and the other bodhisattvas great beings, having gone beyond the twofold course of expression and what is expressible, may quickly awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening and purify for all beings the twofold course of expression and what is expressible."

children.text: bhagavānāha tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, listen, and attend carefully and well.
I shall explain it to you."

children.text: sādhu bhagavan iti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt
children.translated_text: "Good, Blessed One," the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this to him: "There are four kinds of characteristic of verbal discrimination, <s>Mahāmate</s>.
Namely: speech of characteristics, speech of dreams, speech attached to discriminations of corruption, and speech of beginningless discrimination.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, speech of characteristics proceeds from attachment to signs as forms of one's own discrimination.
Dream-speech, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from recollection of objects formerly experienced and from the absence of objects on awakening.
Speech attached to discriminations of corruption, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from recollection of acts formerly done by an enemy.

Speech of beginningless-time discrimination, again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds from the latent impressions, as its own seeds, of the corruption consisting in attachment to proliferation from beginningless time.

children.text: etaddhi mahāmate caturvidhaṃ vāgvikalpalakṣaṇamiti me yaduktam idaṃ tatpratyuktam
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is what I had in mind when I spoke of the fourfold characteristic of verbal discrimination; this has now been explained."

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametamevārthamadhyeṣate sma deśayatu me bhagavān punarapi vāgvikalpābhivyaktigocaram
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One about this very matter: "May the Blessed One teach me further the domain in which verbal discrimination becomes manifest.

children.text: kutra kasmāt kathaṃ kena bhagavan nṛṇāṃ vāgvijñaptivikalpaḥ pravartate bhagavānāha śira uronāsākaṇṭhatālvoṣṭhajihvādantasamavāyān mahāmate vāk pravartamānā pravartate
children.translated_text: Where, from what, how, and by what, Blessed One, does men's discriminative communication of speech proceed?" The Blessed One said: "Speech, <s>Mahāmate</s>, proceeds as it proceeds from the conjunction of head, breast, nose, throat, palate, lips, tongue, and teeth."

children.text: mahāmatirāha kiṃ punarbhagavan vāg vikalpādanyā uta ananyā bhagavānāha na hi mahāmate vāg vikalpādanyā nānanyā
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said, "Blessed One, is speech different from discrimination, or is it not different?" The Blessed One said, "No, <s>Mahāmate</s>, speech is neither different from discrimination nor not different.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yaduta taddhetūtpattilakṣaṇatvānmahāmate vāgvikalpaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: Why is that? Namely, because their characteristic is to arise from the same cause, <s>Mahāmate</s>; verbal discrimination proceeds.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate vāg vikalpādanyā syāt avikalpahetukī syāt
children.translated_text: If, <s>Mahāmate</s>, speech were different from discrimination, it would have non-discrimination as its cause.

children.text: athānanyā syāt arthābhivyaktitvād vāṅ na kuryāt
children.translated_text: But if it were not different, since it manifests meaning, speech would not perform its function.
Yet it does perform it.
Therefore it is neither different nor not different.

children.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha kiṃ punarbhagavan vacanameva paramārthaḥ uta yadvacanenābhilapyate sa paramārthaḥ bhagavānāha na mahāmate vacanaṃ paramārthaḥ na ca yadvacanenābhilapyate sa paramārthaḥ
children.translated_text: Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said, "Blessed One, is speech itself ultimate truth, or is that which is expressed by speech ultimate truth?" The Blessed One said, "No, <s>Mahāmate</s>, speech is not ultimate truth, nor is that which is expressed by speech ultimate truth.

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ yaduta paramārthāryasukhābhilāpapraveśitvāt paramārthasya vacanaṃ na paramārthaḥ
children.translated_text: Why is that? Namely, because speech about ultimate truth enters into the expression of the noble happiness of ultimate truth, but speech is not ultimate truth.
Rather, <s>Mahāmate</s>, ultimate truth is accessible through the inner realization of noble knowledge; it is not the domain of verbal discrimination or intellect.
Therefore discrimination does not bring ultimate truth to manifestation.
Speech, moreover, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is produced and then destroyed, unstable, arisen from mutually conditioning causes and conditions.
And what, <s>Mahāmate</s>, has arisen from mutually conditioning causes and conditions does not bring ultimate truth to manifestation.
Because there is no characteristic of self and other, <s>Mahāmate</s>, it does not bring an external characteristic to manifestation.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate svacittadṛśyamātrānusāritvād vividhavicitralakṣaṇabāhyabhāvābhāvād vāgvikalpaḥ paramārthaṃ na vikalpayati
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, because verbal discrimination follows only what is seen by one's own mind, and because external entities with their many variegated characteristics do not exist, verbal discrimination does not conceive ultimate truth.

children.text: tasmāttarhi mahāmate vāgvicitrā vikalparahitena te bhavitavyam
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, since speech is variegated, you must be free from discrimination.
On this point it is said:
Every existent is without own-being; true speech is likewise unreal.
Not seeing the meaning of emptiness and non-emptiness, the fool runs about.
The own-being of all existents, and the speech of human beings too,
is imagination; that too does not exist. Nirvāṇa is like a dream.

children.text: bhavaṃ parīkṣeta na saṃsāre nāpi nirvāyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should examine becoming: one should neither remain in saṃsāra nor pass into nirvāṇa.
Just as a king or wealthy merchant, with various clay deer,

children.text: pralobhya krīḍayitvā ca bhūtān dadyāttato mṛgān ||
children.translated_text: after enticing and amusing his sons, would then give them real deer,
so I, through the varied characteristics that are reflections of dharmas,
teach to my sons the limit of reality, to be known inwardly by oneself."

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat deśayatu me bhagavān nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayanobhayanaivāstinanāstinityānityavarjitaṃ sarvatīrthyāgatipracāram āryapratyātmajñānagatigamyaṃ parikalpitasvasāmānyalakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ paramārthatattvāvatāraṃ bhūmyanusaṃdhikramottarottaraviśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ tathāgatabhūmyanupraveśalakṣaṇam anābhogapūrvapraṇidhānaviśvarūpamaṇisadṛśaviṣayānantalakṣaṇapracārasvacittadṛśyagocaragativibhāgalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One teach me the entry into the reality of ultimate truth, which is free from nonexistence, existence, oneness, otherness, both, neither, neither-existence-nor-nonexistence, permanence, and impermanence; which is not the course reached by all non-Buddhist teachers; which is accessible through the course of noble inner knowledge; which is devoid of imagined particular and shared characteristics; whose character is the successive higher and higher purification in connection with the stages; whose character is entry into the stage of a tathāgata; whose characteristic is the activity of limitless objects resembling a wish-fulfilling jewel of effortless former vows and varied forms; and whose characteristic is the distinction of the course of the domain seen by one's own mind among all dharmas."

children.text: yathā ca ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā evamādiṣu parikalpitasvabhāvasvasāmānyalakṣaṇavinivṛttadṛṣṭayaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaguṇasaṃpattīḥ paripūrayema
children.translated_text: And may I and the other bodhisattvas great beings, whose views regarding the particular and shared characteristics of imagined own-nature have ceased in such matters, quickly awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening and fulfill all excellences for all beings.

children.text: bhagavānāha sādhu sādhu mahāmate sādhu khalu punastvaṃ mahāmate yattvametamartham adhyeṣitavyaṃ manyase
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Good, good, <s>Mahāmate</s>; it is indeed good, <s>Mahāmate</s>, that you think this matter should be requested.

children.text: bahujanahitāya tvaṃ mahāmate pratipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca
children.translated_text: You have set out, <s>Mahāmate</s>, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great mass of people, of gods and humans.

children.text: tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, listen, and attend carefully and well.
I shall speak to you."
"Good, Blessed One," the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> replied to the Blessed One.
He listened.

children.text: bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhānmahāmate bālapṛthagjanā bāhyavicitrabhāvābhiniveśena ca nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayanaivāstinanāstinityānityasvabhāvavāsanāhetuvikalpābhiniveśena vikalpayanti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this to him: "Because they do not understand that what is seen is only their own mind, <s>Mahāmate</s>, childish ordinary people discriminate through attachment to the variegated external entities and through attachment to conceptual constructions caused by latent impressions of views of nonexistence and existence, unity and difference, both and neither existence nor nonexistence, permanence and impermanence, and own-nature.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate mṛgatṛṣṇodakaṃ mṛgā udakabhāvena vikalpya grīṣmābhitaptāḥ pātukāmatayā pradhāvanti svacittadṛṣṭibhrāntyanavabodhānna prajānanti nātrodakamiti evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanā anādikālavividhaprapañcavikalpavāsitamatayo rāgadveṣamohāgnitāpitamanaso vicitrarūpaviṣayābhilāṣiṇaḥ utpādabhaṅgasthitidṛṣṭyāśayā ādhyātmikabāhyabhāvābhāvākuśalāḥ
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, deer scorched by summer heat, imagining the water of a mirage to be water, run toward it in their wish to drink; because they do not understand the confusion of what is seen by their own mind, they do not know, 'There is no water here.' Just so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, childish ordinary people, whose minds have been perfumed from beginningless time by many kinds of proliferating discrimination, whose minds are burned by the fires of attachment, aversion, and delusion, who long for objects of various forms, whose dispositions are fixed on views of arising, destruction, and abiding, and who are unskilled in the existence and nonexistence of internal and external entities,
fall into grasping at unity and difference, nonexistence and existence.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate gandharvanagare'viduṣām anagare nagarasaṃjñā bhavati
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, in a city of gandharvas, among the ignorant, the notion of a city arises where there is no city.
And that city-shape appears because of attachment to the latent impressions of city-seeds from beginningless time.
Yet that city is neither a non-city nor a city.

Just so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those who are attached to the latent impressions of non-Buddhist doctrines of proliferation from beginningless time become attached to doctrines of unity and difference, existence and nonexistence, their minds not having ascertained that what is seen is only their own mind.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate kaścideva puruṣaḥ śayitaḥ svapnāntare strīpuruṣahastyaśvarathapadātigrāmanagaranigamagomahiṣavanodyānavividhagirinadītaḍāgopaśobhitaṃ janapadam antaḥpuraṃ praviśya prativibudhyeta
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, some man, while sleeping, might in a dream enter a country and a royal inner palace adorned with women and men, elephants, horses, chariots, infantry, villages, cities, market-towns, cows, buffaloes, forests, parks, various mountains, rivers, and ponds, and then wake up.

children.text: sa prativibuddhaḥ saṃs tadeva janapadamantaḥpuraṃ samanusmaret
children.translated_text: When awakened, he would recollect that very country and inner palace.

children.text: tatkiṃ manyase mahāmate api nu sa puruṣaḥ paṇḍitajātīyo bhavet yastadabhūtaṃ svapnavaicitryam anusmaret āha no hīdaṃ bhagavan
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Mahāmate</s>? Would that man be of a wise sort if he recollected that unreal variety of dream?" He said, "Certainly not, Blessed One."

children.text: bhagavānāha evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭidaṣṭāstīrthyamatayaḥ svapnatulyātsvacittadṛśyabhāvānna prativijānante ekatvānyatvanāstyastitvadṛṣṭiṃ samāśrayante
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Just so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, childish ordinary people, bitten by wrong views and whose minds are those of non-Buddhists, do not recognize entities seen by their own mind as being like a dream, and they rely on views of unity and difference, nonexistence and existence.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate citrakarakṛtapradeśā animnonnatāḥ santo nimnonnatā bālaiḥ kalpyante evameva mahāmate bhaviṣyantyanāgate'dhvani tīrthyadṛṣṭivāsanāśayaprativikalpapuṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, painted surfaces made by a painter, though not depressed or raised, are imagined by fools to be depressed and raised. Just so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, in a future time there will be those nourished by the discriminations of dispositions formed by latent impressions of non-Buddhist views.

children.text: te ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayavādābhiniviṣṭāḥ svayaṃ naṣṭā anyānapi sadasatpakṣaviviktānutpādavādino nāstikā iti vakṣyanti
children.translated_text: Attached to doctrines of unity and difference, both and neither, they themselves will be ruined and will call nihilists even those who teach non-arising, free from the positions of existent and nonexistent.
They deny cause and effect; their roots of good and pure qualities have been uprooted, and they are hard to see rightly.

children.text: ete śreyo'rthibhir dūrataḥ parivarjyā iti vakṣyante
children.translated_text: Those seeking the highest good should avoid them from afar, it will be said.

And they, whose dispositions have fallen into views of self, other, or both, whose dispositions have fallen into wrong views that superimpose and deny through discriminations of nonexistence and existence, will be destined for hell.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate taimirikāḥ keśoṇḍukaṃ dṛṣṭvā parasparam ācakṣate idaṃ citramidaṃ citramiti paśyantu bho mārṣāḥ
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, people with eye disease, seeing a hair-net, say to one another, 'This is wonderful, this is wonderful; look, good sirs!'

children.text: tacca keśoṇḍukam ubhayānutpannatayā na bhāvo nābhāvo darśanādarśanataḥ
children.translated_text: But that hair-net, because it is unarisen in both respects, is neither an entity nor a nonentity, in terms of seeing and not seeing.

children.text: evam eva mahāmate tīrthyakudṛṣṭivikalpāśayābhiniviṣṭāḥ sadasatpakṣaikatvānyatvobhayānubhayatvavādābhiniviṣṭāḥ saddharmāpavādakā ātmānaṃ parāṃśca vinipātayiṣyanti
children.translated_text: In the same way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those attached to the dispositions of conceptual wrong views of non-Buddhists, attached to positions of existent and nonexistent, unity and difference, both and neither, slandering the true Dharma, will bring themselves and others to ruin.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate acakramalātacakraṃ bālaiścakrabhāvena parikalpyate na paṇḍitaiḥ evameva mahāmate kudṛṣṭitīrthyāśayapatitā ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayatvaṃ parikalpayiṣyanti sarvabhāvotpattau
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a firebrand with no wheel is imagined by fools as a wheel, but not by the wise. Just so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those who have fallen into the dispositions of wrong non-Buddhist views will imagine unity and difference, both and neither, in the arising of all entities.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate deve pravarṣati jalabudbudakāḥ sphaṭikamaṇisadṛśāḥ khyāyante
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, when rain is falling from the sky, water bubbles appear like crystal gems.

children.text: tatra ca bālāḥ sphaṭikamaṇibhāvam abhiniveśya pradhāvanti
children.translated_text: There fools, becoming attached to the idea that they are crystal gems, run toward them.

children.text: te ca mahāmate udakabudbudakā na maṇayo nāmaṇayo grahaṇāgrahaṇataḥ
children.translated_text: But those water bubbles, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are neither gems nor non-gems, in terms of grasping and non-grasping.

children.text: evameva mahāmate tīrthyadṛṣṭivikalpāśayavāsanāvāsitā asataścotpādaṃ varṇayiṣyanti pratyayaiḥ sataśca vināśam ||
children.translated_text: Just so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those perfumed by the latent impressions of dispositions that discriminate according to non-Buddhist views will describe the arising of what is nonexistent through conditions and the destruction of what is existent."

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate pramāṇatrayāvayavapratyavasthānaṃ kṛtvā āryajñānapratyātmādhigamyaṃ svabhāvadvayavinirmuktaṃ vastu svabhāvato vidyata iti vikalpayiṣyanti
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, after setting up the establishment of the three means of valid cognition and their members, they will imagine that a thing, to be realized inwardly by noble knowledge and free from the two own-natures, exists by its own nature.

children.text: na ca mahāmate cittamanomanovijñānacittaparāvṛttyāśrayāṇāṃ svacittadṛśyagrāhyagrāhakavikalpaprahīṇānāṃ tathāgatabhūmipratyātmāryajñānagatānāṃ yogināṃ bhāvābhāvasaṃjñā pravartate
children.translated_text: But, <s>Mahāmate</s>, for yogins whose basis has been transformed in mind, mentation, mental consciousness, and thought, who have abandoned discrimination of grasped and grasper as what is seen by their own mind, and who have entered the tathāgata stage through noble knowledge realized inwardly, no notion of existence or nonexistence proceeds.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate yoginām evaṃgativiṣayāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvagrāhaḥ pravartate sa evaiṣāmātmagrāhaḥ poṣagrāhaḥ puruṣagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāhaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: If, however, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a grasping at existence and nonexistence proceeds for yogins whose domain has such a course, that very thing would be their grasping at self, their grasping at a nourished being, their grasping at a person, and their grasping at a pudgala.

children.text: yā punareva mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvasvasāmānyalakṣaṇadeśanā eṣā mahāmate nairmāṇikabuddhadeśanā na dharmatābuddhadeśanā
children.translated_text: And, <s>Mahāmate</s>, whatever teaching there is about the own-being of entities and their particular and shared characteristics, that, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the teaching of a magically created Buddha, not the teaching of the dharmatā-Buddha.

children.text: deśanā punarmahāmate bālāśayagatadṛṣṭipravṛttā na ca pratyavasthānagatisvabhāvadharmāryajñānapratyātmādhigamasamādhisukhavihāram udbhāvayati
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Mahāmate</s>, teaching proceeds in accordance with the views that have entered the dispositions of fools, but it does not disclose the happy abiding of samādhi that is the inward realization by noble knowledge of the nature of dharmas whose course is beyond assertion.
For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the shadow of a tree appears in water.

children.text: sā ca na chāyā nāchāyā vṛkṣasaṃsthānāsaṃsthānataḥ evameva mahāmate tīrthyadṛṣṭivāsanāvāsitavikalpā ekatvānyatvobhayatvānubhayatvanāstyastitvaṃ vikalpayiṣyanti svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāritamatayaḥ
children.translated_text: And it is neither shadow nor non-shadow, because of the tree's having and not having a form there. In just this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, those whose discriminations are perfumed by the latent impressions of non-Buddhist views will imagine unity, difference, both, neither, nonexistence, and existence, their minds not ascertaining that there is only what is seen by their own mind.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate darpaṇāntargatāni sarvarūpapratibimbakāni khyāyante yathā pratyayataḥ svavikalpanācca na tāni bimbāni nābimbāni bimbābimbadarśanataḥ
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, all reflected images of forms appear inside a mirror, according to conditions and one's own discrimination; yet they are neither images nor non-images, because image and non-image are seen.

children.text: atha ca te mahāmate svacittadṛśyavikalpāḥ khyāyante bālānāṃ bimbākṛtayaḥ
children.translated_text: And yet, <s>Mahāmate</s>, these discriminations of what is seen by one's own mind appear to fools as forms of images.
In just this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, reflections of one's own mind appear in the form of views of unity, difference, both, and neither.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate pratiśrutkā puruṣanadīpavanasaṃyogāt pravartamānā anuśrūyate
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, an echo, arising from the conjunction of a person, a river, and wind, is heard.

children.text: sā ca na bhāvā nābhāvā ghoṣāghoṣaśravaṇataḥ evameva mahāmate nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayanobhayadṛṣṭisvacittavāsanāvikalpāḥ khyāyante
children.translated_text: And it is neither existent nor nonexistent, because sound and non-sound are heard. In just this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, discriminations from latent impressions in one's own mind, namely the views of nonexistence, existence, unity, difference, both, and neither, appear.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate nistṛṇagulmalatāvanāyāṃ medinyām ādityasaṃyogānmṛgatṛṣṇikāstaraṃgavat syandante
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, on the earth where there is no grass, bush, creeper, or forest, through contact with the sun, masses of mirage flow like waves.

children.text: te ca na bhāvā nābhāvā lobhyālobhyataḥ
children.translated_text: And they are neither existent nor nonexistent, because they are both enticing and not enticing.

children.text: evameva mahāmate bālānām anādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanāvāsitaṃ vikalpavijñānam utpādasthitibhaṅgaikatvānyatvobhayānubhayanāstyastyāryapratyātmajñānavastumukhena mṛgatṛṣṇikāvat taraṅgāyate
children.translated_text: In just this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the discriminating consciousness of fools, perfumed by the latent impression of the roughness of conceptual proliferation from beginningless time, ripples like a mirage with regard to the object of noble knowledge realized inwardly, as arising, abiding, destruction, unity, difference, both, neither, nonexistence, and existence.

children.text: tadyathā mahāmate vetālayantrapuruṣau niḥsattvau piśācayuktiyogāt spandanakriyāṃ kurvāte
children.translated_text: For example, <s>Mahāmate</s>, a vetāla and a mechanical man, though without any living being in them, perform movements and actions through the application of a demonic contrivance.

children.text: tatra ca asadvikalpe bālā abhiniviśante gamanāgamanataḥ
children.translated_text: There fools become attached to unreal discrimination because of going and coming.

children.text: evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭitīrthyāśayapatitā ekatvānyatvavādān abhiniviśante
children.translated_text: In just this way, <s>Mahāmate</s>, foolish ordinary people, fallen into the dispositions of bad views and non-Buddhists, become attached to doctrines of unity and difference.
And that is an unreal superimposition.

Therefore, then, <s>Mahāmate</s>, one should be free from discrimination regarding the inward realization of the noble object as arising, abiding, destruction, unity, difference, both, neither, nonexistence, and existence.
On this point it is said:
The aggregates, with consciousness as the fifth, are like the shadow of a tree in water.
Seen as like illusion and dream, one should not discriminate them as representation.
This is like a hair-net, from the confusion of mirage-water;
seeing the threefold existence as called dream and illusion, one is liberated.
As a mirage in summer shimmers, bewildering the mind,

children.text: mṛgā gṛhṇanti pānīyaṃ na cāsyāṃ vastu vidyate ||
children.translated_text: deer grasp at it as water, but no real thing exists in it.
So indeed the seed of consciousness shimmers in the field of vision;

children.text: bālā gṛhṇanti jāyantaṃ timiraṃ taimirā yathā ||
children.translated_text: fools grasp it as being born, like those with diseased eyes grasp darkness.
In saṃsāra with its beginningless course, one is enfolded by grasping at existence.

children.text: bālaḥ kīle yathā kīlaṃ pralobhya vinivartayet ||
children.translated_text: A fool, as with a peg, should draw out a peg after enticing it away.
Always see the world as like illusion, a vetāla, a machine, dream, lightning, and a cloud,
cut off from the three continuities; seeing it so, one is liberated.
For here there is no representation at all, just as there are no mirage-rays in the sky.
Knowing dharmas in this way, they assert nothing at all.
This so-called representation is merely a name; it does not exist by way of characteristic.
The aggregates are of the form of hair-nets, where that representation is imagined.

children.text: cittaṃ keśoṇḍukaṃ māyā svapnaṃ gandharvameva ca
children.translated_text: Mind appears to human beings as hair-net, illusion, dream, a gandharva-city,

children.text: alātaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇā ca asantaḥ khyāti vai nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: a firebrand-wheel, and a mirage, although these are nonexistent.
Eternal and non-eternal, likewise unity, both, and neither:
because of connection with beginningless fault, fools, deluded, imagine these.

children.text: darpaṇe udake netre bhāṇḍeṣu ca maṇīṣu ca
children.translated_text: In a mirror, in water, in the eye, in vessels, and in jewels,

children.text: bimbaṃ hi dṛśyate teṣu bimbaṃ nāsti ca kutracid ||
children.translated_text: an image is seen in them, yet nowhere is there any image.

children.text: bhāvābhāsaṃ tathā cittaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇā yathā nabhe
children.translated_text: So too the mind, an appearance of existence, is like a mirage in the sky;
it is seen in variegated form, like the son of a barren woman in a dream.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate catuṣṭayavinirmuktā tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanā yaduta ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayapakṣavivarjitā nāstyastisamāropāpavādavinirmuktā
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the tathāgatas' teaching of the dharma is free from the four alternatives: it is devoid of the positions of unity, difference, both, and neither, and free from the superimposition and denial of nonexistence and existence.
The teaching of the dharma by the Tathāgatas, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is preceded by the practice of the cessation of unreal dependent origination, the path, and liberation.
The teaching of the dharma by the Tathāgatas, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is not bound up with nature, a lord as creator, cause, chance, atoms, time, or inherent being.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate kleśajñeyāvaraṇadvayaviśuddhyarthaṃ sārthavāhavadānupūrvyā aṣṭottare nirābhāsapadaśate pratiṣṭhāpayanti yānabhūmyaṅgasuvibhāgalakṣaṇe ca
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, for the sake of purifying the two obscurations, the afflictive and the knowable, like caravan leaders they gradually establish beings in the hundred and eight imageless states, and in the well-divided characteristics of the vehicles, stages, and limbs.
Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, meditation is fourfold.

children.text: katamaccaturvidham yaduta bālopacārikaṃ dhyānam arthapravicayaṃ dhyānam tathatālambanaṃ dhyānam tāthāgataṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam
children.translated_text: What is the fourfold kind? Namely, the meditation practiced by the foolish, the meditation that investigates meaning, the meditation whose support is suchness, and the fourth, Tathāgata-meditation.

children.text: tatra mahāmate bālopacārikaṃ dhyānaṃ katamat yaduta śrāvakapratyekabuddhayogayogināṃ pudgalanairātmyabhāvasvasāmānyabimbasaṃkalānityaduḥkhāśubhalakṣaṇābhiniveśapūrvakam evamidaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nānyatheti paśyataḥ pūrvottarottarata ā saṃjñānirodhād bālopacārikaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the meditation practiced by the foolish? It is that of yogins who practice the yoga of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas: preceded by clinging to the absence of a personal self, to the images of particular and common features of things, and to the marks of impermanence, suffering, and impurity, they see, 'This characteristic is thus and not otherwise.' Progressing from former to later and still later stages up to the cessation of perception, it becomes the meditation practiced by the foolish.

children.text: tatra arthapravicayadhyānaṃ punarmahāmate katamat yaduta pudgalanairātmyasvasāmānyalakṣaṇabāhyatīrthakarasvaparobhayābhāvaṃ kṛtvā dharmanairātmyabhūmilakṣaṇārthaṃ pravicayānupūrvakam arthapravicayadhyānaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what again is the meditation that investigates meaning? Having set aside the particular and common characteristics of the absence of a personal self, and the nonexistence of self, other, or both as maintained by outside tīrthikas, it becomes the meditation that investigates meaning through gradual examination of the meaning of the characteristic of the stage of the selflessness of dharmas.

children.text: tatra tathatālambanaṃ dhyānaṃ mahāmate katamat yaduta parikalpitanairātmyadvayavikalpayathābhūtāvasthānād apravṛtter vikalpasya tathatālambanamiti vadāmi
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is the meditation whose support is suchness? Because the imagination of the twofold selflessness, falsely constructed, abides as it really is, and because discrimination does not proceed, I call it meditation whose support is suchness.

children.text: tāthāgataṃ punarmahāmate dhyānaṃ katamat yaduta tāthāgatabhūmyākārapraveśaṃ pratyātmāryajñānalakṣaṇatrayasukhavihārācintyasattvakṛtyakaraṇatayā tāthāgataṃ dhyānamiti vadāmi
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, what is Tathāgata-meditation? I call it Tathāgata-meditation because it enters the mode of the Tathāgata-stage, because it is a happy abiding in the three characteristics of noble knowledge realized within oneself, and because it carries out the inconceivable works for beings.
On this point this is said:
Meditation that investigates meaning, and meditation practiced by the foolish;
meditation whose support is suchness, and the excellent Tathāgata-meditation.
A yogin practicing yoga sees appearances like the moon and sun,
like a lotus, like the underworld, like the sky, fire, and painted forms.

children.text: nimittāni ca citrāṇi tīrthamārgaṃ nayanti te
children.translated_text: These varied signs lead them onto the path of the tīrthikas;
they fall into śrāvaka-hood and into the sphere of the pratyekajinas.
When, having shaken off all these, one becomes imageless,
then the Buddhas, suns with rays, gathered from all fields,

children.text: śiro hi tasya mārjanti nimittaṃ tathatānugam ||
children.translated_text: stroke that one's head: this is the sign that follows suchness.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantam etadavocat nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇamiti bhagavannucyate
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva great being <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, it is said, "nirvāṇa, nirvāṇa."

children.text: kasyaitadbhagavannadhivacanaṃ yaduta nirvāṇamiti bhagavānāha sarvavijñānasvabhāvavāsanālayamanomanovijñānadṛṣṭivāsanāparāvṛttir nirvāṇamityucyate sarvabuddhair mayā ca nirvāṇagatisvabhāvaśūnyatāvastugocaram
children.translated_text: Blessed One, of what is this a designation, namely "nirvāṇa"?' The Blessed One said: 'The reversal of the latent impressions of the own-nature of all consciousnesses, of the storehouse, mentation, mental consciousness, views, and habits, is called nirvāṇa by all Buddhas and by me; it is the object-domain whose nature is the emptiness of the course of nirvāṇa.

Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, nirvāṇa is the object-domain of the course realized personally by noble knowledge, free from the discriminations of eternalism and annihilationism, existence and nonexistence.

children.text: kathaṃ na śāśvatam yaduta svasāmānyalakṣaṇavikalpaprahīṇam ato na śāśvatam
children.translated_text: How is it not eternal? Since discrimination of particular and common characteristics is abandoned, it is therefore not eternal.

children.text: tatrānucchedo yaduta sarvārthā atītānāgatapratyutpannāḥ pratyātmamapi gacchanti ato nocchedaḥ
children.translated_text: And there is no annihilation here, because all things of the past, future, and present are reached even in personal realization; therefore there is no annihilation.

children.text: punarmahāmate mahāparinirvāṇaṃ na nāśo na maraṇam
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, great parinirvāṇa is neither destruction nor death.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate mahāparinirvāṇaṃ maraṇaṃ syāt punarapi janmaprabandhaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: For if, <s>Mahāmate</s>, great parinirvāṇa were death, there would again be a continuity of birth.
If it were destruction, it would fall under the characteristic of what is conditioned.

children.text: ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate mahāparinirvāṇaṃ na nāśaṃ na maraṇam
children.translated_text: For this reason, <s>Mahāmate</s>, great parinirvāṇa is neither destruction nor death.
Yogins attain death that is free from falling away.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate mahāparinirvāṇam aprahīṇāsaṃprāptito 'nucchedāśāśvatato naikārthato nānārthato nirvāṇamityucyate
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, great parinirvāṇa is called nirvāṇa because it is not something abandoned or acquired, because it is not annihilation and not eternal, and because it is neither one meaning nor many meanings.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nirvāṇaṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇāvabodhād asaṃsargataḥ
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the nirvāṇa of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas comes from awakening to particular and common characteristics and from non-association.
Because they see objects without inversion, discrimination does not proceed.
Therefore they form the idea of nirvāṇa there.

children.text: punar aparaṃ mahāmate dviprakāraṃ svabhāvadvayalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the characteristic of the twofold nature is of two kinds.
What is the twofold kind? Namely, attachment to the nature of verbal expression and attachment to the nature of objects.
There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, attachment to the nature of verbal expression proceeds from attachment to the latent impressions of verbal proliferation from beginningless time.

children.text: tatra vastusvabhāvābhiniveśaḥ punar mahāmate svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhāt pravartate
children.translated_text: Again, <s>Mahāmate</s>, attachment to the nature of objects proceeds from not understanding that what is seen is only one's own mind.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate adhiṣṭhānadvayādhiṣṭhitā bodhisattvāstathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ caraṇayornipatya praśnān paripṛcchanti
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas, sustained by two kinds of sustaining power, fall at the feet of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones and ask questions.

By what two kinds of sustaining power are they sustained? Namely, by the sustaining power of samādhi and attainment, and by the sustaining power of consecration through the body, mouth, and hand of all Tathāgatas.

children.text: tatra mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prathamāyāṃ bhūmau buddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpadyante
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas great beings on the first stage, empowered by the empowerment of the Buddhas, enter the bodhisattva samādhi called the Light of the Great Vehicle.

children.text: samanantarasamāpannānāṃ ca teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ bodhisattvasamādhim atha daśadiglokadhātuvyavasthitāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā mukhānyupadarśya sarvakāyamukhavācāsaṃdarśanenādhiṣṭhānaṃ kurvanti
children.translated_text: And immediately after those bodhisattvas great beings have entered the bodhisattva samādhi called the Light of the Great Vehicle, the tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened ones, established in the world-realms of the ten directions, show their faces and bestow empowerment through the manifestation of the speech from the mouths of their whole bodies.

children.text: yathā mahāmate vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anyeṣāṃ ca tādṛglakṣaṇaguṇasamanvāgatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām evaṃ mahāmate prathamāyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ samādhisamāpattyadhiṣṭhānaṃ pratilabhante
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mahāmate</s>, for the bodhisattva great being <s>Vajragarbha</s> and for other bodhisattvas great beings endowed with such marks and qualities, so, <s>Mahāmate</s>, on the first stage bodhisattvas great beings obtain the empowerment connected with entering samādhi.

children.text: kalpaśatasahasraṃ saṃcitaiḥ kuśalamūlairanupūrveṇa bhūmipakṣavipakṣalakṣaṇagatiṃgatā dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau mahāpadmavimānāsanasthasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tadanurūpair bodhisattvair mahāsattvaiḥ parivṛtasya sarvaratnābharaṇavibhūṣitakirīṭasya haritālakanakacampakacandrāṃśumayūkhapadmasadṛśā daśadiglokadhātvāgatā jinakarāstasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya padmavimānāsanasthasya mūrdhanyabhiṣiñcanti vaśavarticakravartīndrarājavat sarvakāyamukhapāṇyabhiṣekena
children.translated_text: After hundreds of thousands of kalpas, through accumulated roots of merit, having gradually reached the course that knows the characteristics of what belongs to the stages and what opposes them, on the bodhisattva stage called Cloud of Dharma, the victorious ones' rays, come from the world-realms of the ten directions and resembling orpiment, gold, campaka blossoms, moonbeams, and lotuses, anoint the crown of that bodhisattva great being who is seated on the throne of a great lotus palace, surrounded by corresponding bodhisattvas great beings, and whose diadem is adorned with all jewels, as in the case of a mighty wheel-turning sovereign king, with a consecration by the hands from the mouths of their whole bodies.

children.text: sa ca bodhisattvaste ca bodhisattvāḥ pāṇyabhiṣekādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā ityucyante
children.translated_text: And that bodhisattva and those bodhisattvas are said to be empowered by the empowerment of hand-consecration.

children.text: etanmahāmate bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām adhiṣṭhānadvayam yenādhiṣṭhānadvayenādhiṣṭhitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvabuddhamukhānyavalokayanti
children.translated_text: This, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the twofold empowerment of bodhisattvas great beings; empowered by this twofold empowerment, bodhisattvas great beings behold the faces of all Buddhas.
Apart from it, tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened ones are not to be beheld.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate yatkiṃcid bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratibhāti samādhyṛddhideśanākāreṇa tat sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānadvayādhiṣṭhitānām
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, whatever appears to bodhisattvas great beings in the form of samādhi, supernormal power, and teaching, all that belongs to those empowered by the twofold empowerment of all Buddhas.

children.text: yadi punarmahāmate bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām adhiṣṭhānamantareṇa pratibhānaṃ pratibhāyāt bālapṛthagjanānāmapi mahāmate pratibhānaṃ pratibhāyāt
children.translated_text: But if, <s>Mahāmate</s>, eloquence were to appear to bodhisattvas great beings apart from empowerment, eloquence would appear even to foolish ordinary people, <s>Mahāmate</s>.
Why is that? Namely, because they are not empowered by empowerment.

children.text: tṛṇagulmavṛkṣaparvatā api mahāmate vividhāni ca vādyabhāṇḍāni nagarabhavanagṛhavimānāsanasthānāni tathāgatapraveśādhiṣṭhānena pravādyante
children.translated_text: Even grasses, shrubs, trees, and mountains, <s>Mahāmate</s>, and various musical instruments, and the places of cities, buildings, houses, palaces, and seats are made to resound by the empowerment of the tathāgatas' entrance.

children.text: kiṃ punarmahāmate sacetanā mūkāndhabadhirā api mahāmate svadoṣebhyo vimucyante
children.translated_text: How much more, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are sentient beings, even the mute, blind, and deaf, <s>Mahāmate</s>, freed from their own faults?
Such, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the great excellence of the qualities of tathāgata-empowerment.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmatirāha kiṃ punarbhagavaṃstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ samādhisamāpattyavasthānakāle viśeṣabhūmau ca abhiṣekādhiṣṭhānaṃ prakurvanti bhagavānāha mārakarmakleśaviyuktārthaṃ śrāvakadhyānabhūmyaprapatanatayā ca tathāgatabhūmipratyātmādhigamanatayā ca prāptadharmādhigamavivṛddhaye ca
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s> said, "Why, Blessed One, do the tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened ones bestow the empowerment of consecration on bodhisattvas great beings at the time when they abide in the attainment of samādhi and on the special stage?" The Blessed One said, "For the sake of being separated from the works of Māra and the afflictions, and so that they may not fall into the meditative stages of the śrāvakas, and so that they may realize for themselves the stage of the tathāgatas, and for the increase of the realization of the dharmas they have obtained."

children.text: etena mahāmate kāraṇena tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām adhiṣṭhānairadhitiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: For this reason, <s>Mahāmate</s>, the tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened ones empower bodhisattvas great beings with empowerments.

children.text: anadhiṣṭhitāśca mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kutīrthyaśrāvakamārāśayapatitā nānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyeran
children.translated_text: And if they were not empowered, <s>Mahāmate</s>, bodhisattvas great beings, fallen into the dispositions of false teachers, śrāvakas, and Māras, would not awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: atastena kāraṇena bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anugṛhyante ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for that reason, bodhisattvas great beings are supported by the tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly awakened ones.
On this point it is said:
The empowerment of the lords among men is purified by vows;
consecration, samādhi, and the rest extend indeed from the first to the tenth stage.

children.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvaḥ punar api bhagavantam etadavocat pratītyasamutpādaṃ punarbhagavatā deśayatā kāraṇavyapadeśa eva kṛto na svanayaprakṛtyavasthānakathā
children.translated_text: Then the bodhisattva <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: "When the Blessed One taught dependent origination, he made only a designation of cause, not an account of the abiding in the own-principle and nature of things.

children.text: tīrthakarā api bhagavan kāraṇata utpattiṃ varṇayanti yaduta pradhāneśvarapuruṣakālāṇupratyayebhyo bhāvānām utpattayaḥ
children.translated_text: For the makers of non-Buddhist doctrines too, Blessed One, describe arising from a cause, namely the arising of entities from conditions such as primal matter, Īśvara, puruṣa, time, and atoms.

children.text: kiṃ tu bhagavatā pratyayaparyāyāntareṇotpattir varṇyate bhāvānām
children.translated_text: But the Blessed One describes the arising of entities by another series of conditions,
and there is no further distinction in doctrine.

children.text: sadasato hi bhagavaṃstīrthakarā apyutpattiṃ varṇayanti bhūtvā ca vināśaṃ pratyayairbhāvānām
children.translated_text: For the non-Buddhist teachers too, Blessed One, describe the arising of entities, whether existent or nonexistent, and, once they have come into being, their destruction through conditions.

children.text: yadapyuktaṃ bhagavatā avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvajjarāmaraṇamiti ahetuvādavyapadeśa eṣa bhagavatānuvarṇitaḥ na sa hetuvādaḥ
children.translated_text: And when the Blessed One has said, 'With ignorance as condition there are formations,' and so on up to old age and death, this is described by the Blessed One as a designation of the doctrine of non-causality, not as a doctrine of causality.

children.text: yugapadvyavasthitānāṃ bhagavann etadbhavati asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīti na kramavṛttyapekṣāvasthitānām
children.translated_text: This statement, Blessed One, 'when this exists, that comes to be,' applies to things established simultaneously, not to things established in dependence on sequential occurrence.

children.text: kiṃ tu tīrthakaravyapadeśa eva bhagavan viśiṣyate na tvadīyam
children.translated_text: Rather, Blessed One, the designation of the non-Buddhist teachers is superior, not yours."

children.text: tatkasya hetoḥ tīrthakarāṇāṃ hi bhagavan kāraṇam apratītyasamutpannaṃ kāryam abhinirvartayati
children.translated_text: For what reason? For the doctrine-makers, Blessed One, make an effect arise from a cause that has not arisen dependently.

children.text: tava tu bhagavan kāraṇamapi kāryāpekṣaṃ kāryamapi kāraṇāpekṣam
children.translated_text: But for you, Blessed One, the cause also depends on the effect, and the effect also depends on the cause.
Thus there is a confusion of causes and conditions, and in this way a mutual infinite regress follows.

children.text: ahetutvaṃ ca bhagavan lokasya asmin satīdaṃ bruvataḥ
children.translated_text: And, Blessed One, non-causality follows for the world from one who says, 'when this exists, this comes to be.'

children.text: bhagavānāha na mahāmate mamāhetukakāraṇavādo hetupratyayasaṃkaraśca prasajyate asmin satīdaṃ bruvataḥ grāhyagrāhakābhāvāt svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhāt
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: No, <s>Mahāmate</s>, for me a doctrine of causeless causation and a confusion of causes and conditions do not follow from saying, 'when this exists, this comes to be,' because of the absence of grasped and grasper and because of awakening to what is seen as only one's own mind.

children.text: ye tu mahāmate grāhyagrāhakābhiniviṣṭāḥ svacittadṛśyamātraṃ nāvabudhyante bāhyasvaviṣayabhāvābhāvatvena teṣāṃ mahāmate eṣa doṣaḥ prasajyate na tu mama pratītyakāraṇavyapadeśaṃ kurvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But those, <s>Mahāmate</s>, who are attached to grasped and grasper and do not understand what is seen as only one's own mind, in terms of the existence or nonexistence of external objects belonging to themselves, for them, <s>Mahāmate</s>, this fault follows; but not for me, who makes a designation of dependent causation.

children.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmatirāha nanu bhagavan abhilāpasadbhāvātsanti sarvabhāvāḥ
children.translated_text: Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said: Surely, Blessed One, because verbal expression exists, all entities exist.

children.text: yadi punarbhagavan bhāvā na syuḥ abhilāpo na pravartate
children.translated_text: For if, Blessed One, entities did not exist, verbal expression would not occur.
And it does occur.
Therefore, Blessed One, because verbal expression exists, all entities exist.
The Blessed One said: Even of nonexistent entities, <s>Mahāmate</s>, verbal expression is made.
That is, verbal expression is seen in the world for such things as a hare's horn, a tortoise's hair, and the son of a barren woman.

children.text: te ca mahāmate na bhāvā nābhāvāḥ abhilapyante ca
children.translated_text: And these, <s>Mahāmate</s>, are neither entities nor nonentities, yet they are verbally expressed.

children.text: tadyadavocastvaṃ mahāmate abhilāpasadbhāvātsanti sarvabhāvā iti sa hi vādaḥ prahīṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Mahāmate</s>, when you said, 'because verbal expression exists, all entities exist,' that doctrine is abandoned.
And, <s>Mahāmate</s>, verbal expression is not established in all Buddha-fields.
Verbal expression, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is something made.
